XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yn y fersiwn ddwyieithog, mae’r golofn chwith yn cynnwys yr iaith a lefarwyd yn y cyfarfod. Mae’r golofn dde yn cynnwys cyfieithiad o’r areithiau hynny.

Mae [R] yn dynodi bod yr Aelod wedi datgan buddiant wrth gyflwyno’r busnes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
In the bilingual version, the left-hand column includes the language used during the meeting. The right-hand column includes a translation of those speeches.

[R] indicates that the Member has declared an interest when tabling the business.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cyfarfu'r Senedd yn y Siambr a thrwy gynhadledd fideo am 13:30 gyda'r Llywydd (Huw Irranca-Davies) yn y Gadair.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Senedd met in the Chamber and by video-conference at 13:30 with the Llywydd (Huw Irranca-Davies) in the Chair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prynhawn da, bawb. Gadewch i ni ddechrau. Rydyn ni'n dechrau gyda chwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog. Cwestiwn 1, Andrew R.T. Davies.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Good afternoon, all. Let's make a start. We will begin with questions to the First Minister. The first question this afternoon is from Andrew R.T. Davies.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Y Ganolfan Ragoriaeth Fyd-Eang ar gyfer Rheilffyrdd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Global Centre of Rail Excellence

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi diweddariad ar safbwynt Llywodraeth Cymru ar y Ganolfan Ragoriaeth Fyd-eang ar gyfer Rheilffyrdd? OQ64526
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. Will the First Minister provide an update on the Welsh Government's position on the Global Centre of Rail Excellence? OQ64526

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The question does indeed come at an opportune time. A review has been commissioned, looking at how to deliver the best outcome at the Nant Helen site. We are keen now to develop a clear direction of travel with GCRE Ltd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r cwestiwn yn wir yn dod ar adeg briodol. Mae adolygiad wedi cael ei gomisiynu, sy'n edrych ar sut i gyflawni'r canlyniad gorau ar safle Nant Helen. Rydym ni'n awyddus bellach i ddatblygu cyfeiriad teithio eglur gyda GCRE Ltd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that update, First Minister. The Economy, Trade and Rural Affairs Committee in the last session visited the site and looked into the proposals that were presented to us. When this concept was first thought through, there was the potential for 1,000 jobs coming to the site, and the Government of the day was told that there was huge demand for this testing facility. Regrettably, to date, not £1 of private money has gone into it. It is a huge site. I saw a media report saying it's the size of Gibraltar. There's a lot of remediation work to go into it. The one thing we were told as a committee was that the incoming Government, whoever that Government would be, needed to make a quick decision about future investment. The site has burned through £70 million of public money to date. When will you be in the position to formulate what the Government is going to do, bearing in mind £70 million of public money has already gone in and £350 to £400 million is required to build this Global Centre of Rail Excellence?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch am y diweddariad yna, Brif Weinidog. Ymwelodd Pwyllgor yr Economi, Masnach a Materion Gwledig yn y sesiwn ddiwethaf â'r safle gan ymchwilio i'r cynigion a gyflwynwyd i ni. Pan feddyliwyd am y cysyniad hwn yn gyntaf, roedd potensial i 1,000 o swyddi ddod i'r safle, a dywedwyd wrth y Llywodraeth ar y pryd bod galw mawr am y cyfleuster profi hwn. Yn anffodus, hyd yma, nid oes £1 o arian preifat wedi cael ei chyfrannu ato. Mae'n safle enfawr. Gwelais adroddiad yn y cyfryngau yn dweud ei fod yr un maint â Gibraltar. Mae llawer o waith adfer i'w wneud arno. Yr un peth a ddywedwyd wrthym ni fel pwyllgor oedd bod angen i'r Llywodraeth newydd, pwy bynnag fyddai'r Llywodraeth honno, wneud penderfyniad cyflym am fuddsoddiad yn y dyfodol. Mae'r safle wedi gwario £70 miliwn o arian cyhoeddus hyd yma. Pryd fyddwch chi yn y sefyllfa i lunio'r hyn y mae'r Llywodraeth yn mynd i'w wneud, gan gofio bod £70 miliwn o arian cyhoeddus eisoes wedi cael ei gyfrannu a bod angen £350 i £400 miliwn i adeiladu'r Ganolfan Ragoriaeth Fyd-Eang ar gyfer Rheilffyrdd hon?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llywydd, the Member makes very important points. Significant amounts of public funding have gone into the site already. I'm not going to criticise the concept that came from the current leader of the Labour Party, but we have to understand what has happened as those tens of millions of pounds have been spent on the site, and what maybe hasn't happened to enable us to be at a place where there is private funding willing and able and keen to come in. As I say, my Minister has commissioned that work now because I agree that we need to come to a decision soon in order to make the most of the opportunities for what is still a very important site.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Lywydd, mae'r Aelod yn gwneud pwyntiau pwysig iawn. Mae symiau sylweddol o arian cyhoeddus wedi cael eu cyfrannu at y safle eisoes. Nid wyf i'n mynd i feirniadu'r cysyniad a ddaeth gan arweinydd presennol y Blaid Lafur, ond mae'n rhaid i ni ddeall yr hyn sydd wedi digwydd gan fod y degau o filiynau o bunnoedd hynny wedi cael eu gwario ar y safle, a'r hyn efallai nad yw wedi digwydd i ganiatáu i ni fod mewn sefyllfa lle mae cyllid preifat yn barod ac yn gallu ac yn awyddus i ddod i mewn. Fel y dywedais i, mae fy Ngweinidog wedi comisiynu'r gwaith hwnnw bellach gan fy mod i'n cytuno bod angen i ni wneud penderfyniad yn fuan er mwyn manteisio i'r eithaf ar y cyfleoedd ar gyfer safle sy'n dal i fod yn un pwysig iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, it's good to hear that you are commissioning a review, but this Chamber would like to understand that the confidence of your Government in this site must rest on a credible commercial case, which the public actually needs to understand. The additional proposed data centre and energy park may promise local jobs, but these benefits cannot justify an indefinite dependence on taxpayer-funded grants. After more than four months in office, your Government should be able to demonstrate how and when the development will attract private capital and generate a sufficient income to support itself. How will you make any further development conditional on a financially self-supporting business plan that delivers measurable local benefits without further taxpayer-funded grants to GCRE or participating companies? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, mae'n dda clywed eich bod chi'n comisiynu adolygiad, ond hoffai'r Siambr hon ddeall bod yn rhaid i hyder eich Llywodraeth yn y safle hwn fod yn seiliedig ar ddadl fasnachol gredadwy, y mae angen i'r cyhoedd ei deall mewn gwirionedd. Efallai fod y ganolfan ddata a'r parc ynni arfaethedig ychwanegol yn addo swyddi lleol, ond ni all y manteision hyn gyfiawnhau dibyniaeth benagored ar grantiau wedi'u hariannu gan y trethdalwr. Ar ôl mwy na phedwar mis mewn grym, dylai eich Llywodraeth allu dangos sut a phryd y bydd y datblygiad yn denu cyfalaf preifat ac yn cynhyrchu incwm digonol i gynnal ei hun. Sut fyddwch chi'n gwneud unrhyw ddatblygiad pellach yn amodol ar gynllun busnes sy'n ariannol hunangynhaliol ac yn sicrhau manteision lleol mesuradwy heb grantiau pellach wedi'u hariannu gan y trethdalwr i GCRE neu gwmnïau sy'n cymryd rhan? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Again, perfectly appropriate questions to ask. It is not just about making it a credible commercial proposition, it's making sure that the public money that has gone into it has been put to good use, and, as we consider the future, that we look at that balance of where Government works potentially with the private sector on what could be a whole host of different propositions. As I say, the fact that we understand the need to move quickly on this is why that review has been commissioned. Whatever the project, you cannot continue to move forward in an aimless way. This started from a point where there was a real belief in a particular project. Time has moved on. We need to make sure that, in 2026, we understand what the best project is now for that site.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Eto, cwestiynau cwbl briodol i'w gofyn. Nid yw'n fater o'i wneud yn gynnig masnachol credadwy yn unig, mae'n fater o wneud yn siŵr bod yr arian cyhoeddus sydd cael ei gyfrannu ato wedi cael ei ddefnyddio'n dda, ac, wrth i ni ystyried y dyfodol, ein bod ni'n edrych ar y cydbwysedd hwnnw o ble mae'r Llywodraeth yn gweithio o bosibl  gyda'r sector preifat ar yr hyn a allai fod yn llu o wahanol gynigion. Fel y dywedais i, y ffaith ein bod ni'n deall yr angen i symud yn gyflym ar hyn yw pam mae'r adolygiad hwnnw wedi cael ei gomisiynu. Beth bynnag yw'r prosiect, allwch chi ddim parhau i symud ymlaen mewn ffordd ddi-nod. Dechreuodd hyn o bwynt lle'r oedd ffydd gwirioneddol mewn prosiect penodol. Mae amser wedi symud ymlaen. Mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr, yn 2026, ein bod ni'n deall beth yw'r prosiect gorau rŵan ar gyfer y safle hwnnw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Global Centre of Rail Excellence is seen as a promising development for many across my constituency, showing the potential of green travel, a path towards net zero, and supporting the development of stronger, greener and more affordable transport systems right across the world. What other opportunities are there alongside this project that will help people in my constituency? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Ganolfan Ragoriaeth Fyd-Eang ar gyfer Rheilffyrdd yn cael ei hystyried yn ddatblygiad addawol i lawer ar draws fy etholaeth, gan ddangos potensial teithio gwyrdd, llwybr tuag at sero net, a chefnogi datblygiad systemau trafnidiaeth cryfach, gwyrddach a mwy fforddiadwy ledled y byd i gyd. Pa gyfleoedd eraill sy'n bodoli ochr yn ochr â'r prosiect hwn a fydd yn helpu pobl yn fy etholaeth? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Member again points to that original concept around rail. A lot has happened in rail since those times, not least the changes in direction around HS2 and so on. We need to understand where we are now, rather than where we were. We need to understand the significance of decisions that have been made to date. The Member will want to ensure that what we achieve there is something that is of value to the locality, to the constituency that she and others represent, and to the Welsh economy. And those are the principles that will be guiding my Cabinet Minister for enterprise as he now works with the review and looks forward to seeing the results of that review pretty soon.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'r Aelod eto yn tynnu sylw at y cysyniad gwreiddiol hwnnw yn ymwneud â rheilffyrdd. Mae llawer wedi digwydd ym maes rheilffyrdd ers y cyfnod hwnnw, ac yn enwedig y newidiadau mewn cyfeiriad o amgylch HS2 ac yn y blaen. Mae angen i ni ddeall ein sefyllfa rŵan, yn hytrach na ble roeddem ni. Mae angen i ni ddeall arwyddocâd penderfyniadau sydd wedi cael eu gwneud hyd yma. Bydd yr Aelod eisiau sicrhau bod yr hyn yr ydym ni'n ei gyflawni yno yn rhywbeth sydd o werth i'r ardal, i'r etholaeth y mae hi ac eraill yn ei chynrychioli, ac i economi Cymru. A dyna'r egwyddorion a fydd yn arwain fy Ngweinidog Cabinet dros fenter wrth iddo weithio bellach gyda'r adolygiad ac edrych ymlaen at weld canlyniadau'r adolygiad hwnnw yn fuan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Fe ges i hefyd gyfle yn gynharach eleni i ymweld â'r safle yma a gweld y potensial arbennig sydd yno nid yn unig fel canolfan arloesi rheilffyrdd, ond hefyd fel lle ble y gellir cael pethau fel canolfannau data, a fydd yn helpu i ddatgloi y prosiect ehangach.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I also had an opportunity earlier this year to visit this site and to see the great potential that exists there not only for a centre of innovation in rail, but also as a place where you could have things such as data centres, which will help to unlock the broader project.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Welsh Labour invested £2 billion in the Heads of the Valleys road precisely for a reason like this, to connect communities, including along the M4 corridor but also in the old Valleys communities, with projects like this. If we are serious about bringing well-paid jobs and re-industrialising the former coalfields, this is exactly the kind of investment that Wales should secure, recognising that this will take public money as well as private money. So, I've heard a bit of equivocation from you today, which will raise concerns for people wanting to see a rail solution brought forward. We want to see more trains brought forward into Wales, and this would help unlock that. Can you give a reason why your Government would not support the GCRE project specifically? And if you can't give a reason, will you perhaps today commit to supporting it? Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe wnaeth Llafur Cymru fuddsoddi £2 biliwn yn ffordd Blaenau'r Cymoedd yn union am reswm fel hwn, i gysylltu cymunedau, gan gynnwys ar hyd coridor yr M4 ond hefyd yn hen gymunedau'r Cymoedd, gyda phrosiectau fel hyn. Os ydym ni o ddifrif am ddod â swyddi â chyflogau da ac ail-ddiwydiannu'r hen feysydd glo, dyma'r union fath o fuddsoddiad y dylai Cymru ei sicrhau, gan gydnabod y bydd hyn angen arian cyhoeddus yn ogystal ag arian preifat. Felly, rwyf i wedi clywed dipyn o amwysedd gennych chi heddiw, a fydd yn codi pryderon i bobl sydd eisiau gweld ateb rheilffyrdd yn cael ei gyflwyno. Rydym ni eisiau gweld mwy o drenau yn cael eu cyflwyno yng Nghymru, a byddai hyn yn helpu i ddatgloi hynny. A allwch chi roi rheswm pam na fyddai eich Llywodraeth yn cefnogi'r prosiect GCRE yn benodol? Ac os na allwch chi roi rheswm, a wnewch chi efallai ymrwymo heddiw i'w gefnogi? Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n meddwl fy mod i wedi bod mor agored ag y gallaf ynglŷn â'r dewis rydyn ni'n gorfod ei wneud fel Llywodraeth rŵan. A'r dewis hwnnw ydy asesu beth ydy'r defnydd gorau ar gyfer, ie, arian cyhoeddus, ond hefyd y modd gorau o ddenu arian preifat i mewn. A'r broblem efo'r cynllun rheilffordd, fel ag y mae o, ydy ei fod o wedi methu—wedi methu—â denu arian preifat i mewn. Dyna pam yr ydym ni yn y sefyllfa yr ydym ni ynddi heddiw. Mae'r Aelod yn iawn, Lywydd, i ddweud mai beth sydd angen ydy ystyried potensial y safle. Gallaf i ddwyn cymhariaeth efo safle Alwminiwm Môn yn fy etholaeth i. Pan ddaeth y gwaith hwnnw i ben, beth oedd gennym ni oedd safle. A beth sydd angen ei wneud mewn sefyllfa fel yna ydy meddwl 'Ocê, beth ydy'r defnydd gorau ar gyfer y safle hwnnw?', a pheidio bod yn rhy briod i un elfen bosib. Ac ydy, wrth gwrs bod yr opsiwn rheilffyrdd yn dal ar y bwrdd. Beth rydyn ni'n mynd i wneud ydy edrych ar y sefyllfa lle rydym ni rŵan a gwneud y penderfyniadau gorau ar gyfer pobl yr ardal yna a dyfodol economi Cymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I think that I've been as open as I can be about the choice that we have to make as a Government now. And that choice is to assess what the best use is for, yes, public money but also the best way of attracting private investment in. And the problem with the railway plan as it is is that it has failed. It has failed to attract private investment and that's why we're in the situation that we're in today. The Member is correct, Llywydd, to say that what is needed is to consider the potential of the site. I could compare this with the Anglesey Aluminium site. When the work there came to an end, what we had there was a site. And what needs to be done in that kind of situation is to think, 'Right, what's the best use for this site?', and not being too tied to one possible element. And, of course, the railway option is still on the table, but what we are going to do is to look at where we are now and to make the best decisions for the people of that area and the future of Wales's economy.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Blaenoriaethau Gofal Iechyd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Healthcare Priorities

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Beth yw blaenoriaethau gofal iechyd Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer Ceredigion Penfro ar gyfer y deuddeg mis nesaf? OQ64479
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What are the Welsh Government's healthcare priorities for Ceredigion Penfro for the next twelve months? OQ64479

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Improving health outcomes, ensuring timely access to care, supporting sustainable NHS services for communities across Ceredigion Penfro are clearly major priorities for this new Government. As part of our vision to strengthen healthcare in rural and coastal areas in particular, we will engage closely with the local health board and partners to ensure high-quality, patient-centred services that genuinely do meet the needs of local people. We want to make sure they're delivered now and into the future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae gwella canlyniadau iechyd, sicrhau mynediad prydlon at ofal, cefnogi gwasanaethau GIG cynaliadwy ar gyfer cymunedau ledled Ceredigion Penfro yn amlwg yn brif flaenoriaethau i'r Llywodraeth newydd hon. Yn rhan o'n gweledigaeth i gryfhau gofal iechyd mewn ardaloedd gwledig ac arfordirol yn arbennig, byddwn yn ymgysylltu'n agos â'r bwrdd iechyd lleol a phartneriaid i sicrhau gwasanaethau o ansawdd uchel, sy'n canolbwyntio ar y claf sydd wir yn diwallu anghenion pobl leol. Rydym ni eisiau gwneud yn siŵr eu bod nhw'n cael eu darparu nawr ac yn y dyfodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, I believe that the Welsh Government's healthcare priorities for Ceredigion Penfro must be to protect essential health services at its hospitals so that patients do not have to travel further afield for treatment. Now, over the years, my constituents have seen health services centralised and moved further away by the local health board, despite clear public opposition to these changes. And there has been little, if any, intervention or challenge from a Welsh Government over the last 27 years. Now, following the change of Government in May, there was a sense of hope for my constituents that their views would be heard and the health board stopped, and, so far, that has not been the case. So, First Minister, what threshold must be crossed before the Welsh Government is prepared to intervene and prevent Hywel Dda University Health Board from further downgrading services in west Wales? And what message do you have for the people of Ceredigion Penfro who voted for a Government they believed would stand up for local communities and ensure that no further services are removed from their hospitals?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, rwy'n credu ei bod yn rheidrwydd mai blaenoriaethau gofal iechyd Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer Ceredigion Penfro yw diogelu gwasanaethau iechyd hanfodol yn ei ysbytai fel nad oes yn rhaid i gleifion deithio ymhellach i ffwrdd i gael triniaeth. Nawr, dros y blynyddoedd, mae fy etholwyr wedi gweld gwasanaethau iechyd yn cael eu canoli a'u symud ymhellach i ffwrdd gan y bwrdd iechyd lleol, er gwaethaf gwrthwynebiad amlwg y cyhoedd i'r newidiadau hyn. A phrin, os o gwbl, fu'r ymyrraeth neu her gan Lywodraeth Cymru dros y 27 mlynedd diwethaf. Nawr, yn dilyn y newid Llywodraeth ym mis Mai, roedd ymdeimlad o obaith i'm hetholwyr y byddai eu safbwyntiau yn cael eu clywed a'r bwrdd iechyd yn cael ei atal, a hyd yn hyn, nid yw hynny wedi digwydd. Felly, Brif Weinidog, pa drothwy y mae'n rhaid ei groesi cyn bod Llywodraeth Cymru yn barod i ymyrryd ac atal Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Hywel Dda rhag israddio gwasanaethau yng ngorllewin Cymru ymhellach? A pha neges sydd gennych chi i bobl Ceredigion Penfro a bleidleisiodd dros Lywodraeth yr oedden nhw'n credu fyddai'n sefyll yn gadarn dros gymunedau lleol ac yn sicrhau nad oes unrhyw wasanaethau pellach yn cael eu cymryd o'u hysbytai?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Llywydd, the Member is absolutely right that we want to protect essential services, and most of us at one time or another have been involved in various campaigns around particular services in different places. I think the principles that we need to bear in mind always are that we provide timely services in the appropriate location. There will be different stories in different parts of Wales, but those are the principles that tie us together.

Decisions on clinical services are taken by the health boards themselves. I know that the health board in this particular instance has looked at eight out of nine of the services that it provides and consulted on them, and put in place changes that it believes would provide better services to be delivered over the best part of a decade. These aren't overnight changes. And it's important to remember that these are changes that can take time. But my appeal always is for health boards, when they make those changes, when they consult, and afterwards, to ensure that people feel that they are engaged properly on those decisions. But there will be, clearly, different applications of different services in different parts of Wales. It's about getting that balance of appropriate services that will always put the patient first.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Lywydd, mae'r Aelod yn gwbl gywir ein bod ni eisiau diogelu gwasanaethau hanfodol, ac mae'r rhan fwyaf ohonom ni ar un adeg neu'r llall wedi bod yn rhan o wahanol ymgyrchoedd yn ymwneud â gwasanaethau penodol mewn gwahanol leoedd. Rwy'n credu mai'r egwyddorion y mae angen i ni eu cadw mewn cof bob amser yw ein bod ni'n darparu gwasanaethau prydlon yn y lleoliad priodol. Bydd gwahanol straeon mewn gwahanol rannau o Gymru, ond dyna'r egwyddorion sy'n ein clymu at ein gilydd.

Mae penderfyniadau am wasanaethau clinigol yn cael eu gwneud gan y byrddau iechyd eu hunain. Rwy'n gwybod bod y bwrdd iechyd yn yr achos penodol hwn wedi edrych ar wyth o naw o'r gwasanaethau y mae'n eu darparu ac wedi ymgynghori arnyn nhw, ac wedi rhoi newidiadau ar waith y mae'n credu fyddai'n darparu gwasanaethau gwell i'w darparu dros y rhan helaeth o ddegawd. Nid newidiadau dros nos yw'r rhain. Ac mae'n bwysig cofio bod y rhain yn newidiadau a all gymryd amser. Ond fy apêl i bob amser yw i fyrddau iechyd, pan fyddan nhw'n gwneud y newidiadau hynny, pan fyddan nhw'n ymgynghori, ac wedi hynny, sicrhau bod pobl yn teimlo eu bod yn cael eu cynnwys yn briodol yn y penderfyniadau hynny. Ond, yn amlwg, bydd gwahanol ddefnyddiau o wahanol wasanaethau mewn gwahanol rannau o Gymru. Mae'n fater o gael y cydbwysedd hwnnw o wasanaethau priodol a fydd bob amser yn rhoi'r claf yn gyntaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you to Paul Davies for the question. First Minister, 35 per cent of Ceredigion households and 23 per cent in Pembrokeshire rely on oil heating, among the highest rates in Wales. Public Health Wales warns that cold homes increase cardiovascular and respiratory risks, particular for older and vulnerable people. As your Government moves towards net zero, how will you ensure that rural households are not forced to ration heating because of the cost of that transition, and will you guarantee that keeping people warm and healthy comes before hitting arbitrary deadlines? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i Paul Davies am y cwestiwn. Brif Weinidog, mae 35 y cant o aelwydydd Ceredigion a 23 y cant yn sir Benfro yn dibynnu ar wresogi olew, ymhlith y cyfraddau uchaf yng Nghymru. Mae Iechyd Cyhoeddus Cymru yn rhybuddio bod cartrefi oer yn cynyddu peryglon cardiofasgwlaidd ac anadlol, yn enwedig i bobl hŷn ac agored i niwed. Wrth i'ch Llywodraeth symud tuag at sero net, sut wnewch chi sicrhau nad yw aelwydydd gwledig yn cael eu gorfodi i gyfyngu gwres oherwydd cost y newid hwnnw, ac a wnewch chi sicrhau bod cadw pobl yn gynnes ac yn iach yn cael blaenoriaeth dros fodloni terfynau amser mympwyol? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I will accept that there is a healthcare link there, Llywydd, and I'm being very, very generous. We know that a healthy home, a healthy environment, is important for people's health, so the Member is absolutely right in that respect.

On oil heating in particular, of course, these are measures that are reserved. We have consistently appealed to the UK Government to make the right decisions when it comes to the options that it has at its disposal, but that we haven't as a Welsh Government, to relieve the pressure on households in rural Wales in particular that are particularly dependent on off-grid oil. It is a principle that ties this Government together, that we think cross-departmentally, and the Member is right: we need to think housing, we need to think energy, we need to think health when it comes to the well-being of the people that we represent.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe wnaf i dderbyn bod cysylltiad gofal iechyd yn y fan yna, Lywydd, ac rwy'n bod yn hael iawn, iawn. Rydym ni'n gwybod bod cartref iach, amgylchedd iach, yn bwysig i iechyd pobl, felly mae'r Aelod yn llygad ei le yn hynny o beth.

Ar wresogi olew yn benodol, wrth gwrs, mae'r rhain yn fesurau sydd wedi'u cadw yn ôl. Rydym ni wedi apelio'n gyson ar Lywodraeth y DU i wneud y penderfyniadau cywir o ran yr opsiynau sydd ar gael iddi, ond nad ydyn nhw ar gael i ni fel Llywodraeth Cymru, i leddfu'r pwysau ar aelwydydd yng nghefn gwlad Cymru yn enwedig sy'n arbennig o ddibynnol ar olew oddi ar y grid. Mae'n egwyddor sy'n glynu'r Llywodraeth hon at ei gilydd, ein bod ni'n meddwl yn drawsadrannol, ac mae'r Aelod yn iawn: mae angen i ni feddwl am dai, mae angen i ni feddwl am ynni, mae angen i ni feddwl iechyd o ran llesiant y bobl yr ydym ni'n eu cynrychioli.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, I'd like to agree that protecting services at Bronglais and Withybush hospitals remains vital for communities across Ceredigion Penfro. However, in rural areas, we also need innovative ways of bringing healthcare closer to people's homes. Integrated care centres in Cardigan and Aberaeron show what can be achieved when we bring services together, and, again, bring them closer to people, taking the pressure off hospitals. Having recently visited GP services in Fishguard, I know that there is strong local support for a similar approach there. Indeed, my colleague Elin Jones has previously worked with local councillors to make the case for an integrated care centre for Fishguard. So, will the Welsh Government commit to working with Hywel Dda University Health Board and local communities to explore how towns such as Fishguard could benefit from integrated care facilities, ensuring rural communities are not left behind as healthcare services evolve?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, hoffwn gytuno bod diogelu gwasanaethau yn ysbytai Bronglais a Llwynhelyg yn parhau i fod yn hanfodol i gymunedau ledled Ceredigion Penfro. Fodd bynnag, mewn ardaloedd gwledig, rydym ni angen ffyrdd arloesol o ddod â gofal iechyd yn agosach at gartrefi pobl. Mae canolfannau gofal integredig yn Aberteifi ac Aberaeron yn dangos yr hyn y gellir ei gyflawni pan fyddwn ni'n dod â gwasanaethau at ei gilydd, ac, eto, dod â nhw'n agosach at bobl, gan dynnu'r pwysau oddi ar ysbytai. Ar ôl ymweld â gwasanaethau meddygon teulu yn Abergwaun yn ddiweddar, gwn fod cefnogaeth leol gref i ddull tebyg yno. Yn wir, mae fy nghyd-Aelod Elin Jones wedi gweithio gyda chynghorwyr lleol yn flaenorol i wneud y ddadl dros ganolfan gofal integredig ar gyfer Abergwaun. Felly, a wnaiff Llywodraeth Cymru ymrwymo i weithio gyda Bwrdd Iechyd Prifysgol Hywel Dda a chymunedau lleol i archwilio sut allai trefi fel Abergwaun elwa o gyfleusterau gofal integredig, gan sicrhau nad yw cymunedau gwledig yn cael eu gadael ar ôl wrth i wasanaethau gofal iechyd esblygu?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Many of us represent rural areas here, and the health of somebody in a rural part of Wales is as important as somebody in an urban part of Wales. We need to make sure that we have equitable healthcare, but it does mean that a different approach is needed. I'm really interested in the work that is developing—already has begun—into creating a centre of excellence on the delivery of rural healthcare in Bronglais Hospital, which could benefit all parts of Wales, not just Ceredigion Penfro.

The programme for government commitment is clear. We want to ensure that integrated care is delivered closer to home, with prevention in particular at its core, to support earlier diagnosis, reduce admissions and delays in discharge. We have many ideas on how, in general, the delivery can be improved in rural areas, but health officials, I know, are engaging with the health board and Pembrokeshire County Council specifically on the development of that integrated centre in Fishguard.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae llawer ohonom ni'n cynrychioli ardaloedd gwledig yma, ac mae iechyd rhywun mewn rhan wledig o Gymru yr un mor bwysig â rhywun mewn rhan drefol o Gymru. Mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod gennym ni ofal iechyd teg, ond mae'n golygu bod angen gwahanol ddull. Mae gen i ddiddordeb mawr yn y gwaith sy'n datblygu—sydd eisoes wedi cychwyn—i greu canolfan ragoriaeth ar y ddarpariaeth o ofal iechyd gwledig yn Ysbyty Bronglais, a allai fod o fudd i bob rhan o Gymru, nid Ceredigion Penfro yn unig.

Mae ymrwymiad y rhaglen lywodraethu yn eglur. Rydym ni eisiau sicrhau bod gofal integredig yn cael ei ddarparu yn agosach at adref, ag atal yn arbennig yn ganolog iddo, i gefnogi diagnosis cynharach, i leihau derbyniadau ac oedi cyn rhyddhau. Mae gennym ni lawer o syniadau ar sut y gellir, yn gyffredinol, gwella'r ddarpariaeth mewn ardaloedd gwledig, ond mae swyddogion iechyd, rwy'n gwybod, yn ymgysylltu â'r bwrdd iechyd a Chyngor Sir Penfro yn benodol ar ddatblygiad y ganolfan integredig honno yn Abergwaun.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Arweinwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from the Party Leaders

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar arweinwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Prif Weinidog. Yn gyntaf, arweinydd Reform UK, Helen Jenner.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party leaders to question the First Minister. First, the leader of Reform UK, Helen Jenner.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. First Minister, you so often stand on your soapbox and arrogantly claim that you and your party are the ones fighting injustice and standing up for Wales. Yet, you and your party had the chance last week to tackle rape gangs and to stand up for Wales by backing our Reform motion to help bring closure for women and girls by uncovering the extent of rape gang activity in Wales. But, instead, you voted, shamefully, against it. How on earth can women and girls expect you to have their best interests and safety at heart?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Brif Weinidog, rydych chi'n sefyll mor aml ar eich bocs sebon ac yn honni'n fawreddog mai chi a'ch plaid yw'r rhai sy'n ymladd anghyfiawnder ac yn sefyll dros Gymru. Eto, cawsoch chi a'ch plaid gyfle yr wythnos diwethaf i fynd i'r afael â gangiau treisio ac i sefyll dros Gymru trwy gefnogi ein cynnig Reform i helpu i gloi pethau i fenywod a merched trwy ddatgelu graddfa gweithgarwch gangiau treisio yng Nghymru. Ond, yn hytrach, fe wnaethoch chi bleidleisio, yn gywilyddus, yn ei erbyn. Sut ar y ddaear all menywod a merched ddisgwyl i chi fod â'u buddiannau gorau yn flaenllaw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Let me take this opportunity to congratulate the new leader of Reform in Wales on her election to the role. She is certainly a bold politician. Anybody who says she came into politics because she was impressed by the principles of Nigel Farage certainly has to be seen as bold.

There is nothing that is more important to any of us, hopefully, than safeguarding people that we have a duty of care for. That is why my Government at this moment is working on strengthening safeguarding and how it protects vulnerable people, including women and girls, potentially trafficked people, in all parts of Wales. That is something my Government is actively getting on with.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gadewch i mi fanteisio ar y cyfle hwn i longyfarch arweinydd newydd Reform yng Nghymru ar ei hethol i'r swydd. Mae'n sicr yn wleidydd beiddgar. Yn sicr, mae'n rhaid ystyried bod unrhyw un sy'n dweud ei bod wedi dod i fyd gwleidyddiaeth oherwydd bod egwyddorion Nigel Farage wedi creu argraff arni yn feiddgar.

Nid oes unrhyw beth sy'n bwysicach i unrhyw un ohonom ni, gobeithio, na diogelu pobl y mae gennym ni ddyletswydd gofal amdanyn nhw. Dyna pam mae fy Llywodraeth ar hyn o bryd yn gweithio ar gryfhau mesurau diogelu a sut mae'n amddiffyn pobl agored i niwed, gan gynnwys menywod a merched, pobl a allai gael eu masnachu, ym mhob rhan o Gymru. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth y mae fy Llywodraeth yn bwrw ymlaen ag ef yn weithredol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: You had the opportunity for a Wales focus there. Ironically, normally, we like to stand out, don't we, from the rest of the United Kingdom, but, in this case, you are happy to be absorbed into the UK inquiry. First Minister, the evidence suggests that rape gang activity may have been covered up by authorities to avoid racial tensions, and if we don't get to the bottom of what is among the most sickening organised criminal activities of our time, we cannot expect to prevent the risk of many more crimes of this nature. Last year, the Welsh Government said there was no current widespread issue with grooming gangs in Wales, and one of your current Ministers was accused by a grooming gang victim of downplaying her experience. Let's just have a look at the last 11 weeks alone: we've had two men imprisoned in Cardiff, five people convicted in Rhyl, and eight men across south Wales charged as part of Operation Oak, all relating to grooming gang-type activity. First Minister, can you really look me in the eye and say that you didn't let down victims last week by voting against wanting a grooming gang investigation in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Roedd gennych chi gyfle i roi pwyslais ar Gymru yn y fan yna. Yn eironig, fel rheol, rydym ni'n hoffi sefyll allan, onid ydym ni, o weddill y Deyrnas Unedig, ond, yn yr achos hwn, rydych chi'n hapus i gael eich cynnwys yn ymchwiliad y DU. Brif Weinidog, mae'r dystiolaeth yn awgrymu y gallai gweithgarwch gangiau treisio fod wedi cael ei guddio gan awdurdodau i osgoi tensiynau hiliol, ac os na fyddwn ni'n darganfod gwraidd yr hyn sydd ymhlith gweithgareddau troseddol cyfundrefnol mwyaf ffiaidd ein hoes, allwn ni ddim disgwyl atal y perygl o lawer mwy o droseddau o'r natur hon. Y llynedd, dywedodd Llywodraeth Cymru nad oedd unrhyw broblem eang bresennol gyda gangiau meithrin perthynas amhriodol yng Nghymru, a chyhuddwyd un o'ch Gweinidogion presennol gan ddioddefwr gang meithrin perthynas amhriodol o fychanu ei phrofiad. Gadewch i ni edrych ar yr 11 wythnos ddiwethaf yn unig: mae dau ddyn wedi cael eu carcharu yng Nghaerdydd, pump o bobl wedi derbyn euogfarn yn y Rhyl, ac wyth o ddynion ar draws de Cymru yn cael eu cyhuddo yn rhan o Ymgyrch Oak, y cwbl yn gysylltiedig â gweithgarwch o fath gangiau meithrin perthynas amhriodol. Brif Weinidog, a allwch chi wir edrych i fy llygaid a dweud na wnaethoch chi siomi dioddefwyr yr wythnos diwethaf trwy bleidleisio yn erbyn bod eisiau ymchwiliad i gangiau meithrin perthyna amhriodol yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I can look you in the eye every single day of the week and tell you that we have a Government that isn't interested in scoring political points about what is a very, very sensitive issue, and is interested in getting on with finding solutions. Now, we said that we needed to understand the scale of the problem in Wales. Work was done to understand the scale of the problem in Wales, and it is apparent, obviously, that we have issues here that we need to get to grips with in order to safeguard people, which is why my Government is giving all support to the inquiry that is currently looking at the lessons that can be learnt. She may want to make this a constitutional issue; I make this about the safety of people in Wales, and that is the difference between her and me.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gallaf edrych i'ch llygaid bob un diwrnod o'r wythnos a dweud wrthych chi fod gennym ni Lywodraeth nad oes ganddi ddiddordeb mewn sgorio pwyntiau gwleidyddol am yr hyn sy'n fater sensitif iawn, iawn, ac sydd â diddordeb mewn bwrw ymlaen â dod o hyd i atebion. Rŵan, fe wnaethom ni ddweud bod angen i ni ddeall maint y broblem yng Nghymru. Gwnaed gwaith i ddeall maint y broblem yng Nghymru, a gellir gweld, yn amlwg, bod gennym ni broblemau yma y mae angen i ni fynd i'r afael â nhw er mwyn diogelu pobl, a dyna pam mae fy Llywodraeth yn rhoi pob cefnogaeth i'r ymchwiliad sy'n edrych ar hyn o bryd ar y gwersi y gellir eu dysgu. Efallai ei bod yn dymuno gwneud hwn yn fater cyfansoddiadol; rwy'n gwneud hwn yn fater o ddiogelwch pobl yng Nghymru, a dyna'r gwahaniaeth rhyngddi hi a minnau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, making sure victims' voices are heard—that is not political point scoring.

Speaking of uncovering the truth, First Minister, I've got a couple of quotes to read to you today:

'Reform would look at the nation of sanctuary and say Welsh people come first when prioritising council housing, and that is really, really important to me.'

Let me read you my second quote:

'Millions are being wasted on the tree-planting project, which is absolutely incredible, that we are sending money in Wales to Uganda.'

First Minister, these were things said by a Senedd Member that now sits on your benches. Do you agree with these comments, 'yes' or 'no'?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, gwneud yn siŵr bod lleisiau dioddefwyr yn cael eu clywed—nid sgorio pwyntiau gwleidyddol yw hynny.

Wrth sôn am ddatgelu'r gwir, Brif Weinidog, mae gen i gwpl o ddyfyniadau i'w darllen i chi heddiw:

'Byddai Reform yn edrych ar y genedl noddfa ac yn dweud bod pobl Cymru yn dod gyntaf wrth flaenoriaethu tai cyngor, ac mae hynny'n wirioneddol bwysig i mi.'

Gadewch i mi ddarllen fy ail ddyfyniad i chi:

'Mae miliynau yn cael eu gwastraffu ar y prosiect plannu coed, sy'n gwbl anhygoel, ein bod ni'n anfon arian yng Nghymru i Uganda.'

Brif Weinidog, pethau a ddywedwyd gan Aelod o'r Senedd sydd bellach yn eistedd ar eich meinciau chi yw'r rhain. A ydych chi'n cytuno â'r sylwadau hyn, 'ydw' neu 'nac ydw'?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: What I admire is that somebody would have the bravery to stand up to this Reform group in the Senedd and say, 'I now can see you for what you are.' That is precisely what Sarah Cooper-Lesadd did last week. I firmly believe that, in politics, it is up to all of us to show that we are able to change, that we are able to see the light, politically, if you like, and so many other people are doing the same. We have now a scandal-ridden Reform party that is collapsing in chaos around the new Reform leader in Wales. The Member said yesterday that she is all for unity and continuity, but her party is incapable of showing either. Perhaps she can tell us how much of the £72 million arising from the latest Reform scandal she hopes will come to Wales. Maybe she hopes it will be Barnettised.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yr hyn yr wyf i'n ei edmygu yw y byddai gan rywun y dewrder i sefyll i fyny i'r grŵp Reform hwn yn y Senedd a dweud, 'Rwyf i bellach yn gallu eich gweld chi am yr hyn yr ydych chi.' Dyna'n union wnaeth Sarah Cooper-Lesadd yr wythnos diwethaf. Rwy'n credu'n gryf, ym myd gwleidyddiaeth, ei bod hi'n gyfrifoldeb am bob un ohonom ni i ddangos ein bod ni'n gallu newid, ein bod ni'n gallu gweld y goleuni, yn wleidyddol, os mynnwch, ac mae cynifer o bobl eraill yn gwneud yr un fath. Mae gennym ni blaid Reform rŵan lle mae sgandal yn rhemp, sy'n chwalu mewn anhrefn o amgylch yr arweinydd Reform newydd yng Nghymru. Dywedodd yr Aelod ddoe ei bod hi o blaid undod a pharhad, ond nid yw ei phlaid yn gallu dangos y naill na'r llall. Efallai y gall ddweud wrthym ni faint o'r £72 miliwn sy'n deillio o'r sgandal Reform diweddaraf y mae hi'n gobeithio fydd yn dod i Gymru. Efallai ei bod hi'n gobeithio y bydd yn cael ei Farnetteiddio.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 'Yes' or 'no'? Okay. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 'Ydw' neu 'nac ydw'? Iawn. Diolch yn fawr.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, today we remember the deaths of hundreds of people in the Gresford mining disaster. It was a horrific disaster that devastated the community, and I'm sure you, First Minister, will also remember those who died. More than 260 bodies were recovered, but 253 remain entombed. Unfortunately, it wasn't just men that died; boys died in that disaster as well. It clearly was one of Wales's darkest days.

Research by Wrexham.com shows that, whilst the Plaid Government was questioning the need and rationale for an extra £100 million to be spent on additional learning needs, it was at the very same time asking councils how much more they'd be spending on additional learning needs this year. Now, the data was published just before the supplementary budget vote on your own website. And that figure, in total, for all councils and all schools in Wales was an extra £96.3 million—almost exactly the £100 million that Welsh Labour was saying was required to stabilise the system across Wales, and for which you received a major UK Labour Government windfall. Now, does this revelation, uncovered as I say by Wrexham.com, demonstrate that disadvantaged children risk coming second to this Plaid Cymru Government, behind free childcare for millionaires?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, heddiw rydym ni'n cofio marwolaethau cannoedd o bobl yn nhrychineb mwyngloddio Gresffordd. Roedd yn drychineb ofnadwy a ddiffeithiodd y gymuned, ac rwy'n siŵr y byddwch chi, Brif Weinidog, hefyd yn cofio'r rhai a fu farw. Cafodd mwy na 260 o gyrff eu hadfer, ond roedd 253 yn dal i fod wedi eu claddu. Yn anffodus, nid dynion yn unig a fu farw; bu farw bechgyn yn y drychineb honno hefyd. Roedd yn amlwg yn un o ddyddiau tywyllaf Cymru.

Mae gwaith ymchwil gan Wrexham.com yn dangos, er bod Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru yn cwestiynu'r angen a'r rhesymeg dros £100 miliwn ychwanegol i'w wario ar anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, roedd ar yr un pryd yn union yn gofyn i gynghorau faint yn fwy y bydden nhw'n ei wario ar anghenion dysgu ychwanegol eleni. Nawr, cyhoeddwyd y data ychydig cyn y bleidlais ar y gyllideb atodol ar eich gwefan eich hun. A £96.3 miliwn yn ychwanegol oedd y ffigur hwnnw, fel cyfanswm, ar gyfer pob cyngor a phob ysgol yng Nghymru—bron yn union y £100 miliwn yr oedd Llafur Cymru yn dweud yr oedd ei angen i sefydlogi'r system ledled Cymru, ac y cawsoch chi gyllid mawr ar ei gyfer gan Lywodraeth Lafur y DU. Nawr, a yw'r datguddiad hwn, a ddatgelwyd fel y dywedais gan Wrexham.com, yn dangos bod plant difreintiedig mewn perygl o ddod yn ail i'r Llywodraeth Plaid Cymru hon, y tu ôl i ofal plant am ddim i filiwnyddion?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Let me, firstly, associate myself very much with the comments as we remember the Gresford disaster, and we send our thoughts to the community, for whom the pain of that day is still felt in many ways. 

On additional learning needs, I remind the Labour leader that he was intending to spend £9 million, had they won the election. My party's manifesto made it a pledge to put ALN on a sustainable footing. We had a discussion, running up to the supplementary budget, where we were putting £100 million plus on the table, including £40 million for this year—for this year—which is what we gauged, working with officials and others, could actually be spent to take the pressure. That money is still on the table, and I appeal to the Member again: help us to get it out of the door to help those families and the schools and local authorities who need that money spent.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gadewch i mi, yn gyntaf, gysylltu fy hun yn llwyr â'r sylwadau wrth i ni gofio trychineb Gresffordd, ac rydym ni'n anfon ein cydymdeimlad i'r gymuned, y mae poen y diwrnod hwnnw yn dal i gael ei deimlo mewn llawer o ffyrdd.

Ar anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, rwy'n atgoffa arweinydd Llafur ei fod yn bwriadu gwario £9 miliwn, pe baen nhw wedi ennill yr etholiad. Gwnaeth maniffesto fy mhlaid i addewid i roi ADY ar sylfaen gynaliadwy. Cawsom drafodaeth, yn y cyfnod cyn y gyllideb atodol, lle'r oeddem yn rhoi £100 miliwn a mwy ar y bwrdd, gan gynnwys £40 miliwn ar gyfer eleni—ar gyfer eleni—sef yr hyn y gwnaethom ni ei ystyried, gan weithio gyda swyddogion ac eraill, y gellid ei wario mewn gwirionedd i leddfu'r pwysau. Mae'r arian hwnnw'n dal ar y bwrdd, ac rwy'n apelio i'r Aelod eto: helpwch ni i'w gael allan drwy'r drws i helpu'r teuluoedd hynny a'r ysgolion a'r awdurdodau lleol sydd angen i'r arian hwnnw gael ei wario.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, the £9 million that you refer to was before the UK Government budget. Once the UK Government budget had taken place and confirmation that more than £300 million was made available, the then education Minister, Lynne Neagle, was planning to spend an extra £100 million on additional learning needs, had we been re-elected.

Now, I can provide clear, irrefutable evidence of how disadvantaged and disabled children will pay the price for your uncosted pledges. Clwb Cwtsh, which is the only provider of school holiday play for children with complex needs in north Wales, has just been told by the Plaid Government that funding for its services will end. The previous Labour Government here funded that provision, which is, as I say, for children with complex needs. I'm afraid, unless your Government makes a u-turn on this, changes its mind and provides the funding to Clwb Cwtsh, it will be lost. So, can I urge you to reconsider the decision to end funding for this provision? Otherwise, I'm afraid disabled children will be paying the price for free childcare for millionaires.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, roedd y £9 miliwn yr ydych chi'n cyfeirio ato cyn cyllideb Llywodraeth y DU. Ar ôl i gyllideb Llywodraeth y DU fod yn weithredol a chadarnhad bod mwy na £300 miliwn ar gael, roedd y gweinidog addysg ar y pryd, Lynne Neagle, yn bwriadu gwario £100 miliwn yn ychwanegol ar anghenion dysgu ychwanegol, pe baem ni'n cael ein hail-ethol.

Nawr, gallaf ddarparu tystiolaeth eglur ac anwadadwy o sut y bydd plant difreintiedig ac anabl yn talu'r pris am eich addewidion heb eu costio. Mae Clwb Cwtsh, sef unig ddarparwr cylch chwarae gwyliau ysgol i blant ag anghenion cymhleth yng ngogledd Cymru, newydd gael ei hysbysu gan Lywodraeth Plaid Cymru y bydd cyllid ar gyfer ei wasanaethau yn dod i ben. Fe wnaeth y Llywodraeth Lafur flaenorol yma ariannu'r ddarpariaeth honno, sydd, fel y dywedais i, ar gyfer plant ag anghenion cymhleth. Mae gen i ofn, oni bai fod eich Llywodraeth yn gwneud tro pedol ar hyn, yn newid ei meddwl ac yn darparu'r cyllid i Clwb Cwtsh, bydd yn cael ei golli. Felly, a gaf i eich annog i ailystyried y penderfyniad i roi terfyn ar gyllid ar gyfer y ddarpariaeth hon? Fel arall, rwy'n ofni y bydd plant anabl yn talu'r pris am ofal plant am ddim i filiwnyddion.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I ask the Member to look again at when they were promising £9 million, and it was very much after that money was made available. And there are principles here about the ability for us to set directions here in Wales. I am familiar with Clwb Cwtsh. I don't know why the previous Labour administration didn't put its funding on a permanent basis. The Member might be able to shed some light on that. I do understand also that it fills an ALN gap. The Member is asking for £30,000 for that; I have £40 million on the table that I have sought, and continue to seek, agreement with the Member on. That money includes money that would directly go to Flintshire council, so I'm imagining that the leader of Flintshire council would be keen for the Labour leader here to help us get that money out of the door.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gofynnaf i'r Aelod edrych eto ar pryd roedden nhw'n addo £9 miliwn, ac roedd yn sicr ar ôl i'r arian hwnnw gael ei wneud ar gael. A cheir egwyddorion yma ynglŷn â'r gallu i ni bennu cyfeiriadau yma yng Nghymru. Rwy'n gyfarwydd â Clwb Cwtsh. Nid wyf i'n gwybod pam na roddodd y weinyddiaeth Lafur flaenorol ei gyllid ar sail barhaol. Efallai y bydd yr Aelod yn gallu taflu rhywfaint o oleuni ar hynny. Rwy'n deall hefyd ei fod yn llenwi bwlch ADY. Mae'r Aelod yn gofyn am £30,000 ar gyfer hynny; mae gen i £40 miliwn ar y bwrdd yr wyf i wedi gofyn am, ac yn parhau i ofyn am gytundeb gyda'r Aelod arno. Mae'r arian hwnnw yn cynnwys arian a fyddai'n mynd yn uniongyrchol i Gyngor Sir y Fflint, felly rwy'n dychmygu y byddai arweinydd Cyngor Sir y Fflint yn awyddus i'r arweinydd Llafur yma ein helpu i gael yr arian hwnnw allan drwy'r drws.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Arweinydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Darren Millar.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The leader of the Welsh Conservatives, Darren Millar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Llywydd. First Minister, last week, the UK Government published the inflation figures. They showed that inflation was up, with prices rising by 3.1 per cent in the year to August, and of course economists forecast that that increase in inflation will continue to rise to above 4 per cent around the end of this year, in the coming months. And that's going to be as a result of the energy price cap going up, the increase in fuel prices eventually coming through. Now, many households in Wales are facing the pinch in their pockets, and they desperately need help. One thing that your Government could do to help people here in Wales is to take action on council tax. Can I ask you, First Minister, instead of making yet more demands for more power, why don't you help people with their council tax demands? Why don't you initiate a cap on council tax and legislate, with the powers that you already have, so that people require a referendum in order to give local residents a say for any increase above that cap?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Brif Weinidog, yr wythnos diwethaf, cyhoeddodd Llywodraeth y DU y ffigurau chwyddiant. Roedden nhw'n dangos bod chwyddiant wedi cynyddu, â phrisiau yn codi 3.1 y cant yn y flwyddyn hyd at fis Awst, ac wrth gwrs mae economegwyr yn rhagweld y bydd y cynnydd hwnnw i chwyddiant yn parhau i godi i dros 4 y cant tua diwedd eleni, yn y misoedd nesaf. Ac mae hynny'n mynd i fod o ganlyniad i'r cap ar brisiau ynni yn codi, a'r cynnydd i brisiau tanwydd cael eu cyflwyno yn y pen draw. Nawr, mae llawer o aelwydydd yng Nghymru yn wynebu'r brath yn eu pocedi, ac mae angen cymorth arnyn nhw'n daer. Un peth y gallai eich Llywodraeth ei wneud i helpu pobl yma yng Nghymru yw gweithredu ar y dreth gyngor. A gaf i ofyn i chi, Brif Weinidog, yn hytrach na gwneud mwy o alwadau am fwy o rym, pam na wnewch chi helpu pobl gyda'u gofynion treth gyngor? Pam nad wnewch chi sefydlu cap ar dreth gyngor a deddfu, gyda'r pwerau sydd gennych chi eisoes, fel bod pobl angen refferendwm er mwyn rhoi llais i drigolion lleol am unrhyw gynnydd uwchben y cap hwnnw?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I understand that the leader of the Conservatives wants to replicate policy in England. I'm interested in what works for Wales and it's about what works for council tax payers, Llywydd, and it's what works within the bounds of the finances of Welsh Government. And I remind the Senedd that we will be facing a real-terms cut in the day-to-day spending that we have available in the next financial year.

Council tax is set, of course, by local authorities and it's important that it is. I would remind the Member that, in a recent budget deal before we came into power, we made sure that there was a baseline for an increase in funding for councils, and a big part of that was to protect council tax payers, which I agree is something that's very, very important indeed.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n deall bod arweinydd y Ceidwadwyr eisiau copïo polisi yn Lloegr. Mae gen i ddiddordeb yn yr hyn sy'n gweithio i Gymru ac mae'n ymwneud â'r hyn sy'n gweithio i dalwyr y dreth gyngor, Lywydd, ac yn fater o'r hyn sy'n gweithio o fewn ffiniau cyllid Llywodraeth Cymru. Ac rwy'n atgoffa'r Senedd y byddwn ni'n wynebu toriad termau real i'r gwariant o ddydd i ddydd sydd gennym ni ar gael yn y flwyddyn ariannol nesaf.

Mae'r dreth gyngor yn cael ei phennu, wrth gwrs, gan awdurdodau lleol ac mae'n bwysig ei bod. Hoffwn atgoffa'r Aelod ein bod ni wedi gwneud yn siŵr, mewn cytundeb cyllideb diweddar cyn i ni ddod i rym, bod llinell sylfaen ar gyfer cynnydd i gyllid ar gyfer cynghorau, a rhan fawr o hynny oedd amddiffyn talwyr treth gyngor, yr wyf i'n cytuno sy'n rhywbeth sydd wir yn bwysig iawn, iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You know, I was listening to the radio this morning and I heard one of the commentators talking about it being a bad week for NATS; I thought they were talking about the Welsh nats, but actually, they were talking about the National Air Traffic Services, as it happens, and the chaos at our airports. [Laughter.]

One of the things that I want to see is fairness for council tax payers in Wales. You often talk about the need for fair funding between the England and Wales settlement—I get that, I completely get that and we support you on fair funding—but we need fair funding in Wales and we need fairness in council tax bills for people who have to struggle to pay them each and every year. The average band D council tax bill in Wales has risen by more than £600 over the past five years, and some residents have faced hikes of over 50 per cent over that period. It's totally unacceptable. We need urgent action to protect people from the sorts of excessive rises that some people have been having. So, can I urge you again: introduce a cap, legislate so that people have to have referendums for anything above that cap and do one more thing too—let's have a review, an independent review, truly independent of the local government funding formula, to make sure that there's fair funding to all parts of Wales, not just places favoured by the previous Labour Government.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wyddoch chi, roeddwn i'n gwrando ar y radio y bore yma a chlywais un o'r sylwebwyr yn siarad am y ffaith ei bod hi'n wythnos wael i NATS; roeddwn i'n meddwl eu bod nhw'n siarad am nats Cymru, ond mewn gwirionedd, roedden nhw'n siarad am y Gwasanaethau Traffig Awyr Cenedlaethol, fel mae'n digwydd, a'r anhrefn yn ein meysydd awyr. [Chwerthin.]

Un o'r pethau yr wyf i eisiau ei weld yw tegwch i dalwyr y dreth gyngor yng Nghymru. Rydych chi'n sôn yn aml am yr angen am gyllid teg rhwng setliad Cymru a Lloegr—rwy'n deall hynny, rwy'n deall hynny'n llwyr ac rydym ni'n eich cefnogi ar gyllid teg—ond mae angen cyllid teg arnom ni yng Nghymru ac mae angen tegwch arnom ni o ran biliau'r dreth gyngor i bobl sy'n gorfod mynd i drafferthion i'w talu bob blwyddyn. Mae'r bil treth gyngor band D cyfartalog yng Nghymru wedi codi mwy na £600 dros y pum mlynedd diwethaf, ac mae rhai trigolion wedi wynebu cynnydd o dros 50 y cant dros y cyfnod hwnnw. Mae'n gwbl annerbyniol. Mae angen gweithredu brys i amddiffyn pobl rhag y mathau o gynnydd gormodol y mae rhai pobl wedi bod yn eu hwynebu. Felly, a gaf i eich annog chi eto: cyflwynwch gap, deddfwch fel bod yn rhaid i bobl gael refferendwm ar gyfer unrhyw beth uwchlaw'r cap hwnnw a gwnewch un peth arall hefyd—gadewch i ni gael adolygiad, adolygiad annibynnol, yn wirioneddol annibynnol ar fformiwla cyllido llywodraeth leol, i wneud yn siŵr bod cyllid teg i bob rhan o Gymru, nid lleoedd a ffafriwyd gan y Llywodraeth Lafur flaenorol yn unig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Let's be positive and concentrate on the things that we agree on. Absolutely, we want to review, and looking at my local government Cabinet Minister, that is something that is happening under this Government, because it's important that people understand and feel that the decisions taken by Wales are equitable.

The other element that I agree with him on is that we need fair funding for Wales. We have lived under successive Conservative Governments and now Labour Governments that are still not engaging on that need to get the fundamentals right when it comes to fair funding for Wales. And you can't separate the two. It is an absolute truism that a lack of fair funding at the top will come down in the end to the money in the pockets of people the length and breadth of Wales, including through pressures on council tax. We want to be able to help in many ways that we can.

And on the rather glib start, if you're going to say it's a bad week for nats, actually choose a week that is a bad week for this Government. We're about to publish our programme for government, which is about transforming Wales, putting the health service on a firmer footing, raising education standards, halving that productivity gap with the rest of the UK, creating great job opportunities, the most generous childcare offer anywhere in the UK in dealing with child poverty, and standing up for Wales, always, which is something I'm not hearing from any other party in this Chamber.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gadewch i ni fod yn gadarnhaol a chanolbwyntio ar y pethau yr ydym ni'n cytuno arnyn nhw. Yn sicr, rydym ni eisiau adolygu, a chan edrych ar fy Ngweinidog Cabinet llywodraeth leol, mae hynny'n rhywbeth sy'n digwydd o dan y Llywodraeth hon, oherwydd mae'n bwysig bod pobl yn deall ac yn teimlo bod y penderfyniadau sy'n cael eu gwneud gan Gymru yn deg.

Yr elfen arall yr wyf i'n cytuno ag ef arni yw bod angen cyllid teg arnom i Gymru. Rydym ni wedi byw o dan Lywodraethau Ceidwadol olynol a Llywodraethau Llafur bellach sydd dal ddim yn ymgysylltu ar yr angen hwnnw i gael y pethau sylfaenol iawn o ran cyllid teg i Gymru. Ac allwch chi ddim gwahanu'r ddau. Mae'n wirionedd absoliwt y bydd diffyg cyllid teg ar y brig yn dod i lawr yn y pen draw i'r arian ym mhocedi pobl ar hyd a lled Cymru, gan gynnwys trwy bwysau ar dreth gyngor. Rydym ni eisiau gallu helpu mewn llawer o ffyrdd y gallwn.

Ac ar y cychwyn slic braidd, os ydych chi'n mynd i ddweud ei bod hi'n wythnos wael i nats, dylech chi ddewis wythnos sy'n wythnos wael i'r Llywodraeth hon. Rydym ni ar fin cyhoeddi ein rhaglen lywodraethu, sydd â'r bwriad o drawsnewid Cymru, rhoi'r gwasanaeth iechyd ar sail fwy cadarn, codi safonau addysg, haneru'r bwlch cynhyrchiant hwnnw gyda gweddill y DU, creu cyfleoedd gwaith gwych, y cynnig gofal plant mwyaf hael yn unrhyw le yn y DU wrth ymdrin â thlodi plant, a sefyll yn gadarn dros Gymru, bob amser, sy'n rhywbeth nad wyf i'n ei glywed gan unrhyw blaid arall yn y Siambr hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Tywydd Garw ac Eithafol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Adverse and Extreme Weather

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i baratoi ar gyfer digwyddiadau tywydd garw ac eithafol y gaeaf hwn? OQ64508
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What is the Welsh Government doing to prepare for adverse and extreme weather events this winter? OQ64508

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I know the Member agrees with me that the evidence is clear: climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather. We are committed to building stronger, more resilient communities across Wales in that changing context. We're working closely with partners, including through the Wales resilience forum and local resilience forums to prepare for winter risks, to strengthen response arrangements and learn from recent extreme weather events. We're also making communities more resilient to flooding through continued investment in infrastructure and nature-based solutions.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n gwybod bod yr Aelod yn cytuno â mi bod y dystiolaeth yn eglur: mae newid hinsawdd yn cynyddu amlder a dwysedd tywydd eithafol. Rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i greu cymunedau cryfach, mwy gwydn ledled Cymru yn y cyd-destun newidiol hwnnw. Rydym ni'n gweithio'n agos gyda phartneriaid, gan gynnwys drwy fforwm gwytnwch Cymru a fforymau gwytnwch lleol i baratoi ar gyfer risgiau'r gaeaf, i gryfhau trefniadau ymateb ac i ddysgu o ddigwyddiadau tywydd eithafol diweddar. Rydym ni hefyd yn gwneud cymunedau yn fwy gwydn yn erbyn llifogydd trwy fuddsoddiad parhaus mewn seilwaith ac atebion sy'n seiliedig ar natur.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. Last week, First Minister, you issued a statement saying that you will convene a resilience summit focusing on wildfires—very much welcomed. Yet, we must be ready for all of the escalating risks of a changing climate. This includes extreme cold, winter flooding and severe storms this coming winter. The Met Office has warned of a heightened risk on the horizon due to an unprecedented El Niño event this year, only highlighted in shocking headlines yesterday, recording the record breaking of 150 years of records. Weaknesses in our infrastructure and our resilience, such as recently witnessed in Gwaelod-y-garth, will only become more apparent in the coming months.

Wales is dangerously unprepared for the predicted onslaught of extreme weather conditions. Climate response must be integrated as our first line of defence. Welsh Government allocated in its supplementary budget just £1 million for emergency preparedness. Establishing a climate shock fund would be a vital step forward in demonstrating that the Welsh Government is serious about protecting communities this winter, with or without UK Government support. What discussions has the First Minister had with the UK Government on funding these emergency measures? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch. Yr wythnos diwethaf, Brif Weinidog, fe wnaethoch chi gyhoeddi datganiad yn dweud y byddwch chi'n cynnull uwchgynhadledd wydnwch sy'n canolbwyntio ar danau gwyllt—i'w groesawu'n fawr. Eto, mae'n rhaid i ni fod yn barod ar gyfer holl risgiau cynyddol hinsawdd sy'n newid. Mae hyn yn cynnwys oerfel eithafol, llifogydd gaeaf a stormydd difrifol yn ystod gaeaf nesaf hwn. Mae'r Swyddfa Dywydd wedi rhybuddio am risg uwch ar y gorwel oherwydd digwyddiad El Niño digynsail eleni, y tynnwyd sylw ato dim ond ddoe mewn penawdau arswydus ddoe, yn cofnodi torri recordiau 150 mlynedd o recordiau. Bydd gwendidau yn ein seilwaith a'n gwydnwch, fel y gwelwyd yn ddiweddar yng Ngwaelod-y-garth, ddim ond yn dod yn fwy amlwg yn y misoedd nesaf.

Mae Cymru'n beryglus o amharod ar gyfer yr ymosodiad a ragwelir o amodau tywydd eithafol. Mae'n rhaid integreiddio ymateb i'r hinsawdd fel ein llinell amddiffyn gyntaf. Dim ond £1 filiwn wnaeth Llywodraeth Cymru ei ddyrannu yn ei chyllideb atodol ar gyfer parodrwydd ar gyfer argyfwng. Byddai sefydlu cronfa sioc hinsawdd yn gam hanfodol ymlaen i ddangos bod Llywodraeth Cymru o ddifrif ynglŷn â diogelu cymunedau y gaeaf hwn, gyda neu heb gymorth Llywodraeth y DU. Pa drafodaethau y mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi eu cael gyda Llywodraeth y DU ar ariannu'r mesurau brys hyn? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for the question. I think the world is largely unprepared for the challenges that we face. The question is how can we accelerate our preparedness. You will see in the programme for government today that climate change isn't seen as a priority in and of itself; it's one of the priorities that binds us all together as Government Ministers, because this has to be addressed across all portfolios.

Resilience—I talked about this last week—is an issue that I have tried to focus a great deal on since I came into the role of First Minister, understanding the various elements that contribute to the resilience, or lack of, in some ways, that we have as a society. Wildfires happen to be the one that has grabbed our attention, which is why we need to make sure that we're tightening up those resilience elements around that in the summit on 22 October. But the Member is right; flooding is something that many communities will be concerned about. There are other concerns too—the effects of heat, the effects of cold and so on.

It is something that we work across the UK on. I want to ensure (a) that Wales gets its fair share of resilience funding, civil contingency funding, across the UK, and that's something I'm eager to pursue. But the Member has my word that I will absolutely be looking at how we work between Welsh Government and UK Government to get the support that Wales needs to prepare for this wide range of threats that we face in future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am y cwestiwn. Rwy'n credu bod y byd yn amharod i raddau helaeth ar gyfer yr heriau sy'n ein hwynebu. Y cwestiwn yw sut allwn ni gyflymu ein parodrwydd. Byddwch yn gweld yn y rhaglen lywodraethu heddiw nad yw newid hinsawdd yn cael ei ystyried yn flaenoriaeth ynddo'i hun; mae'n un o'r blaenoriaethau sy'n ein clymu ni i gyd gyda'n gilydd fel Gweinidogion Llywodraeth, oherwydd mae'n rhaid mynd i'r afael â hyn ar draws pob portffolio.

Mae gwydnwch—siaradais am hyn yr wythnos diwethaf—yn fater yr wyf i wedi ceisio canolbwyntio'n fawr iawn arno ers i mi ddechrau swydd y Prif Weinidog, gan ddeall y gwahanol elfennau sy'n cyfrannu at y gwydnwch, neu'r diffyg gwydnwch, mewn rhai ffyrdd, sydd gennym ni fel cymdeithas. Yn digwydd bod, tanau gwyllt yw'r un sydd wedi dal ein sylw, a dyna pam mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n tynhau'r elfennau gwydnwch hynny o gwmpas hynny yn yr uwchgynhadledd ar 22 Hydref. Ond mae'r Aelod yn iawn; mae llifogydd yn rhywbeth y bydd llawer o gymunedau yn poeni amdano. Ceir pryderon eraill hefyd—effeithiau gwres, effeithiau oerfel ac yn y blaen.

Mae'n rhywbeth yr ydym ni'n gweithio arno ledled y DU. Rwyf i eisiau sicrhau (a) bod Cymru yn cael ei chyfran deg o gyllid gwydnwch, cyllid argyfyngau sifil posibl, ledled y DU, ac mae hynny'n rhywbeth yr wyf i'n awyddus i fynd ar ei drywydd. Ond rwy'n rhoi fy ngair i'r Aelod y byddaf i'n edrych ar sut rydym ni'n gweithio rhwng Llywodraeth Cymru a Llywodraeth y DU i gael y cymorth sydd ei angen ar Gymru i baratoi ar gyfer yr amrywiaeth eang hon o fygythiadau sy'n ein hwynebu yn y dyfodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, I recognise that £85 million has been invested in flood risk management this year, but Rhondda Cynon Taf's investigation into storm Dennis has found that Blaenllechau was flooded from the steep hillside above it, that felling on Welsh Government-owned Natural Resources Wales-managed woodland may have contributed to surface water run-off, and that modelling suggested three of the four culvert networks lacked adequate capacity. This August, a major wildfire burned around 150 hectares of Llanwonno mountain, above Blaenllechau and Ferndale. So, before the winter rain arrives, will you ensure that Natural Resources Wales and RCT carry out a co-ordinated inspection of that hillside, its drainage and culverts, with the Mining Remediation Authority checking any relevant higher category coal tips within or below that affected area, and report the findings and any remedial work required to the Senedd by the end of October? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, rwy'n cydnabod bod £85 miliwn wedi cael ei fuddsoddi mewn rheoli perygl llifogydd eleni, ond mae ymchwiliad Rhondda Cynon Taf i storm Dennis wedi canfod bod Blaenllechau wedi dioddef llifogydd o'r llethr serth uwch ei ben, y gallai torri coed ar goetir sy'n eiddo i Lywodraeth Cymru ac a reolir gan Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru fod wedi cyfrannu at ddŵr wyneb ffo, a bod modelu wedi awgrymu nad oedd gan dri o'r pedwar rhwydwaith cwlfertau gapasiti digonol. Ym mis Awst eleni, llosgodd tanau gwyllt mawr tua 150 hectar o fynydd Llanwynno, uwchben Blaenllechau a Glynrhedynog. Felly, cyn i law y gaeaf gyrraedd, a wnewch chi sicrhau bod Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru a RhCT yn cynnal archwiliad cydgysylltiedig o'r llethr hwnnw, ei ddraeniad a'i gwlfertau, gyda'r Awdurdod Adfer Safleoedd Mwyngloddio yn gwirio unrhyw domenni glo categori uwch perthnasol o fewn neu islaw'r ardal honno yr effeithiwyd arni, ac adrodd ar y canfyddiadau ac unrhyw waith adfer sydd ei angen i'r Senedd erbyn diwedd mis Hydref? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
There is, of course, an ongoing programme of works that need to happen, some of them under the auspices of Welsh Government or its agencies, Natural Resources Wales, some that are the responsibility of local authorities. I have no doubt that, as we face the challenges of the winter, there needs to be just a double-checking of the robustness of those measures being put in place. I would say that, as well as making sure that your culverts are able to deal with run-off, there are other questions and innovations that we need to be looking at in how you slow down that run-off. Clearly, hot weather—hard ground—makes the situation more difficult. I'm really interested in how we manage the land, working with farmers to try to limit run-off, and so on.

We have to be aware that there are no silver bullets, there are no single measures that can be taken as we face these threats. They are multiple, and the need to be strategic in the way that we approach this is important, which is why the wildfire summit, in particular, looking at that threat, brings in so many different partners who will be able to contribute to making our resilience that much stronger. But I'm sure that your message will have been heard by the local authorities and others today.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae, wrth gwrs, rhaglen barhaus o waith y mae angen ei wneud, rhywfaint ohono o dan nawdd Llywodraeth Cymru neu ei hasiantaethau, Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru, rhywfaint sy'n gyfrifoldeb awdurdodau lleol. Nid oes gen i unrhyw amheuaeth, wrth i ni wynebu heriau'r gaeaf, fod angen ail-wirio cadernid y mesurau hynny sy'n cael eu rhoi ar waith. Byddwn yn dweud, yn ogystal â gwneud yn siŵr bod eich cwlfertau yn gallu delio â dŵr ffo, bod cwestiynau ac arloesiadau eraill y mae angen i ni fod yn edrych arnyn nhw o ran sut rydych chi'n arafu'r dŵr ffo hwnnw. Yn amlwg, mae tywydd poeth—tir caled—yn gwneud y sefyllfa'n anoddach. Mae gen i ddiddordeb mawr yn sut rydym ni'n rheoli'r tir, gan weithio gyda ffermwyr i geisio cyfyngu dŵr ffo, ac yn y blaen.

Mae'n rhaid i ni fod yn ymwybodol nad oes un ateb, nid oes unrhyw fesurau unigol y gellir eu cymryd wrth i ni wynebu'r bygythiadau hyn. Maen nhw'n lluosog, ac mae'r angen i fod yn strategol yn y ffordd yr ydym ni'n mynd i'r afael â hyn yn bwysig, a dyna pam mae'r uwchgynhadledd tanau gwyllt, yn arbennig, yn edrych ar y bygythiad hwnnw, yn dod â chynifer o wahanol bartneriaid a fydd yn gallu cyfrannu at wneud ein gwydnwch gymaint cryfach. Ond rwy'n siŵr y bydd eich neges wedi cael ei chlywed gan yr awdurdodau lleol ac eraill heddiw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, Monmouthshire has faced catastrophic flooding in recent years, and I was pleased that you were able to visit Monmouth and Abergavenny before the Senedd elections to speak to some of the local people affected, as well as to those finding solutions—long-lasting solutions—upstream. The scenes from last year’s flooding, especially those from Monmouth, will be etched in the memory of everyone who saw them for a long time. These once in 100 years events are getting more and more frequent, and we must now assume that they could happen at any time. As we've heard, the approaching El Niño event is on the horizon, with extreme weather events already anticipated, so, with this in mind, how is the Government improving flood preparedness for this winter? And in the longer term, how can we learn from the experiences of Monmouthshire residents to improve flood management for their community and for all of Wales? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, mae sir Fynwy wedi wynebu llifogydd trychinebus yn y blynyddoedd diwethaf, ac roeddwn i'n falch eich bod chi wedi gallu ymweld â Threfynwy a'r Fenni cyn etholiadau'r Senedd i siarad â rhai o'r bobl leol yr effeithiwyd arnyn nhw, yn ogystal â'r rhai sy'n dod o hyd i atebion—atebion hirhoedlog—i fyny'r afon. Bydd y golygfeydd o lifogydd y llynedd, yn enwedig y rhai o Drefynwy, wedi'u hysgythru yng nghof pawb a'u gwelodd am amser maith. Mae'r digwyddiadau unwaith mewn 100 mlynedd hyn yn dod yn fwyfwy aml, ac mae'n rhaid i ni dybio bellach y gallen nhw ddigwydd ar unrhyw adeg. Fel yr ydym ni wedi clywed, mae'r digwyddiad El Niño ar y gorwel, â digwyddiadau tywydd eithafol yn cael eu rhagweld eisoes, felly, gyda hyn mewn golwg, sut mae'r Llywodraeth yn gwella parodrwydd ar gyfer llifogydd ar gyfer y gaeaf hwn? Ac yn y tymor hwy, sut allwn ni ddysgu o brofiadau trigolion sir Fynwy i wella gwaith rheoli llifogydd i'w cymuned ac i Gymru gyfan? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I was pleased, along with the Member, to speak with some of the individuals who were affected by the pretty devasting flooding that they experienced in Monmouth. The Member's right that it is about learning lessons. It's not just about cleaning up; that's the first step. It's about trying to make sure that lessons are learnt for those localities in order to avoid and avert flooding, but lessons for elsewhere too, and I know that Monmouthshire County Council is preparing its section 19 flood investigation report following the devastation of storm Claudia, and the flood investigation report is almost complete, I understand, and will be published in October. But, wherever those floods are, the learnings are ones that we can try to make sure that they are applicable in other parts of Wales too.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Roeddwn i'n falch, ynghyd â'r Aelod, o siarad â rhai o'r unigolion a gafodd eu heffeithio gan y llifogydd eithaf ofnadwy y gwnaethon nhw eu dioddef yn Nhrefynwy. Mae'r Aelod yn iawn ei fod yn fater o ddysgu gwersi. Nid yw'n fater o lanhau yn unig; dyna'r cam cyntaf. Mae'n fater o geisio gwneud yn siŵr bod gwersi yn cael eu dysgu ar gyfer yr ardaloedd hynny er mwyn osgoi ac atal llifogydd, ond gwersi i fannau eraill hefyd, ac rwy'n gwybod bod Cyngor Sir Fynwy yn paratoi ei adroddiad ymchwiliad llifogydd adran 19 yn dilyn dinistr storm Claudia, ac mae'r adroddiad ymchwilio i lifogydd bron wedi'i gwblhau, rwy'n deall, a bydd yn cael ei gyhoeddi ym mis Hydref. Ond, ble bynnag y mae'r llifogydd hynny, mae'r pethau hynny i'w dysgu yn rhai y gallwn ni geisio gwneud yn siŵr eu bod nhw'n berthnasol mewn rhannau eraill o Gymru hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, my colleague Jayne Bryant, asked you, during your oral statement last week, whether the Welsh Government would consider bringing in a climate resilience fund to help us mitigate the impacts of extreme weather. You didn't really answer her directly, and nor did you answer Anthony Slaughter when he raised a very similar point in his opening question. Now, there's widespread support for this from stakeholders that we on the Welsh Labour benches have engaged with over the summer recess. And with resources for agencies involved in climate mitigation measures being really stretched, this is one way to safeguard those funds and make sure they're channelled in the right way. So, is this something that your Government can explore setting up ahead of your wildfire summit next month?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, fy wnaeth fy nghyd-Aelod, Jayne Bryant, ofyn i chi, yn ystod eich datganiad llafar yr wythnos diwethaf, a fyddai Llywodraeth Cymru yn ystyried cyflwyno cronfa gwydnwch hinsawdd i'n helpu i liniaru effeithiau tywydd eithafol. Wnaethoch chi ddim ei hateb yn uniongyrchol, ac wnaethoch chi ddim ateb Anthony Slaughter chwaith pan gododd bwynt tebyg iawn yn ei gwestiwn agoriadol. Nawr, mae cefnogaeth eang i hyn gan randdeiliaid yr ydym ni ar feinciau Llafur Cymru wedi ymgysylltu â nhw dros doriad yr haf. A gydag adnoddau ar gyfer asiantaethau sy'n ymwneud â mesurau lliniaru newid hinsawdd wir yn cael eu hymestyn, mae hon yn un ffordd o ddiogelu'r cyllid hwnnw a gwneud yn siŵr ei fod yn cael ei ddyrannu yn y ffordd gywir. Felly, a yw hyn yn rhywbeth y gall eich Llywodraeth ystyried ei sefydlu cyn eich uwchgynhadledd tanau gwyllt fis nesaf?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: No attempt to avoid the question. There are, in effect, a number of funds, aren't there, on which a Government can draw to deal with emergencies. What you want to make sure is that those funds themselves are resilient. I absolutely am ready to consider whether we can bring together funds in one place, in the same way as the Government is looking at how we can put preventative health funds under one banner, so that we can measure better what the various elements of those funding capacities are. So, absolutely willing to consider that. At the end of the day, it's making sure that we have the tools to do the job that we need. There's more than one way of doing that, but let's put that in the mix too.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Dim ymgais i osgoi'r cwestiwn. Mae nifer, i bob pwrpas, o gronfeydd, onid oes, y gall Llywodraeth fanteisio arnyn nhw i ymdrin ag argyfyngau. Yr hyn yr ydych chi eisiau ei wneud yn siŵr yw bod y cronfeydd hynny eu hunain yn wydn. Rwy'n hollol barod i ystyried a allwn ni ddod â chyllid at ei gilydd mewn un lle, yn yr un modd ag y mae'r Llywodraeth yn edrych ar sut y gallwn ni roi cronfeydd iechyd ataliol o dan un faner, fel y gallwn ni fesur yn well beth yw gwahanol elfennau y galluoedd ariannu hynny. Felly, yn hollol barod i ystyried hynny. Yn y pen draw, mae'n fater o wneud yn siŵr bod gennym ni'r arfau i wneud y gwaith sydd ei angen arnom ni. Mae mwy nag un ffordd o wneud hynny, ond gadewch i ni roi hynny yn y gymysgedd hefyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Strategaeth Fwyd Genedlaethol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: National Food Strategy

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am y cynnydd o ran datblygu strategaeth fwyd genedlaethol newydd? OQ64561
