XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, nid yw'r trosglwyddiad y mae'r Aelod yn cyfeirio ato yn berthnasol i senario'r Bil tribiwnlysoedd. Dyna'r peth cyntaf i'w ddweud. O ran datganoli pellach, mater gwleidyddol yw hwnnw'n amlwg. Nid wyf i'n rhan o'r peiriant gwleidyddol fel y cyfryw. Rwy'n cael fy nghyflogi gan Lywodraeth Cymru ar faterion cyfreithiol. Os a phryd y byddem ni'n cyrraedd sefyllfa lle gofynnir i mi am fy nghyngor ynglŷn â'r pwyntiau y mae o'n eu codi yn briodol iawn, yna fe fyddaf i'n rhoi fy nghyngor eglur ar y cam hwnnw. Ar hyn o bryd, ni allaf fod o unrhyw gymorth pellach.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Mike Hedges.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Labour spokesperson, Mike Hedges.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. What discussion has the Counsel General had with the Law Society regarding securing fully funded level 7 solicitor apprenticeships in Wales? Level 7 solicitor apprenticeships are a well-established route to qualifications in England, allowing aspiring solicitors to earn while they learn and avoid taking on significant tuition debt. In Wales, however, aspiring solicitors still cannot access an equivalent funded route. The uptake of level 7 solicitor apprenticeships in England has grown, with more than 5,000 people starting an apprenticeship between 2018 and 2025. We cannot allow Wales to be left behind, can we?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch. Pa drafodaeth a gafodd y Cwnsler Cyffredinol gyda Chymdeithas y Gyfraith ynglŷn â sicrhau prentisiaethau cyfreithwyr lefel 7 a ariennir yn llawn yng Nghymru? Mae prentisiaethau cyfreithwyr lefel 7 yn cynnig llwybr sefydledig i gymwysterau yn Lloegr, sy'n caniatáu i rai sy'n awyddus i fod yn gyfreithwyr ennill arian wrth ddysgu ac osgoi mynd i ddyled sylweddol wrth hyfforddi. Yng Nghymru, serch hynny, ni all darpar gyfreithwyr fyth gymryd mantais ar lwybr cyfatebol sy'n cael ei ariannu. Mae'r defnydd o brentisiaethau cyfreithwyr lefel 7 wedi cynyddu yn Lloegr, a mwy na 5,000 o bobl yn dechrau ar brentisiaeth rhwng 2018 a 2025. Ni ddylem ni ganiatáu i Gymru gael ei gadael ar ôl, ddylem ni?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: That is a very good question, and I fully agree with the Member on what he says. What I can tell him, which may cheer him up slightly, is that level 7 apprenticeships at the bar and also solicitors are uppermost in this Government's mind. We are pushing forward on them and, indeed, I shall be making a speech on them in about a fortnight's time, during the Legal Wales conference. So, as he is interested, I'll send him a copy of the speech, and he can see that we are doing what we can.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae hwnnw'n gwestiwn da iawn, ac rwy'n cytuno yn llwyr â'r hyn y mae'r Aelod yn ei ddweud. Yr hyn y gallaf i ei ddweud wrtho, a allai ei galonogi ychydig, yw bod prentisiaethau lefel 7 wrth y bar a chyfreithwyr hefyd yn uchel iawn yn ystyriaethau'r Llywodraeth hon. Rydym ni'n gwthio ymlaen ar hynny ac, yn wir, fe fyddaf i'n rhoi araith ar hynny ymhen rhyw bythefnos, yn ystod cynhadledd Cymru'r Gyfraith. Felly, gan fod diddordeb ganddo, fe wnaf i anfon copi o'r araith ato, ac fe gaiff weld ein bod ni'n gwneud yr hyn allwn ni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you very much for that answer. Let's see if I can keep being on a roll. Access to justice is a core component of the rule of law and yet many areas of Wales are facing a growing crisis in access to legal services. Described as legal deserts, these are areas where the presence of solicitors is so limited that people cannot easily obtain legal advice or representation when they need it. The Law Society has produced a report that draws on the latest data available, including solicitor distribution, demographic trends and the impact of legal aid funding pressures. The findings include severe geographic inequality in solicitor density, rising solicitor retirements without adequate replacements, the attrition of legal aid providers, and increasing numbers of unrepresented litigants in civil, criminal and welfare cases. What are the Counsel General's views on this report?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi am yr ateb hwnnw. Gadewch inni weld a allaf barhau i fod yn llwyddiannus. Mae mynediad at gyfiawnder yn ddarn creiddiol o reolaeth y gyfraith ac eto mae llawer ardal yng Nghymru yn wynebu argyfwng cynyddol o ran mynediad at wasanaethau cyfreithiol. Fe'u gelwir yn ddiffeithdiroedd cyfreithiol ac mae'r rhain yn ardaloedd lle mae presenoldeb cyfreithwyr mor brin fel na all pobl gael cyngor na chynrychiolaeth gan gyfreithiwr yn rhwydd pan fydd ei angen arnynt. XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cymhwysedd Deddfwriaethol y Senedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Senedd’s Legislative Competence

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa gyngor cyfreithiol y mae’r Cwnsler Cyffredinol wedi’i roi i’r Llywodraeth ar amddiffyn cymhwysedd deddfwriaethol y Senedd lle mae safbwyntiau Llywodraeth Cymru a Llywodraeth y DU yn wahanol? OQ64507
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What legal advice has the Counsel General provided to the Government regarding maintaining the Senedd’s legislative competence where the Welsh Government and UK Government's views differ? OQ64507

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, of course, the role of Welsh Government is to defend the devolution settlement, but also to ensure that things such as the Sewel convention are observed, and to defend and extend the relationship, one hopes. In July of this year, I published the Welsh Government's principles on UK legislation in devolved areas, and this includes a commitment that the UK legislation in devolved areas will only be used where the legislation protects or strengthens the devolution settlement and does not introduce new constraints on devolved competence. I am very clear, as is this Government, that we are focused on enhancing the devolution settlement and, with that, the Senedd’s legislative competence, rather than simply maintaining it. However, where there are attempts to limit or constrain the Senedd’s legislative competence, these will be firmly resisted, and this includes opposing the imposition of any further reservations or restrictions in the Government of Wales Act 2006, as well as securing relevant consents and carve-outs to ensure that devolved provisions conferred by UK parliamentary Acts can be removed by the Senedd at a later date. And I think key to all of this is the principle of legislative consent as set out clearly in the Sewel convention. This is essential to our devolution settlement and safeguards the Senedd’s role as the Welsh national legislature. As Counsel General, I am clear that the Sewel convention must be respected, particularly where there are any attempts to reduce or restrict the Senedd’s legislative competence via UK legislation.

Now, the Government's view is we would like it to have statutory underpinning. That is not forthcoming at the moment. There are discussions going on. Meantime, what is currently happening is there's a detailed discussion about a firm, proper solid memorandum of understanding on Sewel. It's probably second-best to having it on a statutory footing, but it is being undertaken and discussed as we speak now. So, something is happening. I fully appreciate the force of the question. It is vital that we ensure that Sewel is respected, as it has been disrespected so often of late.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, wrth gwrs, gwaith Llywodraeth Cymru yw amddiffyn y setliad datganoli, ond hefyd i sicrhau bod pethau fel confensiwn Sewel yn cael eu dilyn, yn ogystal ag amddiffyn ac ymestyn y berthynas, mae rhywun yn gobeithio. Ym mis Gorffennaf eleni, fe gyhoeddais egwyddorion Llywodraeth Cymru ar ddeddfwriaeth y DU yn y meysydd datganoledig, ac mae hyn yn cynnwys ymrwymiad y bydd deddfwriaeth y DU yn y meysydd datganoledig yn cael ei defnyddio pan fo'r ddeddfwriaeth yn diogelu neu'n atgyfnerthu'r setliad datganoli yn unig ac na fydd yn cyflwyno cyfyngiadau newydd ar gymhwysedd datganoledig. Rwyf i'n eglur iawn, fel mae'r Llywodraeth hon, ein bod ni'n canolbwyntio ar loywi'r setliad datganoli a chymhwysedd deddfwriaethol y Senedd yn sgil hynny, yn hytrach na dim ond ei gynnal. Er hynny, pan fo ymdrechion i ymatal neu gyfyngu ar gymhwysedd deddfwriaethol y Senedd, fe fydd yna wrthwynebiad cadarn i'r rhain, ac mae hyn yn cynnwys gwrthwynebu gorfodaeth unrhyw ataliadau neu gyfyngiadau pellach yn Neddf Llywodraeth Cymru 2006, yn ogystal â sicrhau cydsyniadau ac eithriadau perthnasol i sicrhau y gall y Senedd hon ddiddymu darpariaethau datganoledig a gyflwynir gan Ddeddfau Senedd San Steffan yn ddiweddarach. Ac rwy'n credu bod yr egwyddor o gydsyniad deddfwriaethol yn allweddol i hyn i gyd fel y nodir yn eglur yng nghonfensiwn Sewel. Mae hyn yn hanfodol i'n setliad datganoli ac yn diogelu gwaith y Senedd fel deddfwrfa genedlaethol Cymru. Fel Cwnsler Cyffredinol, rwy'n glir bod yn rhaid parchu confensiwn Sewel, yn enwedig pan fo unrhyw ymdrechion i grebachu neu gyfyngu ar gymhwysedd deddfwriaethol y Senedd drwy gyfrwng deddfwriaeth y DU.

Rŵan, barn y Llywodraeth yw y byddem ni'n dymuno i hynny fod ar sail statudol. Nid yw hynny ar y ffordd ar hyn o bryd. Mae trafodaethau yn mynd rhagddyn nhw. Yn y cyfamser, yr hyn sy'n digwydd ar hyn o bryd yw bod trafodaeth fanwl am femorandwm cyd-ddealltwriaeth cadarn, priodol ar gonfensiwn Sewel. Mae'n debyg mai ail-orau fydd hynny i'w gael ar sail statudol, ond mae hynny'n cael ei ymdrin ag o a'i drafod ar y foment hon. Felly, mae rhywbeth yn digwydd. Rwy'n llwyr sylweddoli grym y cwestiwn. Mae'n hanfodol ein bod ni'n sicrhau bod confensiwn Sewel yn cael ei barchu, gan ei fod wedi cael ei amharchu mor fynych yn ddiweddar.

I do know, actually, that women and people from ethnic minority backgrounds are unfortunately particularly targeted by harassment and abuse. This misogyny is appalling and should be condemned by all decent campaigners. I know that the police welcome reports of any potentially unlawful material or behaviour in political campaigns. Whilst this does not take away the very real problem of abuse, anyone considering standing for election should know there is support out there. Now, that's the crucial point, I think. Ahead of next year's local elections, we are funding Elect Her to support female candidates in Wales. The programme includes a digital self-defence and self-care toolkit, including resources to support candidates to create their own digital self-care plan and strategies for dealing with online abuse. The Deputy First Minister is considering how the Welsh Government's diversity and inclusion guidance for political parties can be strengthened. So, it is an issue very much on the table at the moment. I would say that politicians and candidates should always report any harmful online material to Ofcom and also the police as appropriate. All digital campaign material must clearly show who it is being promoted by. These digital imprints ensure that there is accountability for all official campaign material. Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, eto, diolchaf i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn pwysig hwn. Rwy'n gwybod, mewn gwirionedd, bod menywod a phobl o gefndiroedd lleiafrifoedd ethnig yn arbennig yn anffodus yn cael eu targedu gan aflonyddu a chamdriniaeth. Mae'r misogynedd hwn yn ofnadwy a dylid ei gondemnio gan yr holl ymgyrchwyr gweddaidd. Rwy'n gwybod bod yr heddlu yn croesawu adroddiadau am unrhyw ddeunydd neu ymddygiad a allai fod yn anghyfreithlon mewn ymgyrchoedd gwleidyddol. Er nad yw hyn yn dileu'r broblem wirioneddol o gamdriniaeth, dylai unrhyw un sy'n ystyried sefyll etholiad wybod bod cefnogaeth allan yna. Rŵan, dyna'r pwynt hanfodol, rwy'n credu. Cyn etholiadau lleol y flwyddyn nesaf, rydym yn ariannu Elect Her i gefnogi ymgeiswyr benywaidd yng Nghymru. Mae'r rhaglen yn cynnwys pecyn cymorth hunan-amddiffyn a hunan-ofal digidol, gan gynnwys adnoddau i gefnogi ymgeiswyr i greu eu cynllun hunan-ofal digidol eu hunain a strategaethau ar gyfer ymdrin â cham-drin ar-lein. Mae'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog yn ystyried sut y gellir cryfhau canllawiau amrywiaeth a chynhwysiant Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer pleidiau gwleidyddol. Felly, mae'n fater sydd ar y bwrdd ar hyn o bryd. Byddwn yn dweud y dylai gwleidyddion ac ymgeiswyr bob amser adrodd am unrhyw ddeunydd ar-lein niweidiol i Ofcom a hefyd i'r heddlu fel y bo'n briodol. Rhaid i'r holl ddeunydd ymgyrchu digidol ddangos yn glir pwy sy'n gyfrifol am yr hyrwyddo. Mae'r argraffnodau digidol hyn yn sicrhau bod atebolrwydd am yr holl ddeunydd ymgyrchu swyddogol. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Counsel General, under Wales's electoral law voting system, voters get one vote for a political party and its list of candidates, so there's a very clear statement of accountability. What happens when a candidate asks voters to back one party, gets elected on that party's manifesto and then walks away from those commitments? The voter doesn't have to change their vote—[Interruption.]
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gwnsler Cyffredinol, o dan system bleidleisio cyfraith etholiadol Cymru, mae pleidleiswyr yn cael un bleidlais dros blaid wleidyddol a'i rhestr o ymgeiswyr, felly mae datganiad clir iawn o atebolrwydd. Beth sy'n digwydd pan fydd ymgeisydd yn gofyn i bleidleiswyr gefnogi un blaid, yna'n cael ei ethol ar faniffesto'r blaid honno ac yna'n cerdded i ffwrdd o'r ymrwymiadau hynny? Nid oes rhaid i'r pleidleisiwr newid ei bleidlais—[Torri ar draws.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We're trying to listen—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydyn ni'n ceisio gwrando—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: They can't choose another candidate—[Interruption.]
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Ni allant ddewis ymgeisydd arall—[Torri ar draws.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Colleagues, we're trying to listen to the question. I think the Counsel General is trying to listen.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gyd-aelodau, rydyn ni'n ceisio gwrando ar y cwestiwn. Rwy'n credu bod y Cwnsler Cyffredinol yn ceisio gwrando.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lywydd. Yet, the Member keeps their seat, alongside their very generous salary. Now, some learned legal minds, such as yourself, could consider that to be fraud by misrepresentation. So, Counsel General, does Welsh electoral law provide any legal protection for voters where a candidate's conduct after election departs from the political representation they were elected under? Does Plaid Cymru still consider that politicians who mislead constituents should be criminalised? And have you considered that, in order to protect Welsh democracy, the Member should do the right thing and resign? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Lywydd. Eto, mae'r Aelod yn cadw ei sedd, ynghyd â chyflog hael iawn. Nawr, gallai rhai meddyliau cyfreithiol dysgedig, fel chi, ystyried bod hynny'n dwyll trwy gamliwio. Felly, Gwnsler Cyffredinol, a yw cyfraith etholiadol Cymru yn darparu unrhyw amddiffyniad cyfreithiol i bleidleiswyr lle mae ymddygiad ymgeisydd ar ôl etholiad yn gwyro o'r gynrychiolaeth wleidyddol y cawsant eu hethol oddi tani? A yw Plaid Cymru yn dal i ystyried y dylid troseddoli gwleidyddion sy'n camarwain etholwyr? Ac ydych wedi ystyried y dylai'r Aelod wneud y peth iawn ac ymddiswyddo, er mwyn amddiffyn democratiaeth Cymru? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I regret, Llywydd, that I haven't got my wellingtons with me. [Laughter.] I've never heard such a load of muck in a long time. And I'm not getting involved in the politics of it, but is the Member seriously saying that nobody within Reform has ever switched sides during the currency of an election?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n ddrwg gen i, Lywydd, nad wyf wedi dod â fy wellingtons gyda mi. [Chwerthin.] Nid wyf erioed wedi clywed y fath lwyth o faw ers amser maith. Ac ni fyddaf yn cymryd rhan yng ngwleidyddiaeth hynny, ond a yw'r Aelod o ddifrif yn dweud nad oes neb o fewn Reform erioed wedi newid ochr tra bod etholiad yn mynd rhagddo?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We've all been elected.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydyn ni i gyd wedi cael ein hethol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: No, I'm not—. I'm the legal officer. I thank him for that question, but it's not for me. Thank you very much.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Na, dydw i ddim—. Y swyddog cyfreithiol ydw i. Diolchaf iddo am y cwestiwn yna, ond nid yw i mi. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Right. Now, we're going to try and move ahead and get some more questions in further down the list, if we can, with everybody's help.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Iawn. Nawr, rydyn ni'n mynd i geisio symud ymlaen a chael mwy o gwestiynau sydd yn is i lawr ar y rhestr, os gallwn, gyda chymorth pawb.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Felly, cwestiwn 5, Mair Rowlands.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Therefore, question 5, Mair Rowlands.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mynediad at Wasanaethau Cyfreithiol a Chyfiawnder drwy Gyfrwng y Gymraeg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Access to Legal Services and Justice through the Medium of Welsh

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Pa asesiad mae'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol wedi ei wneud o allu pobl i gael mynediad at wasanaethau cyfreithiol a chyfiawnder drwy gyfrwng y Gymraeg? OQ64495
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What assessment has the Counsel General made of people's ability to access legal services and justice through the medium of Welsh? OQ64495

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Maddeuwch imi, Mair, doeddwn i methu eich ffeindio chi am funud bach.

Mae gallu cael mynediad at wasanaethau cyfreithiol a chyfiawnder yn y Gymraeg yn rhan bwysig o fynediad at gyfiawnder yng Nghymru. Wrth imi feithrin cysylltiadau efo'r proffesiwn cyfreithiol a hefyd y sector cyfiawnder ehangach, mi fyddaf i'n dal ati i edrych ar sut y gallwn ni sicrhau gwell mynediad at gyfiawnder i gymunedau ar draws Cymru, gan gynnwys siaradwyr Cymraeg.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Forgive me, Mair, I couldn't find you for just a moment there.

The ability to access legal services and justice through the medium of Welsh is an important part of access to justice in Wales. As I engage with the legal profession and also the wider justice sector, I will continue to explore how we can improve access to justice for communities across Wales, including Welsh speakers.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Gwnsler. Ym mis Chwefror, fe adroddodd Cymdeithas y Cyfreithwyr ar yr anialwch cyfreithiol yng Nghymru, gan amlinellu sut mae mynediad pobl at wasanaethau cyfreithiol yn gostwng y tu allan i goridor yr M4. Tra bod gan Gaerdydd 12.3 cyfreithiwr i bob 1,000 o drigolion, yng ngogledd Cymru, mae'r ffigur yn agosach at 2.3 mewn bob 1,000. Mae'r anghydraddoldeb daearyddol yma'n cael effaith sylfaenol ar gymunedau Cymraeg ym Mangor Conwy Môn ac ar draws y gogledd i gael mynediad at wasanaethau cyfreithiol a chyfiawnder drwy gyfrwng y Gymraeg. A wnaiff y Cwnsler amlinellu beth yw cynlluniau'r Llywodraeth i fynd i'r afael â'r annhegwch hwn?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Counsel General. In February, the Law Society reported on the legal deserts in Wales, outlining how access to legal services declines outside the M4 corridor. While Cardiff has 12.3 solicitors for every 1,000 residents, in north Wales, the figure is closer to 2.3 per 1,000. This geographical inequality has a fundamental impact on Welsh-speaking communities in Bangor Conwy Môn and across north Wales in terms of access to legal services and justice through the medium of Welsh. Will the Counsel General outline the Government's plans to address this inequality?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Wrth gwrs, mae mynediad at gyfiawnder yn fwy o lawer na mynediad at y llysoedd yn unig. Mae'n rhaid i bobl allu deall eu hawliau, cael cyngor dibynadwy ar yr adeg iawn a chymryd rhan yn effeithiol mewn prosesau cyfreithiol sy'n effeithio arnyn nhw. Mae gallu i ddefnyddio'r Gymraeg mewn achosion cyfreithiol yn egwyddor bwysig o fewn y system gyfiawnder yng Nghymru. Mae trefniadau yn bodoli i gefnogi achosion drwy gyfrwng y Gymraeg, gan gynnwys cyfieithu, cyfieithu ar y pryd a dogfennaeth ddwyieithog pan fo angen.

Mae Cymru, wrth gwrs, yn wlad ddwyieithog, ond o ofyn beth, yn benodol, y gellid ei wneud, mae hon, rŵan, yn ddadl fyw. Mae hi'n ddadl sy'n mynd i godi mewn gwahanol gynadleddau dros y gaeaf yma. Mae diffygion darparu cyngor yn y Gymraeg wedi bod yn rhy amlwg i bawb, ond hefyd, gyda llaw, mewn sawl man drwy'r Saesneg hefyd. Ond mae'n dwysáu yn achos y Gymraeg, oherwydd, yn amlach na pheidio, dŷn ni'n sôn am gefn gwlad, ac mae cefn gwlad, ar hyn o bryd, wedi cael ei ddisgrifio fel 'anialwch cyfreithiol'.

Felly, mae yna job o waith mawr o'n blaenau ni, ac mae o'n rhan o'm swydd ddisgrifiad i i sicrhau bod mynediad at y gyfraith yn bosibl drwy'r ddwy iaith. Mae'n rhywbeth sydd yn fy meddwl i, ac mae'n rhywbeth y byddaf i'n gweithio arno fo yn y misoedd i ddod.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Of course, access to justice means more than just access to the courts. People must understand their rights, get reliable advice at the right time and participate effectively in legal processes that have an impact upon them. The ability to use the Welsh language in legal cases is an important principle within the justice system in Wales. Arrangements are in place to support Welsh-medium cases, including translation, interpretation and bilingual documentation as necessary.

Wales, of course, is a bilingual nation, but in asking what specifically can be done, this is now a very live issue. It is an issue that will be raised in various conferences over this winter. The deficiencies in the provision of providing advice through the medium of Welsh has been too apparent to all, but also, by the way, through the medium of English in many areas too. But it is particularly bad in the case of the Welsh language, because, more often than not, we are talking about rural areas, and rural areas have been described as 'legal deserts'.

So, there is a great job of work to be done, and it is part of my job description to ensure that access to the law is possible through the medium of both languages. It's something that's at the forefront of my mind, and something that I will be working on in the coming months.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cymorth Cyfreithiol a Mynediad at Gyfiawnder
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Legal Aid and Access to Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: My question has some crossover with the question that Mike Hedges asked earlier.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae yna elfen yn fy nghwestiwn sy'n debyg i elfen yn y cwestiwn a ofynnodd Mike Hedges yn gynharach.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Pa asesiad y mae'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol wedi'i wneud o effaith pwysau ar ddarpariaeth cymorth cyfreithiol ar fynediad at gyfiawnder yng Nghymru? OQ64498
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What assessment has the Counsel General made of the impact of pressures on legal aid provision on access to justice in Wales? OQ64498

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Pressures on legal aid provision in Wales are a very serious concern. Reduced provision means many communities cannot access the legal help they need. Although legal aid is reserved to the UK Government, we will always look for opportunities to bring these problems to the attention of the Ministry of Justice.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae pwysau ar y ddarpariaeth o gymorth cyfreithiol yng Nghymru yn bryder difrifol iawn. Mae llai o ddarpariaeth yn golygu nad yw llawer o gymunedau yn gallu cael mynediad at y cymorth cyfreithiol sydd ei angen arnynt. Er bod cymorth cyfreithiol yn fater a gedwir yn ôl i Lywodraeth y DU, byddwn bob amser yn chwilio am gyfleoedd i ddod â'r problemau hyn i sylw'r Weinyddiaeth Gyfiawnder.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn. We know how vital legal aid is to helping those in need and ensuring that everybody has the right to adequate legal representation. A report by the House of Lords select committee last year concluded that there are people who are both unable to access legal aid and unable to afford to pay for legal services privately. As the Law Society have noted, proposals put forward by the UK Government have not addressed the distinct issues facing the legal sector in Wales and that the part or full devolution of justice, if implemented and funded appropriately, offers significant potential opportunities to the people of Wales. What advice has the Counsel General given the Welsh Government on the adequacy of legal aid in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch yn fawr iawn. Rydym yn gwybod pa mor hanfodol yw cymorth cyfreithiol i helpu'r rhai mewn angen a sicrhau bod gan bawb yr hawl i gynrychiolaeth gyfreithiol ddigonol. Daeth adroddiad gan bwyllgor dethol Tŷ'r Arglwyddi y llynedd i'r casgliad bod yna bobl nad ydynt yn gallu cael mynediad at gymorth cyfreithiol ac nad ydynt yn gallu fforddio talu am wasanaethau cyfreithiol yn breifat. Fel y nododd Cymdeithas y Gyfraith, nid yw cynigion a gyflwynwyd gan Lywodraeth y DU wedi mynd i'r afael â'r materion penodol sy'n wynebu'r sector cyfreithiol yng Nghymru a bod datganoli cyfiawnder rhannol neu lawn, os caiff ei weithredu a'i ariannu'n briodol, yn cynnig cyfleoedd posibl sylweddol i bobl Cymru. Pa gyngor y mae'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol wedi'i roi i Lywodraeth Cymru ar ddigonolrwydd cymorth cyfreithiol yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, it is a matter that the Welsh Government are acutely aware of, and it's partly because of the narrowing of the scope of legal aid alongside tighter eligibility criteria. That's had a very significant impact over many years on the justice system across England and Wales. I'm particularly concerned that people in many parts of Wales are unable to access local legal advice because legal aid fees are no longer sufficient to support sustainable provision. In Wales, reduced provision has contributed to legal advice deserts, leaving some communities without local access to specialist legal help. For example, the Law Society's heat maps show that 82 per cent of the people of Wales have no access to a legal aid-funded local welfare provider, and no less than 88 per cent have no education law provider.

These pressures are acute everywhere, but particularly so in rural, post-industrial and lower income communities, similar to the area that the Member represents. Where alternative sources of advice may be very limited, and without early legal advice, problems can escalate, increasing pressures on devolved services including health, housing and social care. Through the regional advice networks, we are supporting closer collaboration between private law firms and not-for-profit advice providers so that people across Wales can access the advice they need. Although, as I've said before, legal aid is reserved, we will work closely with the Ministry of Justice, the UK Government and legal professions in Wales to ensure Wales's needs are clearly understood and are reflected in the response to these pressures.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, mae'n fater y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ymwybodol iawn ohono, ac mae'n rhannol oherwydd bod cwmpas cymorth cyfreithiol wedi culhau ochr yn ochr â meini prawf cymhwysedd llymach. Mae hynny wedi cael effaith sylweddol iawn dros nifer o flynyddoedd ar y system gyfiawnder ledled Cymru a Lloegr. Rwy'n arbennig o bryderus nad yw pobl mewn sawl rhan o Gymru yn gallu cael cyngor cyfreithiol lleol oherwydd nad yw ffioedd cymorth cyfreithiol bellach yn ddigonol i gefnogi darpariaeth gynaliadwy. Yng Nghymru, mae llai o ddarpariaeth wedi cyfrannu at anialwch cyngor cyfreithiol, gan adael rhai cymunedau heb fynediad lleol at gymorth cyfreithiol arbenigol. Er enghraifft, mae mapiau gwres Cymdeithas y Gyfraith yn dangos nad oes gan 82 y cant o bobl Cymru fynediad at ddarparwr lles lleol a ariennir gan gymorth cyfreithiol, a dim llai na 88 y cant heb ddarparwr cyfraith addysg.

Mae'r pwysau hyn yn ddwys ym mhobman, ond yn enwedig mewn cymunedau gwledig, ôl-ddiwydiannol ac incwm is, yn debyg i'r ardal y mae'r Aelod yn ei chynrychioli. Lle gall ffynonellau cyngor amgen fod yn gyfyngedig iawn, a heb gyngor cyfreithiol cynnar, gall problemau waethygu, gan gynyddu pwysau ar wasanaethau datganoledig gan gynnwys iechyd, tai a gofal cymdeithasol. Trwy'r rhwydweithiau cynghori rhanbarthol, rydym yn cefnogi cydweithrediad agosach rhwng cwmnïau cyfreithiol preifat a darparwyr cyngor nid-er-elw fel y gall pobl ledled Cymru gael mynediad at y cyngor sydd ei angen arnynt. Er, fel y dywedais i o'r blaen, mae cymorth cyfreithiol yn fater a gedwir yn ôl, byddwn yn gweithio'n agos gyda'r Weinyddiaeth Gyfiawnder, Llywodraeth y DU a phroffesiynau cyfreithiol yng Nghymru i sicrhau bod anghenion Cymru yn cael eu deall yn glir ac yn cael eu hadlewyrchu yn yr ymateb i'r pwysau hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Datganoli Cyfiawnder
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Devolution of Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae hwn yn teimlo ychydig bach yn od, gofyn cwestiwn i'r dyn drws nesaf. [Chwerthin.]
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: This feel slightly strange, asking a question to the person next to me. [Laughter.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. Pa gyngor cyfreithiol y mae'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol wedi ei roi i Lywodraeth Cymru ar ddatganoli cyfiawnder? OQ64506
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. What legal advice has the Counsel General provided to the Welsh Government on the devolution of justice? OQ64506

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n falch nad ydych chi'n cwffio efo'r dyn drws nesaf. [Chwerthin.] Mae datganoli pwerau dros blismona a chyfiawnder wedi bod yn argymhelliad mewn cyfres o gomisiynau annibynnol, sy'n dyddio'n ôl i gomisiwn Silk yn 2014. Mi wnaeth y comisiynau hynny, y tri ohonyn nhw, ystyried y goblygiadau cyfreithiol, ymhlith eraill, wrth ddod i'w casgliadau clir. Mi fyddaf i'n gweithio'n agos efo cydweithwyr wrth inni barhau i weithio tuag at hyn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I'm pleased you're not fighting with the man next to you. [Laughter.] The devolution of powers over policing and justice has been recommended in a series of independent commissions, dating back to the Silk commission in 2014. Those commissions, all three of them, considered the legal implications, among others, in arriving at their clear conclusions. I will be working closely with colleagues as we continue to work towards this objective.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Gwnsler. Mae'r angen i ddatganoli cyfiawnder wedi ei ddangos droeon yn y Siambr yma gan y Comisiwn Annibynnol dros Ddyfodol Cyfansoddiadol Cymru a chan Gymdeithas y Cyfreithwyr. Dŷn ni'n gwybod bod y system bresennol yn gwaethygu canlyniadau i bobl Cymru. A dwi wedi cael braw, a bod yn onest, fod 40 y cant o'r cyllid yn dod wrth Lywodraeth Cymru, er nad ydy cyfiawnder wedi'i ddatganoli. Dydy hynny ddim yn gynaliadwy. Felly, ydy'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol yn cytuno efo fi fod datganoli cyfiawnder yn angenrheidiol i wella'r canlyniadau i'r rheini sy'n mynd drwy'r system?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Counsel General. The need to devolve justice has been outlined several times in this Chamber by the Independent Commission on the Constitutional Future of Wales and by the Law Society. We know that the current system deteriorates outcomes for people in Wales. And I've been frightened, truth be told, that 40 per cent of the funding comes from the Welsh Government, although justice has not been devolved. That isn't sustainable. So, does the Counsel General agree that devolution of justice is vital to improve outcomes for those who go through the system?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Does gen i ddim amheuaeth pan wyf yn cytuno efo'r Aelod ar y pwynt yna, ac mae datganoli pwerau dros gyfiawnder a phlismona yn flaenoriaeth i'r Llywodraeth hon. Mae'r achos dros ddatganoli cyfiawnder a phlismona i Gymru, fel yn yr Alban a gogledd yr Iwerddon, yn glir. Dyna gasgliad clir, fel y dywedodd yr Aelod, comisiwn Silk, comisiwn Thomas, ac, yn fwy diweddar, y Comisiwn Annibynnol ar Ddyfodol Cyfansoddiadol Cymru. Mi wnaeth y comisiynau hynny ganfod y byddai datganoli cyfiawnder yn galluogi gwasanaethau mwy atebol, cydgysylltiedig ac effeithiol sy'n cyd-fynd yn well ag anghenion pobl a chymunedau Cymru ac wedi'u hintegreiddio'n agos â chyfrifoldebau datganoledig, fel iechyd, gofal cymdeithasol, addysg a thai. Mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi rhoi gwybod i Brif Weinidog y Deyrnas Unedig fod hyn yn brif flaenoriaeth i Lywodraeth Cymru, a bydd Gweinidogion yn ceisio sicrhau cynnydd, gan gynnwys drwy'r Bil diwygio'r heddlu sydd ar ddod. Mae hwnnw, feddyliwn i, yn gyfrwng ardderchog i gychwyn ar y broses efo datganoli'r heddlu, ac mae o'n gyfle rydym ni fel Llywodraeth yn mynd i afael ynddo fo efo'r ddwy law. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I have no doubt when I agree with the Member on that point, and the devolution of powers over policing and justice is a priority of this Government. The case for the devolution of justice and policing to Wales, as is the case in Scotland and the north of Ireland, is clear. That's a clear conclusion, as the Member said, of the Silk commission, the Thomas commission, and, more recently, the Independent Commission on the Constitutional Future of Wales. Those commissions did find that the devolution of justice would allow for more accountable, co-ordinated and effective services that align better with the needs of the people and communities of Wales and that are integrated more closely with devolved responsibilities, such as health, social care, education and housing. The First Minister has informed the UK Prime Minister that this is a main priority of the Welsh Government, and Ministers will try and secure progress on this, including through the police reform Bill, which is in the pipeline. I would have thought that that is an excellent opportunity to start the process of the devolution of policing, and it is an opportunity that we as a Government will grasp with both hands. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yn olaf, cwestiwn 8—Kiera Marshall.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Finally, question 8—Kiera Marshall.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mynediad at Gyfiawnder i Oroeswyr Treisio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Access to Justice for Rape Survivors

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 8. Sut mae'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol yn hyrwyddo mynediad at gyfiawnder i oroeswyr treisio? OQ64490
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 8. How is the Counsel General promoting access to justice for rape survivors? OQ64490

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
While criminal justice, as the Member knows, is largely reserved, the Welsh Government works with policing, the Crown Prosecution Service, courts and specialist services to improve access to justice for rape survivors. Through the violence against women, domestic abuse and sexual violence agenda, we fund advocacy, counselling and support services, including independent sexual violence advisers, helping survivors access information, support and justice.

I would further say that the Government has invested in specialist support services throughout the piece. More needs to be done, I hasten to add, and we recognise that access to justice is about more than court outcomes. Survivors must be able to access timely support, information and advocacy so they can make informed decisions and recover from the impact of abuse.

And with regard to the university sector, all learners, including university students, should be able to study in safe environments free from violence, abuse, harassment and intimidation. Whilst universities in Wales are autonomous, we expect them to take robust action to ensure safe and supportive teaching environments. Medr's new staff and learner welfare condition has introduced clearer expectations on well-being, safety and protection from harassment and misconduct, including sexual violence. Officials are working closely with Medr and universities and sector partners to strengthen prevention, reporting and support, improve consistency and transparency and support providers to create safe cultures where concerns are taken seriously. I would suggest to the Member that she writes to my colleague the Deputy First Minister on this matter, and I am sure that she will get a full and substantive response on the current steps being taken.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Er bod cyfiawnder troseddol, fel y gŵyr yr Aelod, yn fater a gedwir yn ôl i raddau helaeth, mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn gweithio gyda phlismona, Gwasanaeth Erlyn y Goron, llysoedd a gwasanaethau arbenigol i wella mynediad at gyfiawnder i oroeswyr treisio. Trwy'r agenda trais yn erbyn menywod, cam-drin domestig a thrais rhywiol, rydym yn ariannu gwasanaethau eiriolaeth, cwnsela a chymorth, gan gynnwys cynghorwyr trais rhywiol annibynnol, gan helpu goroeswyr i gael gwybodaeth, cymorth a chyfiawnder.

Byddwn hefyd yn dweud bod y Llywodraeth wedi buddsoddi mewn gwasanaethau cymorth arbenigol ar draws y maes. Mae angen gwneud mwy o bethau, ac rydym yn cydnabod bod mynediad at gyfiawnder yn ymwneud â mwy na chanlyniadau llys. Rhaid i oroeswyr allu cael mynediad at gefnogaeth, gwybodaeth ac eiriolaeth amserol fel y gallant wneud penderfyniadau ar sail gwybodaeth a gwella yn dilyn effaith camdriniaeth.

Ac o ran y sector prifysgol, dylai pob dysgwr, gan gynnwys myfyrwyr prifysgol, allu astudio mewn amgylcheddau diogel heb drais, cam-drin, aflonyddu na bygylu. Er bod prifysgolion yng Nghymru yn ymreolaethol, rydym yn disgwyl iddynt gymryd camau cadarn i sicrhau amgylcheddau addysgu diogel a chefnogol. Mae amodau lles staff a dysgwyr newydd Medr wedi cyflwyno disgwyliadau cliriach ar lesiant, diogelwch ac amddiffyniad rhag aflonyddu a chamymddygiad, gan gynnwys trais rhywiol. Mae swyddogion yn gweithio'n agos gyda Medr a phrifysgolion a phartneriaid sector i gryfhau atal, adrodd a chefnogaeth, gwella cysondeb a thryloywder a chefnogi darparwyr i greu diwylliannau diogel lle mae pryderon yn cael eu cymryd o ddifrif. Byddwn yn awgrymu i'r Aelod ei bod yn ysgrifennu at fy nghyd-Weinidog y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog ar y mater hwn, ac rwy'n siŵr y bydd hi'n cael ymateb llawn a sylweddol ar y camau presennol sy'n cael eu cymryd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for that. I was pleased to see the UK Government announcement that specialist courts to deal with rape and sexual offences are to be introduced across England and Wales, and, hopefully, this begins to tackle the shamefully low prosecution rates of rape in the UK, which has, effectively, been decriminalised.

However, we also must look at prevention, not just justice. I met with a group of young women at Cardiff University, so I was glad to hear you talk about the university sector. They're called Time to Act, and they've been campaigning to eliminate sexual assault and sexual harassment from campuses, alongside supporting survivors. In England, as you'll know, there are currently regulatory consequences for institutions that fail to prevent and to tackle harassment and sexual misconduct. Students in Wales don't have this equivalent protection, so I was wondering if you would, potentially, look at what avenues are available for the Welsh Government to legislate and prevent sexual harassment and violence on university campus.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch am hynna. Roeddwn i'n falch o weld cyhoeddiad Llywodraeth y DU bod llysoedd arbenigol i ymdrin â threisio a throseddau rhywiol yn cael eu cyflwyno ledled Cymru a Lloegr, a gobeithio y bydd hyn yn dechrau mynd i'r afael â'r cyfraddau erlyn cywilyddus o isel o ran trais yn y DU, sydd wedi'i ddad-droseddoli i bob pwrpas.

Fodd bynnag, mae'n rhaid i ni hefyd edrych ar atal, nid cyfiawnder yn unig. Fe wnes i gyfarfod â grŵp o ferched ifanc ym Mhrifysgol Caerdydd, felly roeddwn i'n falch o'ch clywed chi'n siarad am y sector prifysgolion. Maen nhw'n cael eu galw'n Amser i Weithredu, ac maen nhw wedi bod yn ymgyrchu i ddileu ymosodiadau rhywiol ac aflonyddu rhywiol o gampysau, ochr yn ochr â chefnogi goroeswyr. Yn Lloegr, fel y gwyddoch chi, mae canlyniadau rheoleiddiol ar hyn o bryd i sefydliadau sy'n methu ag atal aflonyddu a chamymddwyn rhywiol. Nid oes gan fyfyrwyr yng Nghymru yr amddiffyniad cyfatebol hwn, felly meddwl oeddwn i tybed a fyddech chi, o bosibl, yn edrych ar ba lwybrau sydd ar gael i Lywodraeth Cymru ddeddfu ac atal aflonyddu rhywiol a thrais ar gampws prifysgolion.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, I hear what the Member says, and I appreciate the work that she's doing in the area. It's certainly very important, and I can speak from my own personal knowledge of work I do at the university in Aberystwyth. It's high on the agenda at that university and, I have no doubt, in every university in Wales, and so it should be. So, things are moving, albeit slower than all of us would want, but they are moving in the right direction. And our job, it seems to me, is to pressurise and ensure that the continued improvement in this area is to be seen by all.

If I add one final thing, on the issue of rape generally—horrific as it is—there has been an announcement that there will be, from 1 October, designated courts dealing with rape. That will lessen the backlog, and that will include specialists available to help and back up individuals but also things like separate entrances and waiting rooms, basic protections of that kind. This is something, I believe, to be welcomed. I would also say, on a more positive note, that the backlogs in Wales are considerably better than they are elsewhere in the UK, and we need to maintain that, but this, again, will assist, I believe.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Wel, rwy'n clywed beth mae'r Aelod yn ei ddweud, ac rwy'n gwerthfawrogi'r gwaith y mae hi'n ei wneud yn yr ardal. Mae'n sicr yn bwysig iawn, a gallaf siarad o fy ngwybodaeth bersonol fy hun o'r gwaith rwy'n ei wneud yn y brifysgol yn Aberystwyth. Mae'n uchel ar yr agenda yn y brifysgol honno a, does gen i ddim amheuaeth, ym mhob prifysgol yng Nghymru, ac felly dylai fod. Felly, mae pethau'n symud, er yn arafach nag y byddai pob un ohonom yn dymuno, ond maen nhw'n symud i'r cyfeiriad cywir. A'n gwaith ni, mae'n ymddangos i mi, yw pwyso a sicrhau bod y gwelliant parhaus yn y maes hwn i'w weld gan bawb.

Os ychwanegaf un peth yn olaf, ar y mater o dreisio yn gyffredinol—ofnadwy fel yw e'—bu cyhoeddiad y bydd yna lysoedd penodedig sy'n ymdrin â threisio o 1 Hydref. Bydd hynny'n lleihau'r ôl-groniad, a bydd hynny'n cynnwys arbenigwyr sydd ar gael i helpu a chefnogi unigolion ond hefyd pethau fel mynedfeydd ac ystafelloedd aros ar wahân, amddiffyniadau sylfaenol o'r math hwnnw. Mae hyn yn rhywbeth i'w groesawu, rwy'n credu. Byddwn hefyd yn dweud, ar nodyn mwy cadarnhaol, bod yr ôl-groniadau yng Nghymru yn sylweddol well nag y maen nhw mewn mannau eraill yn y DU, ac mae angen i ni gynnal hynny, ond bydd hyn, unwaith eto, yn helpu, rwy'n credu.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Daeth y Dirprwy Lywydd (Kerry Ferguson) i’r Gadair.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Deputy Presiding Officer (Kerry Ferguson) took the Chair.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Gwnsler Cyffredinol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Counsel General.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Symudwn ymlaen i eitem 3, datganiad a chyhoeddiad busnes. Galwaf ar y Trefnydd, Heledd Fychan.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We'll move now to item 3, the business statement and announcement. I call on the Trefnydd, Heledd Fychan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Trefnydd, Chief Whip and Cabinet Minister for Culture and Sport
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Trefnydd, Prif Chwip a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Ddiwylliant a Chwaraeon
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Mae dau ddatganiad llafar wedi eu hychwanegu at yr agenda heddiw, sef 'Uchelgais Newydd i Gymru', y rhaglen lywodraethu, a hefyd fframwaith moesegol amddiffyn Cymru. Mae busnes drafft y tair wythnos nesaf wedi'i nodi yn y datganiad busnes sydd ar gael i'r holl Aelodau'n electronig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Dirprwy Lywydd. Two oral statements have been added to today's agenda, namely 'New Ambition for Wales', the programme for government, and also the Welsh defence ethical framework. Draft Plenary business for the next three weeks is shown on the business statement, which is available to all Members electronically.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Trefnydd, I'd be grateful if I could have a statement on local train overcrowding. Transport for Wales's service for Bridgend to Rhymney is currently the third most overcrowded service between peak hours in the UK. That service now is affecting commuters, affecting their transport into work. It's not very easy for elderly people to get a seat, and it's something that my constituents are raising with me quite often. So, I'd be grateful, Trefnydd, if the Minister sitting here could come forward with something so that we can address the overcrowding on Welsh trains. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Drefnydd, byddwn yn ddiolchgar pe bawn i'n gallu cael datganiad ar orlenwi trenau lleol. Gwasanaeth Trafnidiaeth Cymru ar gyfer Pen-y-bont ar Ogwr i Rymni ar hyn o bryd yw'r trydydd gwasanaeth gwaethaf o ran gorlenwi rhwng oriau brig yn y DU. Mae'r gwasanaeth hwnnw nawr yn effeithio ar gymudwyr, gan effeithio ar eu cludiant i'r gwaith. Nid yw'n hawdd iawn i bobl oedrannus gael sedd, ac mae'n rhywbeth y mae fy etholwyr yn ei godi gyda mi yn eithaf aml. Felly, byddwn yn ddiolchgar, Drefnydd, pe bai'r Gweinidog sy'n eistedd yma yn gallu cyflwyno rhywbeth er mwyn i ni allu mynd i'r afael â'r gorlenwi ar drenau Cymru. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater yna. Yn lwcus iawn, mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth yma, ac mi fydd o'n ysgrifennu atoch chi. Byddwn i'n eich annog chi hefyd i rannu unrhyw wybodaeth—annog unrhyw Aelod yma i wastad rhannu gwybodaeth lle mae gwasanaeth angen sylw pellach gennym ni fel Llywodraeth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for raising that matter. Fortunately, the Deputy Minister for Transport is here, and he'll be writing to you. I would encourage you also to share any information that you have, and encourage any Member here to always share information where services need further attention from us as a Government.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Last week, I was glad to be joined by my Welsh Labour colleague Ken Skates at Llanwern steelworks in my constituency. Llanwern is strategically important to Wales and the whole of the UK, and it must not be lost in the wider debate on the steel industry. Steel making is in Newport's DNA, and it should have a proud future, but the workers that I spoke to last week were concerned about that future and that it's under threat from cheap galvanised steel imports. The Welsh Government must work with the UK Government to protect steel jobs in Wales and engage with the unions to support the workforce. So, Trefnydd, can we have a statement from the Welsh Government confirming that you will do everything in your power to ensure a sustainable future for the steel industry in Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yr wythnos diwethaf, roeddwn i'n falch o ymuno â fy nghyd-Aelod Llafur Cymru, Ken Skates, yng ngwaith dur Llanwern yn fy etholaeth. Mae Llanwern yn strategol bwysig i Gymru a'r DU gyfan, ac ni ddylid ei golli yn y ddadl ehangach ar y diwydiant dur. Mae gwneud dur yn rhan o DNA Casnewydd, a dylai fod ganddo ddyfodol balch, ond roedd y gweithwyr y siaradais â nhw yr wythnos diwethaf yn pryderu am y dyfodol hwnnw a'i fod dan fygythiad gan fewnforion dur galfanedig rhad. Rhaid i Lywodraeth Cymru weithio gyda Llywodraeth y DU i ddiogelu swyddi dur yng Nghymru ac ymgysylltu â'r undebau i gefnogi'r gweithlu. Felly, Drefnydd, a allwn ni gael datganiad gan Lywodraeth Cymru yn cadarnhau y byddwch yn gwneud popeth o fewn eich gallu i sicrhau dyfodol cynaliadwy i'r diwydiant dur yng Nghymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Wel, diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater sydd, wrth gwrs, o bwys. Mi fyddwch chi'n ymwybodol iawn, dwi'n siŵr, fod y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog, pan wnaeth hi gyfarfod gyda Phrif Weinidog newydd y Deyrnas Unedig, Andy Burnham, dros yr haf, wedi mynegi pryderon y Llywodraeth newydd hon ynglŷn â'r diffyg a wnaed gan y Llywodraeth Lafur o ran peidio â sicrhau dyfodol iawn i ddur yng Nghymru, a diystyru hefyd y diwydiant dur yma. Yn sicr, mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni yma yn y Siambr ac wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi'n dweud, ac, fel bob amser, rydyn ni'n barod iawn i drafod gydag Aelodau lleol lle mae angen hynny. Ond, yn ddiamwys, mi fedraf i ddweud ein bod ni'n gweld dyfodol i'r diwydiant dur, eisiau gweithio gyda'r rheini sy'n pryderu am hyn, ac, wrth gwrs, yn gwneud yr achos drwy'r adeg i Lywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig roi sylw digonol i'r diwydiant dur yma yng Nghymru.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Well, I thank the Member for raising an issue that is, of course, hugely important. You will be highly aware, I'm sure, that the Deputy First Minister, when she met with the new UK Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, over the summer, expressed this new Government's concerns about the lack of action taken by the Labour Government in not securing a future for steel in Wales and ignoring the steel industry here. Certainly, the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy is in the Chamber and has heard what you had to say, and, as always, we are more than willing to have discussions with local Members where necessary. But, unambiguously, I can say that we do see a future for the steel industry, and we do want to work with those who are concerned about this issue, and, of course, are constantly making the case at a UK level for the UK Government to give sufficient attention to the steel industry here in Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Trefnydd, continuing on the theme of trains, I'd like to request a statement from the Deputy Minister for Transport on the delivery of rail services in west Wales. I'm regularly contacted by constituents from across Ceredigion Penfro who express concerns about the frequency, reliability and overall availability of rail services in the region. They want to see more regular and dependable train services operating across all rail lines in west Wales throughout the week, because for too long west Wales has not received the level of attention it deserves when it comes to rail connectivity and service delivery, and I believe there should be a review of rail provision in the region to assess whether current services are meeting the needs of local communities, and indeed to identify where improvements are required. Therefore, I'd be grateful if the Welsh Government could provide a statement outlining what steps it intends to take to improve the delivery, frequency and reliability of rail services in west Wales so that we can understand how it plans to address the long-standing concerns of passengers in Ceredigion Penfro.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Drefnydd, gan barhau ar y thema trenau, hoffwn ofyn am ddatganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth ar ddarparu gwasanaethau rheilffyrdd yn y gorllewin. Mae etholwyr o bob rhan o Geredigion Penfro yn cysylltu â mi yn rheolaidd yn mynegi pryderon am amlder, dibynadwyedd ac argaeledd cyffredinol gwasanaethau rheilffyrdd yn y rhanbarth. Maent eisiau gweld gwasanaethau trenau mwy rheolaidd a dibynadwy yn gweithredu ar draws pob rheilffordd yn y gorllewin drwy gydol yr wythnos, oherwydd ers gormod o amser nid yw'r gorllewin wedi derbyn y lefel o sylw y mae'n ei haeddu o ran cysylltedd rheilffyrdd a darparu gwasanaethau, ac rwy'n credu y dylid adolygu darpariaeth rheilffyrdd yn y rhanbarth i asesu a yw'r gwasanaethau presennol yn diwallu anghenion cymunedau lleol, ac yn wir i nodi lle mae angen gwelliannau. Felly, byddwn yn ddiolchgar pe gallai Llywodraeth Cymru ddarparu datganiad yn amlinellu pa gamau y mae'n bwriadu eu cymryd i wella darpariaeth, amlder a dibynadwyedd gwasanaethau rheilffyrdd yn y gorllewin fel y gallwn ddeall sut mae'n bwriadu mynd i'r afael â phryderon hirsefydlog teithwyr yng Ngheredigion Penfro.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r materion hyn. Ddirprwy Lywydd, wrth gwrs, mi fydd pob Aelod wedi clywed datganiadau blaenorol, gan gynnwys datganiadau blaenoriaeth, gan gynnwys gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth. Mi ydym ni hefyd yn rhannu'r weledigaeth honno o ran sicrhau bod trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus ar gael ym mhob rhan o Gymru, ac mae'r weledigaeth honno yn cynnwys y gwaith sy'n mynd rhagddo er mwyn edrych ar y ddarpariaeth honno. Wrth i'r gwaith hwnnw barhau, mi fydd y Dirprwy Weinidog yn rhoi diweddariadau i'r Senedd hon, ac, wrth gwrs, yn barod iawn i ymgysylltu efo Aelodau, fydd eisiau gwneud yr achos dros eu hetholaethau nhw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for raising those issues. Dirprwy Lywydd, of course, every Member will have heard previous statements, including statements on priorities, including those from the Deputy Minister for Transport. We too share that vision in terms of ensuring that public transport is available in every part of Wales, and that vision includes the work in train to look at that provision. As that work continues, the Deputy Minister will be providing updates to the Senedd and will, of course, be very willing to engage with Members, who will want to make the case for their constituencies.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Trefnydd, we just heard questions to the Counsel General about the legal position surrounding health service reconfiguration. Last week, Powys Teaching Health Board decided to press ahead with consultation on proposals that could remove in-patient beds from a number of our community hospitals. There is considerable concern across Powys and many of us are far from convinced that the voices of local people or their elected representatives are being heard. Will you therefore arrange for an urgent statement from the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care setting out the Government's position, what discussions he has had with the health board, and, crucially, whether he is prepared to intervene?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Drefnydd, rydym newydd glywed cwestiynau i'r Cwnsler Cyffredinol am y sefyllfa gyfreithiol ynglŷn ag ad-drefnu'r gwasanaeth iechyd. Yr wythnos diwethaf, penderfynodd Bwrdd Iechyd Addysgu Powys fwrw ymlaen ag ymgynghoriad ar gynigion a allai gael gwared ar welyau cleifion mewnol o nifer o'n hysbytai cymunedol. Mae cryn bryder ar draws Powys ac mae llawer ohonom ymhell o fod yn argyhoeddedig bod lleisiau pobl leol neu eu cynrychiolwyr etholedig yn cael eu clywed. Felly, a wnewch chi drefnu datganiad brys gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Iechyd a Gofal yn nodi safbwynt y Llywodraeth, pa drafodaethau y mae wedi'u cael gyda'r bwrdd iechyd, ac, yn hollbwysig, a yw'n barod i ymyrryd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Yn amlwg, mae hwn yn fater a godwyd wythnos diwethaf hefyd, ac, fel gwnes i amlinellu'r adeg honno, ymgymryd gyda'r ymgysylltiad cychwynnol y mae'r bwrdd iechyd. Does dim penderfyniadau wedi'u gwneud. A'r hyn byddwn i'n gofyn i bob Aelod sydd gydag etholwyr wedi'u heffeithio gan y posibiliadau yn yr ymgynghoriad hwn wneud yw ymwneud â'r ymgynghoriad, ac annog eraill, ac i fod yn glir nad yw'r bwrdd iechyd wedi gwneud unrhyw benderfyniad ar ei gynllun gwasanaethau clinigol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for raising this issue. Clearly, it's an issue that was raised last week as well, and, as I outlined at that time, dealing with that initial engagement, that's what the health board is doing. No decisions have been made. And what I would ask every Member who has constituents who have been affected by the possibilities raised in this consultation to do is to become involved in the consultation, and to encourage others to engage, and to be clear that the health board has yet to make any decision on its clinical services plan.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Trefnydd, we know that many people were preparing for surgery when they heard, by word of mouth or by social media, that their surgeries under the Welsh Gender Service had been paused during the Senedd's summer recess. One of my constituents was actually in hospital for surgery when they were told that their operation was cancelled, with no further support provided since then. You'll know that I've written, with other Members, to the NHS Wales Joint Commissioning Committee, who were responsible for this decision, asking about the evidence that informed this decision, the lack of communication with patients, and how patients' voices were not heard.

I know that this decision was made by a medical body, rather than a political one, but I'd like to request a statement outlining how the Government will ensure that this community will be listened to, how their concerns will be central to any further decisions made about trans healthcare, and how they will be supported. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Drefnydd, gwyddom fod llawer o bobl wrth baratoi ar gyfer llawdriniaeth wedi clywed, ar lafar neu ar y cyfryngau cymdeithasol, bod eu llawdriniaethau o dan Wasanaeth Rhywedd Cymru wedi cael eu gohirio yn ystod toriad haf y Senedd. Roedd un o'm hetholwyr mewn gwirionedd yn yr ysbyty ar gyfer llawdriniaeth pan gafodd wybod bod y llawdriniaeth wedi'i chanslo, heb unrhyw gymorth pellach ers hynny. Byddwch yn gwybod fy mod wedi ysgrifennu, gydag Aelodau eraill, at Gyd-bwyllgor Comisiynu GIG Cymru, a oedd yn gyfrifol am y penderfyniad hwn, yn gofyn am y dystiolaeth a lywiodd y penderfyniad hwn, y diffyg cyfathrebu â chleifion, a pham nad oedd lleisiau cleifion yn cael eu clywed.

Rwy'n gwybod bod y penderfyniad hwn wedi'i wneud gan gorff meddygol, yn hytrach nag un gwleidyddol, ond hoffwn ofyn am ddatganiad yn amlinellu sut y bydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau y bydd y gymuned hon yn cael gwrandawiad, sut y bydd eu pryderon yn ganolog i unrhyw benderfyniadau pellach a wneir am ofal iechyd traws, a sut y byddant yn cael eu cefnogi. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater eithriadol o bwysig. Dwi'n siŵr bod nifer ohonom ni wedi clywed gan ffrindiau, gan etholwyr, sydd wedi'u heffeithio, a chlywed am yr effaith dirdynnol mae hyn wedi'i gael.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for raising such an important matter. I'm sure that many of us will have heard from friends, from constituents, who've been impacted, and have heard about the very powerful impact that this has had.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Please be assured that this Government stands with the trans community and will continue to protect and promote trans rights in line with our commitment to a welcoming and inclusive Wales. Members will be aware that a debate is tabled tomorrow by Anthony Slaughter. There will be an opportunity then to ask questions of the Cabinet Minister for health, and he will also be responding in full then.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gallwch fod yn sicr bod y Llywodraeth hon yn sefyll gyda'r gymuned draws a bydd yn parhau i amddiffyn a hyrwyddo hawliau traws yn unol â'n hymrwymiad i Gymru groesawgar a chynhwysol. Bydd yr Aelodau yn ymwybodol bod dadl yn cael ei chyflwyno yfory gan Anthony Slaughter. Bydd cyfle wedyn i ofyn cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros iechyd, a bydd hefyd yn ymateb yn llawn bryd hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
To be fair, you, like me, Trefnydd, have been an advocate for ensuring children and young people get to school safely and happy, and I'm sure that you'll agree with me that the first priority of governments at every level should be to protect children's and young people's well-being and not leave them anxious and worried. This policy of getting as many pupils as possible onto public buses rather than school buses is majorly flawed. It may work in urban areas, but it certainly doesn't work in rural areas, where routes like the Usk to Monmouth are long and winding, with national speed limit roads. Children packed in like sardines, standing for 40 minutes, is just not acceptable, and I'm sure you'll agree with that. But, sadly, this was the case in Monmouthshire on the first day of term, with multiple parents and pupils contacting me, with issues—similar issues, actually—flagged all over Monmouthshire and Torfaen. How can we possibly be in a situation where children have to have their own seat and even wear a seat belt for school trips, but this is acceptable?

Cost-cutting exercises by councils—and we all know they're strapped for cash—should never come at the expense of children's safety and well-being. Trefnydd, on that note, I would like to request an urgent statement from the Cabinet Minister responsible as to when this policy will be reviewed to ensure all children and young people get to school safely, on time and ready to learn. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I fod yn deg, rydych chi, fel fi, Drefnydd, wedi bod yn eiriolwr dros sicrhau bod plant a phobl ifanc yn cyrraedd yr ysgol yn ddiogel ac yn hapus, ac rwy'n siŵr y byddwch chi'n cytuno â mi y dylai blaenoriaeth gyntaf llywodraethau ar bob lefel fod i amddiffyn llesiant plant a phobl ifanc a pheidio â'u gadael yn poeni ac yn bryderus. Mae'r polisi hwn o gael cymaint o ddisgyblion â phosibl ar fysiau cyhoeddus yn hytrach na bysiau ysgol yn ddiffygiol iawn. Efallai y bydd yn gweithio mewn ardaloedd trefol, ond yn sicr nid yw'n gweithio mewn ardaloedd gwledig, lle mae llwybrau fel yr un o Frynbuga i Fynwy yn hir ac yn droellog, gyda ffyrdd â therfyn cyflymder cenedlaethol. Nid yw gwasgu plant i mewn fel sardîns i sefyll am 40 munud, yn dderbyniol, ac rwy'n siŵr y byddwch chi'n cytuno â hynny. Ond, yn anffodus, roedd hyn yn wir yn sir Fynwy ar ddiwrnod cyntaf y tymor, gyda nifer o rieni a disgyblion yn cysylltu â mi, gyda materion—materion tebyg, mewn gwirionedd—wedi'u nodi ledled sir Fynwy a Thorfaen. Sut allwn ni fod mewn sefyllfa lle mae plant yn gorfod bod a sedd eu hunain a hyd yn oed gwisgo gwregys diogelwch ar deithiau ysgol, ond bod hyn yn dderbyniol?

Ni ddylai ymarferion torri costau gan gynghorau—ac rydym i gyd yn gwybod eu bod yn brin o arian—byth ddod ar draul diogelwch a llesiant plant. Drefnydd, ar y nodyn hwnnw, hoffwn ofyn am ddatganiad brys gan y Gweinidog Cabinet sy'n gyfrifol am benderfynu pryd y bydd y polisi hwn yn cael ei adolygu i sicrhau bod pob plentyn a pherson ifanc yn cyrraedd yr ysgol yn ddiogel, ar amser ac yn barod i ddysgu. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwn. Mae o'n fater sydd yn fyw iawn yn ein trafodaethau ni fel Llywodraeth. Mae'n fater traws-bortffolio. Dwi'n falch bod y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Drafnidiaeth yma. Rydyn ni wedi cael trafodaethau hyd yn oed yr wythnos yma, fel Gweinidogion, yn edrych ar yr effaith o ran rhwystro pobl rhag cael mynediad at addysg, sydd yn effeithio ar faint o arian sydd gan deuluoedd, ac ati. Mae hwn yn fater byw. Mae'r gwaith yn mynd rhagddo. Wrth fod yna ddiweddariadau, mi fydd y Dirprwy Weinidog, wrth gwrs, yn ymgysylltu efo Aelodau o'r Senedd sydd yn poeni am y mater hwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for raising this issue. It is a very live issue as part of our discussions as a Government. It's a cross-portfolio issue. I'm pleased that the Deputy Minister for Transport is here. We have had discussions even this week, as Ministers, looking at the impacts in terms of barriers to people's access to education, and that does affect how much money families have too. This is a very live issue. The work is ongoing. As there are updates, the Deputy Minister will, of course, engage with Members of the Senedd who are concerned about this issue.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Trefnydd, can I call for a statement from the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy on access to banking services in Wales? I appreciate that banking is not a devolved matter, but banking services really do matter to people across the country, particularly in communities that don't have access to a bank. I've been blessed in my own constituency to have two banking hubs, which are serving the communities of Abergele and Prestatyn, but there are other communities, places like Llangollen that lost its last bank a couple of years ago, that don't have a bank present. At the moment, the FCA, the Financial Conduct Authority, simply do assessments of access to cash, rather than access to banking services.

Shortly after the election, the UK Government did announce a review of access to banking services. That consultation finished over the summer. I wonder whether the Welsh Government has made a submission to that about the particular circumstances in Wales, particularly given our rurality, to make sure that people have access to these vital services. If it hasn't, is there any way we can work together to make sure that we make a call and a demand for legislation in this area, to ensure that banking services are available?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Drefnydd, a gaf i alw am ddatganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni ar fynediad at wasanaethau bancio yng Nghymru? Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi nad yw bancio yn fater datganoledig, ond mae gwasanaethau bancio yn bwysig i bobl ledled y wlad, yn enwedig mewn cymunedau nad oes ganddyn nhw fynediad at fanc. Rydw i'n ffodus iawn i fod â dwy ganolfan fancio yn fy etholaeth i sy'n gwasanaethu cymunedau Abergele a Phrestatyn, ond mae yna gymunedau eraill, trefi fel Llangollen a gollodd ei banc olaf ychydig flynyddoedd yn ôl, nad oes ganddyn nhw fanc o gwbl. Ar hyn o bryd, mae'r Awdurdod Ymddygiad Ariannol, y FCA, yn gwneud asesiadau o fynediad at arian parod, yn hytrach na mynediad at wasanaethau bancio.

Yn fuan ar ôl yr etholiad, cyhoeddodd Llywodraeth y DU adolygiad o fynediad at wasanaethau bancio. Daeth yr ymgynghoriad hwnnw i ben dros yr haf. Tybed a yw Llywodraeth Cymru wedi gwneud cais i hwnnw ynghylch yr amgylchiadau arbennig yng Nghymru, yn enwedig o ystyried ein gwledigrwydd, i wneud yn siŵr bod pobl yn cael mynediad at y gwasanaethau hanfodol hyn. Os nad yw wedi gwneud hynny, a oes unrhyw ffordd y gallwn weithio gyda'n gilydd i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn gwneud galwad a galw am ddeddfwriaeth yn y maes hwn, i sicrhau bod gwasanaethau bancio ar gael?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Dwi'n siŵr nad chi yw'r unig un a dwi'n gwybod ein bod ni wedi bod yn rhan o ymgyrchoedd pan oedd banciau mewn perygl, ac wedi gweld yr effaith pan maen nhw wedi diflannu, a beth oedd effaith hynny wedyn ar rai o'r trigolion mwyaf bregus neu'r rhai hynaf yn y gymdeithas. Mae hwn hefyd yn fater y mae'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb wedi bod yn ei godi, oherwydd mae hwn yn fater o gyfiawnder cymdeithasol: sicrhau'r gwasanaethau hynny. Dwi'n falch iawn bod y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni wedi clywed yr hyn rydych chi wedi ei ddweud rŵan. Fe wnawn ni ystyried hynny, a dwi'n siŵr y bydd y Gweinidog yn ymgysylltu â chi.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. I'm sure that you're not the only one and I know that we've been part of campaigns in the past when banks have been at risk, and have seen the impact when they have gone from those places, and what impact that has then had on some of the most vulnerable residents or the oldest people in that society. This is also an issue that the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality has been raising, because this is a social justice issue: ensuring those services. I am very pleased that the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy heard what you said just then. We will consider that, and I'm sure that the Minister will engage with you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yn sgil effeithiau difrifol storm Bert ym mis Tachwedd 2024, pan agorodd canolfan gymunedol Aberfan a chanolfan hamdden Merthyr Tudful eu drysau i gefnogi trigolion a oedd wedi gorfod gwacáu yn ystod y llifogydd dinistriol, mae llawer o etholwyr ar draws Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr yn bryderus ynghylch risg gynyddol llifogydd dros y gaeaf sydd i ddod. Mae'r Afon Taf a'r Afon Cynon yn peri bygythiad sylweddol i gartrefi, busnesau ac isadeiledd cymunedol. O ystyried y pryderon hyn, hoffwn ofyn am ddatganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd yn amlinellu sut mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cryfhau parodrwydd Cymru ar gyfer llifogydd dros gyfnod y gaeaf. Dylai hyn gynnwys manylion am gynllunio gwydnwch presennol, cefnogaeth ar lefel gymunedol, parodrwydd seilwaith, ac unrhyw fesurau ychwanegol sy'n cael eu cymryd i ddiogelu ardaloedd sydd mewn perygl yn ein rhanbarth. Gan ystyried maint y digwyddiadau diweddar, mae eglurder a sicrwydd i drigolion yn hanfodol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Given the significant impact of storm Bert in November 2024, when the community centre in Aberfan and the leisure centre in Merthyr Tydfil opened their doors to support residents who had had to evacuate because of the destructive floods, many constituents across Pontypridd Cynon Merthyr are very concerned about the increasing risk of flooding over the coming winter. The Taff and Cynon rivers pose a serious threat to homes, businesses and community infrastructure. Given these concerns, I would like to ask for a statement from the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability outlining how the Welsh Government is strengthening Wales's preparedness for floods over the winter months. This should include details about current resilience planning, support at a community level, the readiness of infrastructure, and any additional measures being taken in order to safeguard areas that are at risk in our region. Given the scale of recent events, clarity and assurance for residents is crucial.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch i'r Aelod am godi mater a godwyd hefyd yn ystod cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog heddiw. Mi ddylwn i ddatgan fy mod i'n rhannu etholaeth â chi ac wedi bod yn eiriolwr cryf dros weithredu o ran cefnogi cymunedau sydd efo'r risg parhaus hwn. Rwyf wedi gweld yr effaith y mae hyn yn ei gael, nid yn unig pan fydd llifogydd yn digwydd, ond unrhyw dro pan fydd hi'n bwrw glaw yn drwm, a'r ofn parhaus sydd yna fod pobl yn mynd i ddioddef llifogydd a'r effaith y bydd hynny'n ei gael ar eu bywydau dydd i ddydd nhw.

Mi fydd y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd yn gwneud datganiad yn yr wythnosau nesaf yma ynglŷn â pharatoi at y gaeaf. Ac yn sicr, yr hyn rydyn ni wedi ei weld rŵan, gyda'r tywydd mwyaf eithafol, yw bod yn rhaid inni fod yn gwneud y gwaith hwn drwy gydol y flwyddyn, oherwydd un o'r heriau rydyn ni wedi eu gweld ydy bod rhai o'r stormydd yn dod yn gynt neu'n hwyrach yn y flwyddyn, ac wedyn bod angen y parodrwydd hwnnw. Wedyn, yn sicr, mi fydd y datganiad hwnnw yn yr wythnosau nesaf. A dwi'n credu, o'r hyn ddywedodd y Prif Weinidog yn gynharach heddiw, fod y gwaith medrwn ni ei wneud fel pob Aelod o'r Senedd, i fod yn cefnogi cymunedau o ran y gwydnwch hwnnw ac i fod yn eirioli drostyn nhw, yn eithriadol o bwysig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I thank the Member for raising that issue, and it was spoken about earlier today in First Minister's questions. I should declare that I share a constituency with you and I have been a strong advocate of taking action in terms of supporting communities who face this continuing risk. I've seen the impact that this has, not just when the floods happen, but any time it rains heavily, and that continuing fear that people have that they are going to suffer further flooding and the impact that that will have on their day-to-day lives.

The Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability will be making a statement in these next weeks about preparing for the winter. And certainly, what we have seen now, with this extreme weather, is that we have to do this work throughout the year, because one of the challenges that we have seen is that some of the storms happen earlier or later in the year, and that then that preparedness is needed. Certainly, that statement will be coming in the next few weeks. And I think, from what the First Minister said earlier today, that the work that we can do as each Member of the Senedd, in terms of supporting communities with that resilience and advocating for them, is incredibly important.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm raising this as an MS for Carmarthenshire, but I need to declare that I am also the Chair of the Local Government, Housing and Planning Committee. Trefnydd, can I ask for a statement from the Welsh Government on nutrient neutrality and its impact on housing delivery in west Wales?

Following Natural Resources Wales's marine assessment and subsequent planning advice to councils last year, social and affordable housing schemes across Carmarthenshire and Pembrokeshire face significant delays. I have been contacted by one contractor who builds almost exclusively for affordable social housing, and he has an order book of £30 million-worth of secured work that has now stalled. Its turnover has halved, it supports approximately 80 staff and 320 subcontractors, from groundworkers and bricklayers through to merchants, plant hire firms and delivery drivers. Everyone accepts in this Chamber the need to protect our rivers and estuaries, but nutrient pollution comes from a wide range of sources across whole catchment areas. These delays are affecting both families waiting for homes and the firms ready to build them.

So, can we have a statement on what has replaced the marine nitrates development taskforce, what further mitigation measures are being considered, and when these housing schemes can realistically move forward? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n codi hwn fel AS dros Sir Gaerfyrddin, ond mae angen i mi ddatgan fy mod hefyd yn Gadeirydd y Pwyllgor Llywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio. Drefnydd, a gaf i ofyn am ddatganiad gan Lywodraeth Cymru ar niwtraliaeth maethynnau a'i heffaith ar y ddarpariaeth o dai yn y gorllewin?

Yn dilyn asesiad morol Cyfoeth Naturiol Cymru a'r cyngor cynllunio dilynol i gynghorau y llynedd, mae cynlluniau tai cymdeithasol a fforddiadwy ar draws sir Gaerfyrddin a sir Benfro yn wynebu oedi sylweddol. Mae un contractwr wedi cysylltu â mi sy'n adeiladu bron yn gyfan gwbl ar gyfer tai cymdeithasol fforddiadwy, ac mae ganddo lyfr archebion o werth £30 miliwn o waith wedi'i sicrhau sydd bellach wedi'i oedi. Mae ei drosiant wedi haneru, mae'n cefnogi tua 80 o staff a 320 o isgontractwyr, o weithwyr tir a bricwyr i fasnachwyr, cwmnïau llogi peiriannau a gyrwyr danfon nwyddau. Mae pawb yn derbyn yn y Siambr hon bod angen amddiffyn ein hafonydd a'n aberoedd, ond mae llygredd maethynnau yn dod o ystod eang o ffynonellau ar draws dalgylchoedd cyfan. Mae'r oedi hwn yn effeithio ar deuluoedd sy'n aros am gartrefi ac ar gwmnïau sy'n barod i'w hadeiladu.

Felly, a allwn ni gael datganiad ar yr hyn sydd wedi disodli'r tasglu datblygu nitradau morol, pa fesurau lliniaru pellach sy'n cael eu hystyried, a phryd y gall y cynlluniau tai hyn symud ymlaen yn realistig? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch i'r Aelod am godi'r mater hwnnw. Mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio wedi clywed eich galwadau chi a'r hyn rydych chi wedi ei godi. Ac mi fyddaf i'n trafod efo hi y ffordd fwyaf priodol i fod yn rhoi'r ymateb hwnnw, boed yn ddatganiad neu drwy lythyr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I thank the Member for raising that issue. The Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning will have heard your calls and the issues that you've raised. And I will discuss with her the most appropriate way of responding to those, be that a statement or by correspondence.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to request two statements, one from the Cabinet Minister for Social Justice and Equality on how they are working with councils and the UK Government to prevent rogue builders and their ability to phoenix, which is starting up again after you've left people with incomplete builds and in lots of debt, and also on identity fraud, quishing and other scams that are taking place in north Wales, where it has emerged that there is a higher degree of scams now affecting our older constituents. I'm working with trading standards and the BBC, as north Wales does seem to be this key place where it's happening. The Federation of Master Builders Cymru have called on the Welsh Government to work alongside the UK Government to produce a mandatory licensing scheme for building companies. Will your Government support that?

And a second one from the Cabinet Minister for Health and Care on the parking provision at Ysbyty Gwynedd—and Ysbyty Glan Clwyd is just as bad. Patients and visitors are continuously struggling to find appropriate parking, despite driving around continuously for almost an hour sometimes, and sometimes they will actually accept that they're going to get a fine because otherwise they would miss that appointment. This has been going on for too long now, so we need something from the health Minister to say that he's accepting that this isn't adequate. Please help.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Hoffwn ofyn am ddau ddatganiad, un gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb ar sut maen nhw'n gweithio gyda chynghorau a Llywodraeth y DU i atal adeiladwyr twyllodrus a'u gallu i godi fel ffenics, sef dechrau eto ar ôl i chi adael pobl gydag adeiladau anghyflawn ac mewn dyled fawr, a hefyd ar dwyll hunaniaeth, QR-rwydo a sgamiau eraill sy'n digwydd yn y gogledd, lle mae wedi dod i'r amlwg bod lefel uwch o sgamiau bellach yn effeithio ar ein hetholwyr hŷn.
