XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr, Ddirprwy Lywydd, a diolch am y cyfle i ddiweddaru'r Aelodau am y rhaglen diogelwch adeiladau. Byddaf yn sôn am y camau y mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn eu cymryd i amddiffyn lesddeiliaid a sicrhau bod y cartrefi sydd o dan y rhaglen yn ddiogel, a bod y bobl sy'n byw ynddyn nhw yn cael eu trin efo'r tegwch a'r urddas y maen nhw yn eu haeddu.

Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod person, ac yn aml teulu cyfan, y tu ôl i bob ystadegyn. Mae lesddeiliaid ledled Cymru wedi wynebu blynyddoedd o ansicrwydd. Mae llawer wedi methu â gwerthu eu cartrefi. Mae llawer wedi gweld cynigion am forgais yn cael eu tynnu'n ôl, premiymau yswiriant yn codi a chodi, a'u cynlluniau'n cael eu rhwystro neu eu rhoi ar stop. Dyma realiti bywyd sydd wedi achosi caledi go iawn a straen aruthrol i bobl gyffredin sydd heb wneud dim byd ond prynu cartref gyda phob bwriad da.

Dwi am fod yn glir iawn y prynhawn yma: dydy'r cynnydd o ran y gwaith cyweirio ddim wedi symud yn ddigon cyflym. A dwi'n cydnabod y rhwystredigaeth a'r anobaith y mae hynny wedi'i achosi i lawer. Nid lesddeiliaid sydd wedi creu'r sefyllfa hon ac nid nhw ddylai orfod ysgwyddo'r baich.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much, Dirprwy Lywydd, and thank you for the opportunity to update Members on the building safety programme. I will talk about the steps that the Government is taking to protect leaseholders and to ensure that the homes covered by the programme are safe, and that those living in them are treated with the fairness and the dignity they deserve.

We know that there is a person, and often a whole family, behind every statistic. Leaseholders across Wales have faced years of uncertainty. Many have been unable to sell their homes. Many have seen mortgage offers being withdrawn, they've seen insurance premiums spiral, and they've had their life plans hampered or put on hold. This is the lived reality that has caused genuine hardship and profound stress for ordinary people who did nothing beyond buying a home in good faith.

I want to be really clear this afternoon: the progress in terms of the remediation work has not moved quickly enough. And I recognise the frustration and the hopelessness that this has caused to many. Leaseholders did not create this situation and they should not be made to bear its weight.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Ers derbyn y rôl yma yn Llywodraeth Cymru, dwi wedi cwrdd â lesddeiliaid a gwrando ar eu straeon, ac mae'r hyn dwi wedi'i glywed ganddyn nhw wedi fy nghyffwrdd i. Mae eu hanesion nhw wedi aros efo mi, ac maen nhw wedi siapio fy mhenderfyniad i weithredu ar eu rhan. A dyna pam dwi'n falch o gyhoeddi heddiw lansio grant larymau fel mesur interim Cymru. Bydd y grant yma yn rhoi cymorth ariannol i lesddeiliaid sy'n wynebu costau systemau larwm dros dro sydd eu hangen i gefnogi polisi gwagio adeiladau cydamserol. Bydd rhagor o fanylion am gymhwysedd a sut y gall pobl gael gafael ar y cymorth ar gael yn fuan, ac mi fyddaf i'n sicrhau bod y wybodaeth hon yn cyrraedd y bobl berthnasol cyn gynted â phosibl. A dwi yn gobeithio y bydd y cyhoeddiad yma yn gwneud gwahaniaeth arwyddocaol i lesddeiliaid sy'n ysgwyddo costau mesurau interim. 

Gan droi at Ddeddf Diogelwch Adeiladau (Cymru) 2026, dwi'n falch o ddweud bod y gwaith yn symud yn ei flaen yn dda. Mae'r Ddeddf yn gam mawr ymlaen o ran cyflwyno diwygiadau parhaol i wneud adeiladau yng Nghymru yn fwy diogel. Mae'r Ddeddf yn cryfhau'r fframwaith rheoleiddio ar gyfer adeiladau preswyl amlfeddiannaeth ac yn cyflwyno gofynion cymhwysedd newydd ar gyfer aseswyr risg tân. Mae'r Ddeddf hefyd yn creu mecanweithiau cadarnach i ddwyn perchnogion adeiladau i gyfrif, ac yn rhoi llais cryfach i drigolion mewn materion sy'n effeithio ar eu diogelwch.

Mae pawb yn gwybod beth ydy fy marn i erbyn hyn, sef na ddylid disgwyl i lesddeiliaid dalu am gostau cyweirio na wnaethon nhw eu hachosi. A dwi yn credu, lle bynnag y bo'n bosibl, mai'r bobl sydd wedi datblygu, comisiynu neu elwa ar adeiladau anniogel ddylai fod yn gyfrifol. Dyna pam y gwnes i weithio'n galed i sicrhau bod y Ddeddf yn cynnwys darpariaethau sy'n caniatáu i bartïon â diddordeb wneud cais i'r tribiwnlys eiddo preswyl am orchmynion cyweirio a gorchmynion cyfraniadau cyweirio sy'n ymdrin â diffygion diogelwch tân a strwythurol.

Daeth yr ymgynghoriad ar y rheoliadau sydd eu hangen i gynnal yr elfen hon o'r drefn i ben yn gynharach y mis yma, a dwi'n gobeithio gosod y rheoliadau cyn toriad y Nadolig. Dros y flwyddyn nesaf, mi fyddwn ni'n parhau i ymgynghori ar y rheoliadau sydd eu hangen i gynnal y drefn ehangach fel rhan o'n hamserlen weithredu arfaethedig. Ac rydyn ni'n rhagweld y bydd cofrestru adeiladau categori 1 yn dechrau ym mis Rhagfyr 2027. Mi fyddaf i'n diweddaru'r Aelodau wrth i'r rhaglen weithredu fynd yn ei blaen.

Mae'r Ddeddf yn ategu'r rhaglen ddiwygio helaeth sydd wedi'i chyflwyno'n barod drwy Ddeddf Diogelwch Adeiladau 2022 y Deyrnas Unedig, a'r is-ddeddfwriaeth ddilynol, a hynny'n sail i'r drefn reolaeth adeiladu newydd a ddaeth i rym ym mis Gorffennaf. Mae'r drefn newydd yn cryfhau atebolrwydd i ddeiliaid dyletswydd, ac yn ymgorffori'r gofynion cymhwysedd uwch ar gyfer arolygwyr cofrestredig adeiladu a chymeradwywyr cofrestredig rheolaeth adeiladu. Cafodd dogfen gymeradwyo B o'r rheoliadau adeiladu ei newid y llynedd hefyd.

Mi fydd yr Aelodau'n gwybod yn iawn mai trasiedi tŵr Grenfell ydy'r cyd-destun ar gyfer ein rhaglen diogelwch adeiladau gyfan. Wrth i ni gofio am y 72 o bobl a fu farw, hoffwn i roi'r wybodaeth ddiweddaraf am y gwaith sy'n cael ei wneud i weithredu argymhellion ymchwiliad tŵr Grenfell. Mae dros chwarter yr argymhellion bellach wedi cael eu rhoi ar waith yng Nghymru, a dwi’n disgwyl i hynny ddyblu erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn. Rydyn ni'n delio â llawer o'r argymhellion drwy'r newidiadau deddfwriaethol dwi eisoes wedi sôn amdanyn nhw. Yn ogystal, rydyn ni'n cymryd camau i wella parodrwydd ar gyfer argyfyngau ac ymgorffori gwersi Grenfell ar draws y system.

Yn olaf, fe wnaf i ddychwelyd at ein rhaglen gyweirio. Yr wythnos diwethaf, fe wnes i gyfarfod â datblygwyr sydd wedi llofnodi contract Llywodraeth Cymru. Y Llywodraeth flaenorol oedd hynny. Fe wnes i bwysleisio bod yn rhaid i'r holl rwymedigaethau o dan y contract gael eu bodloni neu mi fyddaf i'n ystyried pob cam gorfodi posib mewn perthynas ag unrhyw fethiannau. Dwi wedi ymrwymo i sicrhau bod y gwaith cyweirio yn cyflymu ac i ddwyn datblygwyr i gyfrif. Mi fyddaf i'n parhau i ddiweddaru cydweithwyr wrth i'r rhaglen fynd yn ei blaen, a dwi'n croesawu'r gwaith craffu gan Aelodau, a fydd yn ein helpu ni i wneud hyn yn iawn er lles pobl Cymru. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Since taking up this role in the Welsh Government, I have met leaseholders and I've listened to their stories, and what I've heard from them has truly moved me. Their accounts have stayed with me, and they have shaped my determination to take action on their behalf. That is why I am pleased to announce today the launch of the Wales interim measures alarm grant. This grant will provide financial support to leaseholders who are facing the costs of interim alarm systems that are required to support a simultaneous evacuation policy. Further detail on eligibility and how people can access the support will be available shortly, and I will ensure that this information reaches the relevant people as quickly as possible. And I do hope that this announcement will make a meaningful difference to leaseholders who are shouldering the costs of interim measures.  

Turning to the Building Safety (Wales) Act 2026, I'm pleased to say that we are making steady progress with implementation. The Act marks a major step forward in delivering lasting building safety reform in Wales. The Act strengthens the regulatory framework for multi-occupied residential buildings and it introduces new competence requirements for fire risk assessors. The Act also creates stronger mechanisms to hold building owners to account, and it gives residents a stronger voice in matters affecting their safety.

Everyone knows what my view is now, which is that leaseholders should not be expected to pay for remediation costs that they did not cause. And I do believe that, wherever possible, the people who developed, commissioned or profited from unsafe buildings should be responsible. And that's why I worked hard to ensure that the Act did include provisions that allow interested parties to apply to the residential property tribunal for remediation orders and remediation contribution orders covering fire and structural safety defects.

The consultation on the regulations that are needed to support this element of the regime closed earlier this month, and I hope to the lay regulations before the Christmas recess. Over the coming year, we’ll continue consulting on the regulations that are required to underpin the wider regime as part of our planned implementation schedule. And we anticipate that the registration of category 1 buildings will begin in December 2027. I'll keep Members updated as the implementation programme progresses.

The Act complements the extensive programme of reform already delivered through the UK Building Safety Act 2022, as well as the subsequent secondary legislation, and that underpins the new building control regime that came into force in July. The new regime strengthens accountability for duty holders and it embeds the enhanced competence requirements for registered building inspectors and registered building control approvers. Amendments were also made to approved document B of the building regulations last year.

Members will be very well aware the Grenfell tower tragedy is the backdrop to our entire building safety programme. As we remember the 72 people who lost their lives, I would like to provide an update on the progress being made to implement the recommendations of the Grenfell tower inquiry. Over a quarter of the recommendations have now been implemented in Wales, and I expect that number to double by the end of the year. We are addressing many of the recommendations through the legislative changes I have already spoken about. Additionally, we've taken action to strengthen emergency preparedness and to embed the lessons from Grenfell across the system.

Finally, I'll return to our remediation programme. Last week, I met with developers who have signed up to the Welsh Government contract. That was the previous Government's contract. I emphasised that all obligations under the contract must be met or I will consider all appropriate enforcement avenues in relation to any failures. I am committed to accelerating the pace of remediation and to holding developers to account. I will continue to update colleagues as the programme progresses, and I welcome the scrutiny work from Members, which will help us to get this right for the people of Wales. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you to the Minister for her statement this afternoon. The Minister told this Chamber today that progress on the remediation has not moved quickly, and I totally agree with her statement on that, but her predecessor said much the same thing. What we've not heard, for nine years may I add, is a satisfactory explanation for why so little has actually been done. I also note that there is not a single remediation figure in today's statement. So, let me put some numbers alongside that statement. As of the summer this year, out of 161 private sector buildings that developers are responsible for, only four have been fully remediated, which is shocking. Seventy per cent have not even started work, though most, we are told, have plans in place. The Minister's predecessor described this as significant progress. Well, Minister, if that is how they describe significant progress, I would hate to see what failure looks like. If those numbers have improved, though, why aren't they included in today's statement?

What has happened over the years though? Well, social housing has been remediated using public money, up to 100 per cent of eligible costs, through the Welsh building safety fund. At Celestia in Cardiff Bay, the Welsh Government funded cladding replacement on the social housing block to the tune of nearly £2 million. The other seven blocks at Celestia, including private leaseholders, remain untouched. Same development, same defects, but years waiting. Let me be clear, I do not believe that taxpayers should be picking up more of the bill—exactly what you've said in your statement—for the private developers. Those who have built these unsafe homes and profited from them must pay to put them right. But that cannot become an excuse for private leaseholders to wait years longer than their neighbours in social housing. The Government found the urgency to fix the social side. It must now find the same urgency on the private side.

Plaid Cymru claim they stand for fairness, so I ask the Minister: does she accept that this two-tier approach, faster action for social housing and barely there action for the private leaseholders, has been a failure of fair treatment by the Welsh Government? Just take Meridian Quay in my constituency, for example. Phil Lake, a resident, took an insurance giant to the High Court on behalf of residents. Their claim was worth more than £25 million. Only now, seven years after Mr Lake stepped in, is remediation expected to start, and will be paid through the financial services compensation scheme, not by this Government.

Today, in your statement, you announced a Wales interim measures alarm grant. Any help for leaseholders is really welcome. But, in England, the funding for these alarms began in December 2020. Wales is almost six years behind. And we've been given no budget, no eligibility criteria and no opening date in this statement. So, will leaseholders who have already paid the price for alarms get anything back, because in my constituency, and I'm sure of many of us sitting here today, people are paying around £500 a month for these alarms, which is more than some people's mortgages?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch i'r Gweinidog am ei datganiad y prynhawn yma. Dywedodd y Gweinidog wrth y Siambr hon heddiw nad yw'r cynnydd ar y gwaith cyweirio wedi symud yn gyflym, ac rwy'n cytuno'n llwyr â'i datganiad ar hynny, ond dywedodd ei rhagflaenydd yr un peth. Yr hyn nad ydym ni wedi'i glywed, ers naw mlynedd, os caf i ychwanegu, yw esboniad boddhaol pam mae cyn lleied wedi'i wneud mewn gwirionedd. Sylwaf hefyd nad oes un ffigur cyweirio yn y datganiad heddiw. Felly, gadewch i mi roi rhai rhifau ochr yn ochr â'r datganiad hwnnw. Fel yr oedd hi yn haf eleni, o 161 o adeiladau sector preifat y mae datblygwyr yn gyfrifol amdanynt, dim ond pedwar sydd wedi'u cyweirio'n llawn, sy'n syfrdanol. Nid yw gwaith wedi dechrau hyd yn oed gyda saith deg y cant ohonyn nhw, er bod gan y mwyafrif ohonyn nhw, fe ddywedir wrthym ni, gynlluniau ar waith. Disgrifiodd rhagflaenydd y Gweinidog hyn fel cynnydd sylweddol. Wel, Weinidog, os mai dyna sut maen nhw'n disgrifio cynnydd sylweddol, byddwn yn casáu gweld sut olwg sydd ar fethiant. Os yw'r niferoedd hynny wedi gwella, fodd bynnag, pam nad ydyn nhw wedi'u cynnwys yn y datganiad heddiw?

Beth sydd wedi digwydd dros y blynyddoedd? Wel, mae tai cymdeithasol wedi cael eu cyweirio gan ddefnyddio arian cyhoeddus, hyd at 100 y cant o'r costau cymwys, trwy gronfa diogelwch adeiladau Cymru. Yn Celestia ym Mae Caerdydd, ariannodd Llywodraeth Cymru y gwaith o gyfnewid cladin ar y bloc tai cymdeithasol ar gost o bron i £2 filiwn. Mae'r saith bloc arall yn Celestia, gan gynnwys lesddeiliaid preifat, yn parhau i fod heb eu cyffwrdd. Yr un datblygiad, yr un diffygion, ond blynyddoedd o aros. Gadewch i mi fod yn glir, nid wyf yn credu y dylai trethdalwyr fod yn talu mwy o'r bil—yn union yr hyn rydych chi wedi'i ddweud yn eich datganiad—ar gyfer y datblygwyr preifat. Rhaid i'r rhai sydd wedi adeiladu'r cartrefi anniogel hyn ac elwa ohonyn nhw dalu i'w cyweirio. Ond ni all hynny ddod yn esgus i lesddeiliaid preifat aros flynyddoedd yn hirach na'u cymdogion mewn tai cymdeithasol. Gwelodd y Llywodraeth fod angen brys i gyweirio'r ochr gymdeithasol. Mae'n rhaid iddi nawr weld yr un brys ar yr ochr breifat.

Mae Plaid Cymru yn honni eu bod yn sefyll dros degwch, felly gofynnaf i'r Gweinidog: a yw hi'n derbyn bod y dull dwy haen hwn, gweithredu cyflymach ar gyfer tai cymdeithasol a phrin unrhyw weithredu i'r lesddeiliaid preifat, wedi bod yn fethiant i drin yn deg gan Lywodraeth Cymru? Cymerwch Meridian Quay yn fy etholaeth i, er enghraifft. Aeth Phil Lake, preswylydd, â chwmni yswiriant mawr i'r Uchel Lys ar ran preswylwyr. Roedden nhw'n hawlio gwerth mwy na £25 miliwn. Dim ond nawr, saith mlynedd ar ôl i Mr Lake ymyrryd, mae disgwyl i'r gwaith cyweirio ddechrau, a bydd yn cael ei dalu trwy gynllun iawndal y gwasanaethau ariannol, nid gan y Llywodraeth hon.

Heddiw, yn eich datganiad, fe wnaethoch chi gyhoeddi Grant larymau fel mesur interim Cymru. Mae croeso mawr i unrhyw gymorth i lesddeiliaid. Ond, yn Lloegr, dechreuodd y cyllid ar gyfer y larymau hyn ym mis Rhagfyr 2020. Mae Cymru bron i chwe blynedd ar ei hôl hi. Ac nid ydym ni wedi cael unrhyw gyllideb, dim meini prawf cymhwysedd a dim dyddiad dechrau yn y datganiad hwn. Felly, a fydd lesddeiliaid sydd eisoes wedi talu'r pris am larymau yn cael unrhyw beth yn ôl, oherwydd yn fy etholaeth i, ac rwy'n siŵr o lawer ohonom ni sy'n eistedd yma heddiw, mae pobl yn talu tua £500 y mis am y larymau hyn, sy'n fwy na morgeisi rhai pobl?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr, a diolch am nifer o gwestiynau pwysig, ac mi fyddaf i'n ceisio eu hateb nhw fesul un. Dwi'n cytuno'n llwyr efo chi, dydy'r cynnydd ddim wedi digwydd yn ddigon cyflym, a bai'r datblygwyr ydy hynny. Nhw sydd i fod i wneud y gwaith cyweirio ar yr adeiladau yma yng Nghymru. Fe gawson nhw'r neges yna'n glir gen i yr wythnos diwethaf. Mi wnes i gyfarfod efo'r 11 datblygwr—.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, and thank you for asking a number of important questions, and I will seek to take them one at a time. I agree entirely with you that progress hasn't happened swiftly enough, and that is the fault of the developers. They are supposed to carry out the remediation work on these buildings in Wales. They received that message clearly from me just last week. I met with the 11 developers—.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I met the 11 developers last week, and my message to them was very, very clear. The message was that the pace of delivery is simply not good enough. And I said that if I don't see progress, as outlined in the contract that they signed with the previous Government by the end of this year, I will be bringing their names forward here in the Senedd. I will be taking action. And I think that that is one route that I can definitely tell you about, because I've told them, and that that will happen within this year as we look at the progress reports. I'm hoping that that's not going to happen. I hope that they will really ramp up the work. Because we all want to see the leaseholders feeling protected and feeling safe in their places, in their apartments and what have you.

In terms of the data, I can absolutely give you the latest data, which, as you say, is not good enough, but I can give you the data. So, there are 161 buildings in the programme. By now, 11 buildings have been completed or they didn't need work in the first place. I understand that there are two or three others very, very near to that point as well. Work is progressing on 71 of those buildings, but there's work that's being talked about, but hasn't started yet, on 65 buildings, and there are 14 that are awaiting the reviews. So, it's not good enough, and I agree with you on that.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Fe wnes i gwrdd â'r 11 datblygwr yr wythnos diwethaf, ac roedd fy neges iddyn nhw yn glir iawn, iawn. Y neges oedd nad yw'r cyflawni yn ddigon cyflym. A dywedais, os nad ydw i'n gweld cynnydd, fel yr amlinellwyd yn y contract a lofnodwyd ganddyn nhw gyda'r Llywodraeth flaenorol erbyn diwedd eleni, byddaf yn eu henwi nhw yma yn y Senedd. Byddaf yn cymryd camau. Ac rwy'n credu bod hynny'n un llwybr y gallaf i ddweud wrthych chi yn bendant amdano, oherwydd rydw i wedi dweud wrthyn nhw, ac y bydd hynny'n digwydd yng nghwrs eleni wrth i ni edrych ar yr adroddiadau cynnydd. Rwy'n gobeithio na fydd hynny'n digwydd. Rwy'n gobeithio y byddant yn cyflymu'r gwaith mewn gwirionedd. Oherwydd rydym ni i gyd eisiau gweld y lesddeiliaid yn teimlo'n ddiogel yn eu lleoedd, yn eu fflatiau ac ati.

O ran y data, gallaf roi'r data diweddaraf i chi, nad yw, fel y dywedwch chi, yn ddigon da, ond gallaf roi'r data i chi. Felly, mae 161 o adeiladau yn y rhaglen. Erbyn hyn, mae 11 adeilad wedi'u cwblhau neu doedd dim angen gwaith arnyn nhw yn y lle cyntaf. Rwy'n deall bod dau neu dri arall yn agos iawn, iawn at y pwynt hwnnw hefyd. Mae gwaith yn mynd rhagddo ar 71 o'r adeiladau hynny, ond mae yna waith sy'n cael ei siarad amdano, ond heb ddechrau eto, ar 65 o adeiladau, ac mae 14 yn aros am yr adolygiadau. Felly, nid yw'n ddigon da, ac rwy'n cytuno â chi ar hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Roeddech chi'n sôn am ddatblygiad penodol yn fanna, yn eich cyfraniad. Dwi'n awgrymu bod yr Aelodau yn cymryd cyfle i ddod i'r briffiad technegol y mae fy swyddogion yn mynd i fod yn cynnal. Bydd cyfle yr amser hynny ichi drafod adeiladau unigol. Yn amlwg, dwi ddim yn mynd i fedru mynd i mewn i bob un o'r sefyllfaoedd, y 161 adeilad, yn fan hyn heddiw, ond mae yna sesiwn friffio i Aelodau ar y gweill. Ac mae'r rheina'n mynd i gael eu cynnal—un yr wythnos yma ac un yr wythnos nesaf. So, mae yna gyfle i bobl ddod a dod â'u cwestiynau ymlaen efo hynny i gyd.

O ran y grant ei hun, dwi'n falch eich bod chi'n croesawu'r grant, achos mae hwn wedi bod yn bryder i nifer o lesddeiliaid, fod y costau o roi'r systemau larwm dros dro i mewn yn yr adeiladau tra bod y gwaith yn digwydd—. Mae rhai ohonyn nhw wedi ffeindio mai nhw sy'n gorfod talu, a dydy hynna ddim yn deg. Dydy hynna ddim yn deg. Mae yna rai datblygwyr wedi talu amdano fo, ond mae yna rai sefyllfaoedd lle dydy hynna ddim wedi digwydd. Mi fydd y grant ar gael—mi fydd y ceisiadau yn agor yn fuan iawn ar gyfer hynny, a'r asiant neu'r person, yr endid cyfrifol, fydd efo'r hawl i wneud y cais yna am y grant, nid y datblygwyr. Y bobl sy'n gweithredu ar ran y llesddeiliaid fydd yn gallu gwneud y cais penodol yna.

O ran y rheoliadau, fel dwi'n dweud, dwi wedi symud yn sydyn ar gael y rheoliadau. Dwi yr un mor rhwystredig â chi am arafwch symud pethau ymlaen, ond byddai'r rheoliadau yna ddim yna o gwbl heblaw am y gwaith y gwnaethom ni ei wneud wrth graffu'r Bil, mewn cydweithrediad efo'r cyn-Ysgrifennydd Cabinet ar y pryd. Felly, mae'r hawl i fynd i dribiwnlys i hawlio arian yn ôl—. Mae'n rhaid gosod y rheoliadau, ac wedyn mae'n rhaid—. Fel dŷch chi'n dweud, mae'n rhwystredig nad ydym ni'n gallu cychwyn arno fo yn syth, ond mi ddaw i fodolaeth.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
You mentioned a particular development there in your contribution. I would suggest that Members take the opportunity to come to the technical briefing that my officials will be providing. There will be an opportunity at that point for you to discuss individual buildings. Clearly, I can't go into every single example, in terms of the 161 buildings, here today, but there will be a Members' briefing session held. And those sessions will be held—one this week and one next week. So, there's an opportunity for people to bring their questions forward in that forum too.

In terms of the grant itself, I'm pleased that you've welcomed that, because this has been a concern for many leaseholders, that the costs of putting the temporary alarm systems in place in these buildings while the work is ongoing—. In some cases, leaseholders have had to pay, and that isn't fair. That isn't fair. There are some developers who have paid for it, but there are other scenarios where that hasn't been the case. The grant will be available, and the application process will open very soon for that, and the agent or the responsible body will have that responsibility to make that application, not the developer. It'll be people acting on behalf of the leaseholders who will be able to make that particular application.

In terms of the regulations, as I've said, I've moved swiftly in getting those regulations in place. I am just as frustrated as you about the slow progress here, but those regulations wouldn't be there at all if it wasn't for the work that we did in scrutinising the Bill, in collaboration with the former Cabinet Secretary. So, the right to go to tribunal to claim money back—. We do have to have those regulations in place, and then we have to—. As you say, it is frustrating that we can't start that immediately, but it will come in due course.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I thank the Minister for her statement today. As she said, the origins of this work are following the dreadful events of 14 June 2017, when 72 people lost their lives in the fire at Grenfell Tower. Following the tragedy, the Welsh Labour Government set out to deliver a new building safety programme for the benefit of residents of shared buildings across Wales, regardless of building height or tenure. Change on this scale is complex and time-consuming and resulted in one of the largest Bills ever to be considered by this Senedd. I was very glad to be able to take the landmark Building Safety (Wales) Bill through the Senedd, and I'm grateful to the current Minister, and others in this Chamber, for their collaborative approach, which ensured that a whole series of complex amendments were unanimously agreed at Stage 3. This, Deputy Llywydd, was a Senedd first and demonstrated a desire to get this right.

The legislation that we passed here in Wales is far broader in its scope and ambition than the equivalent legislation in England. Three key principles are fundamental to the Act. First is safety. While we can never eliminate all risks, we can significantly enhance safety by identifying risks and ensuring that these risks are properly managed. The second principle is accountability. The Act ends any confusion about who is answerable for managing building safety risks. It ensures that those responsible for buildings are held to account in law for their safety. The third principle is residents' voice. Residents' experiences and concerns must be heard and addressed.

But passing the primary legislation is only the first step. Our focus must now be on ensuring that the Act is fully implemented, so it transforms safety in multi-occupied residential buildings across Wales. We now need to ensure that the Bill is practical and deliverable, and this means ensuring that regulations are clear and achievable. The Act will be determined by secondary regulations and statutory guidance, and how housing associations, building safety authorities and fire safety authorities are appropriately resourced to deliver their enhanced responsibilities.

So, what proactive steps is the Welsh Government taking to address the specialist workforce shortages ahead of the implementation? I know that Community Housing Cymru has been sharing with the Government feedback from their members across Wales. It's important that the Government listens and shares additional information that will be brought forward by regulations, so that housing associations can effectively prepare. Given the financial impact of compliance, how will the Welsh Government ensure that funding mechanisms support compliance and do not force housing associations to trade off the maintenance of existing homes against the delivery of urgently needed new affordable housing?

I'm very aware of the financial and well-being impact on people waiting for remediation. The Welsh Labour Government proactively supported residents by putting in place contracts with developers, and this Government must continue to do everything possible to remove barriers to progress.

I do welcome the alarm grant announced today, but people need to know urgently if they're eligible, how much this will be and how they can access it. When in Government, I set up the developers forum, which met regularly, and it's really good to hear that the Minister is continuing that work. I look forward to further updates on the pace of remediation, something that all of us in this Siambr want to see.

I'm really pleased that you're also continuing with the Members' briefing, the technical briefing, that I established. Those sessions, I think, are really important for Members to raise with your officials really local issues. That's something we can always get to grips with, and I hope officials can follow that progress as well. But I think it's really important for Members to understand the parts of the Welsh Government and the progress the Welsh Government is trying to make.

But much work remains to implement a new building safety regime across Wales. I said when the building safety Bill passed that I hoped the next Welsh Government would bring forward a remediation Bill to further support leaseholders. So, now, Cabinet Minister, that you're the Cabinet Minister, can you confirm whether your Government intends to bring forward a remediation Bill? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolchaf i'r Gweinidog am ei datganiad heddiw. Fel y dywedodd, mae gwreiddiau'r gwaith hwn yn dilyn digwyddiadau ofnadwy 14 Mehefin 2017, pan gollodd 72 o bobl eu bywydau yn y tân yn Nhŵr Grenfell. Yn dilyn y trychineb, aeth Llywodraeth Lafur Cymru ati i gyflwyno rhaglen diogelwch adeiladu newydd er budd trigolion adeiladau cydbreswylio ledled Cymru, waeth beth fo'u huchder neu ddeiliadaeth yr adeilad. Mae newid ar y raddfa hon yn gymhleth ac yn cymryd llawer o amser ac arweiniodd at un o'r Biliau mwyaf erioed i gael ei ystyried gan y Senedd hon. Roeddwn yn falch iawn o allu mynd â'r Bil Diogelwch Adeiladau (Cymru) nodedig drwy'r Senedd, ac rwy'n ddiolchgar i'r Gweinidog presennol, ac eraill yn y Siambr hon, am eu dull cydweithredol, a sicrhaodd fod cyfres gyfan o welliannau cymhleth yn cael eu cytuno'n unfrydol yng Nghyfnod 3. Roedd hyn, Ddirprwy Lywydd, yn beth cyntaf i'r Senedd ac yn dangos awydd i wneud hyn yn iawn.

Mae'r ddeddfwriaeth a basiwyd gennym ni yma yng Nghymru yn llawer ehangach yn ei chwmpas a'i huchelgais na'r ddeddfwriaeth gyfatebol yn Lloegr. Mae tair egwyddor allweddol yn sylfaenol i'r Ddeddf. Y cyntaf yw diogelwch. Er na allwn ni byth ddileu pob risg, fe allwn ni wella diogelwch yn sylweddol trwy adnabod risgiau a sicrhau bod y risgiau hyn yn cael eu rheoli'n iawn. Yr ail egwyddor yw atebolrwydd. Mae'r Ddeddf yn rhoi terfyn ar unrhyw ddryswch ynghylch pwy sy'n atebol am reoli risgiau diogelwch adeiladau. Mae'n sicrhau bod y rhai sy'n gyfrifol am adeiladau yn cael eu dwyn i gyfrif yn y gyfraith am eu diogelwch. Y drydedd egwyddor yw llais preswylwyr. Rhaid clywed a mynd i'r afael â phrofiadau a phryderon preswylwyr.

Ond dim ond y cam cyntaf yw pasio'r ddeddfwriaeth sylfaenol. Rhaid i'n pwyslais nawr fod ar sicrhau bod y Ddeddf yn cael ei gweithredu'n llawn, fel ei bod yn trawsnewid diogelwch mewn adeiladau preswyl amlfeddiannaeth ledled Cymru. Mae angen i ni nawr sicrhau bod y Bil yn ymarferol a bod modd ei gyflawni, ac mae hyn yn golygu sicrhau bod rheoliadau'n glir ac yn gyraeddadwy. Bydd y Ddeddf yn cael ei phenderfynu gan reoliadau eilaidd a chanllawiau statudol, a sut mae cymdeithasau tai, awdurdodau diogelwch adeiladau ac awdurdodau diogelwch tân yn cael adnoddau priodol i gyflawni eu cyfrifoldebau uwch.

Felly, pa gamau rhagweithiol y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â'r prinder gweithlu arbenigol cyn gweithredu? Fe wn i fod Cartrefi Cymunedol Cymru wedi bod yn rhannu adborth gyda'r Llywodraeth gan eu haelodau ledled Cymru. Mae'n bwysig bod y Llywodraeth yn gwrando ac yn rhannu gwybodaeth ychwanegol a fydd yn cael ei gyflwyno gan reoliadau, fel y gall cymdeithasau tai baratoi'n effeithiol. O ystyried effaith ariannol cydymffurfio, sut y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau bod mecanweithiau cyllido yn cefnogi cydymffurfiaeth ac nad ydynt yn gorfodi cymdeithasau tai i gynnal a chadw cartrefi presennol yn hytrach na darparu tai fforddiadwy newydd sydd eu hangen ar frys?

Rwy'n ymwybodol iawn o'r effaith ariannol a lles ar bobl sy'n aros am waith cyfeirio. Cefnogodd Llywodraeth Lafur Cymru drigolion yn rhagweithiol trwy roi contractau ar waith gyda datblygwyr, ac mae'n rhaid i'r Llywodraeth hon barhau i wneud popeth posibl i gael gwared ar rwystrau i gynnydd.

Rwyf yn croesawu'r grant larymau a gyhoeddwyd heddiw, ond mae angen i bobl wybod ar frys os ydyn nhw'n gymwys, faint fydd hyn a sut y gallan nhw gael mynediad ato. Pan oeddwn yn rhan o'r Llywodraeth, sefydlais y fforwm datblygwyr, a gyfarfu'n rheolaidd, ac mae'n dda iawn clywed bod y Gweinidog yn parhau â'r gwaith hwnnw. Edrychaf ymlaen at ddiweddariadau pellach ar gyflymder y gwaith cyweirio, rhywbeth y mae pob un ohonom ni yn y Siambr hon eisiau ei weld.

Rwy'n falch iawn eich bod hefyd yn parhau gyda'r cyfarfodydd briffio Aelodau, y cyfarfodydd briffio technegol, a sefydlais. Mae'r sesiynau hynny, rwy'n credu, yn bwysig iawn i Aelodau godi gyda'ch swyddogion faterion lleol iawn. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth y gallwn ni bob amser fynd i'r afael ag ef, ac rwy'n gobeithio y gall swyddogion ddilyn y cynnydd hwnnw hefyd. Ond rwy'n credu ei bod hi'n bwysig iawn i Aelodau ddeall y rhannau o Lywodraeth Cymru a'r cynnydd y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ceisio ei wneud.

Ond mae llawer o waith i'w wneud o hyd i weithredu cyfundrefn diogelwch adeiladau newydd ledled Cymru. Dywedais pan basiwyd y Bil diogelwch adeiladau fy mod i'n gobeithio y byddai Llywodraeth nesaf Cymru yn cyflwyno Bil cyweirio i gefnogi lesddeiliaid ymhellach. Felly, nawr, Weinidog Cabinet, mai chi yw'r Gweinidog Cabinet, a allwch chi gadarnhau a yw eich Llywodraeth yn bwriadu cyflwyno Bil cyweirio? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r cyn-Weinidog, neu Ysgrifennydd Cabinet, a oedd yn gyfrifol am lywio, yn ddeheuig iawn, y Bil sydd bellach yn Ddeddf yn ystod y Senedd ddiwethaf, ac roeddwn i'n falch iawn o gydweithio efo chi. Ac, ie, fel dŷch chi'n ein hatgoffa ni, roedd o'r tro cyntaf i'r Senedd weithredu yn y ffordd hollol gynhwysol yna a phasio'r ddeddfwriaeth yn unfrydol. Mae hi yn fwriad gen i i geisio gweithio yn yr un ffordd efo pawb yn y Siambr yma.

Mi fyddwch chi'n gwybod ein bod ni wedi ymrwymo i ddod â deddfwriaeth newydd i mewn yn y maes tai—nifer o Filiau penodol—er mwyn rhoi gwell gwarchodaeth i rentwyr, ac i edrych yn union ar ba fath o fesurau sydd eu hangen arnom ni yng Nghymru wrth inni symud ymlaen. A dwi yn gobeithio y gallwn ni weithio efo'n gilydd, bawb ohonom ni, er mwyn efelychu'r dull a ddefnyddiwyd yn ystod y Senedd ddiwethaf. Dwi'n edrych ymlaen at gael cyfarfodydd cychwynnol efo'r llefaryddion er mwyn inni fod yn egluro sut dŷn ni'n bwriadu symud ymlaen efo deddfwriaeth—ddim yn y maes yma, yn amlwg, ond yn y maes tai yn fwy cyffredinol.

Dŷch chi'n hollol iawn, mae'r ddeddfwriaeth yma yng Nghymru yn eang ei sgôp, ac mae'n cyd-fynd, wrth gwrs, efo'r ddeddfwriaeth a basiwyd yn Lloegr, ond mae'n adeiladu ar hynny ac yn dod ag elfennau gwahanol i mewn—diogelwch a phwy sy'n atebol, ond hefyd, ie, llais y trigolion. Dwi'n meddwl ei bod hi'n hollbwysig inni gydnabod llais y trigolion yn hyn oll, a phwysigrwydd eu cynnwys nhw wrth inni symud ymlaen. Felly, dwi yn bwriadu cyhoeddi cyn bo hir y byddwn ni'n sefydlu fforwm ar gyfer llesddeiliaid, a bydd mater diogelwch adeiladu yn rhywbeth pwysig y bydd y fforwm yna yn ei drafod. Mae hwnna yn adeiladu ar y gwaith a oedd yn digwydd yn ystod cyfnod y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf.

Dwi'n gwerthfawrogi'n fawr iawn fy mod i wedi cael cyfle i glywed yn uniongyrchol gan y Cladiators fel grŵp ymgyrchu, sydd wedi bod yn ddiflino yn sôn am y gwaith sydd angen ei brysuro. Y bore yma, fe ges i gyfle hefyd i gyfarfod cynrychiolwyr o lesddeiliaid y Sand Wharf yng Nghaerdydd a Swansea Point yn Abertawe, a chlywed yn uniongyrchol ganddyn nhw beth mae'r profiad presennol yn ei olygu i lesddeiliaid a'r pryder y mae o'n ei achosi. Ac yn sicr, mae siarad efo nhw a siarad efo'r pwyllgor hefyd—. Wrth inni fynd yn ein blaenau, dwi'n gobeithio y bydd y pwyllgor llywodraeth leol yn helpu i graffu'r rheoliadau i wneud yn union beth dŷch chi'n awgrymu, sef i wneud y rheoliadau sydd yn mynd i orwedd o dan y ddeddfwriaeth rŵan i wneud yn siŵr bod hynna'n glir a bod y rheini'n bwrpasol. Felly, mae'r gwaith yna. Mae yna lot o waith i'w wneud o dan y Ddeddf, ddim jyst pasio'r Ddeddf—mae yna gymaint o waith sydd angen digwydd o dan hynny, ac mae gennym ni amserlen ar ei gyfer o. Ond y peth cyntaf un gwnes i wneud oedd dod â'r ymgynghoriad ynglŷn â rheoliadau ynglŷn â chostau cyweirio, achos roeddwn i'n ymwybodol bod hwnna'n pwyso yn fawr ar nifer fawr o bobl.

O ran y gweithlu arbenigol sydd ei angen, yn sicr, mae hwnna'n rhywbeth rydym ni'n rhoi sylw iddo fo. Fel rydych chi'n gwybod, mae adrannau rheolaeth adeiladu ac adrannau cynllunio wedi colli gweithwyr, wedi colli staff, dros gyfnod hir rŵan, ac, yn sicr, rydym ni'n rhoi sylw i hynny o ran sut medrwn ni ddod â'r arbenigedd penodol yna yn ôl. Wrth gwrs, y syniad ydy bod yna dri awdurdod yn arwain ar y gwaith yma, a dwi'n meddwl drwy wneud o fel yna—ac roeddwn i'n falch o gefnogi'r gwelliant yna ar gyfer y Bil hefyd—o'i wneud o mewn ffordd sydd wedi—. Dydyn ddim yn disgwyl i'r 22 awdurdod lleol gymryd y baich yma yn unigol. Rydym ni'n mynd i wneud o mewn ffordd ranbarthol, ac felly dwi'n meddwl bydd hwnna'n creu'r gweithlu arbenigol rydym ni'n mynd i fod ei angen. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much to the former Minister, or Cabinet Secretary, who was responsible for steering, very agilely, the Bill that is now an Act during the last Senedd, and I was very pleased to work together with you. And, yes, as you remind us, it was the first time for this Senedd to operate in that entirely inclusive, collaborative way and to pass that legislation unanimously. It is my intention to try and work in that same way with everyone in this Chamber.

You will know that we have committed to bring forward new legislation in the area of housing—a number of specific Bills—in order to give better protections to renters, and to look at exactly what kinds of measures are needed here in Wales as we move forward. And I do hope that we can work together, every one of us, in order to follow the same approach that we followed in the last Senedd. I look forward to having initial meetings with party spokespeople in order for us to explain how we intend to move forward with the legislation—not in this area, clearly, but in the area of housing more generally.

You are quite right, this legislation in Wales is very broad in its scope, and it aligns, of course, with the legislation that was passed in England, but it builds on that and brings different elements in—safety and who is accountable, but also, yes, the residents' voice. I think it is crucial that we acknowledge the residents' voice in all of this, and the importance of including them as we move forward. So, I do intend to announce shortly that we will establish a forum for leaseholders, and the issue of building safety will be something very important that that forum will be discussing. That builds on the work that was happening during the last Government.

I very much appreciate that I had the opportunity to hear directly from the Cladiators as a campaign group, who have been tirelessly campaigning and talking about the work that needs to happen at pace. This morning, I also had an opportunity to meet with representatives from the leaseholders of the Sand Wharf in Cardiff and Swansea Point in Swansea, and to hear directly from them about what the current experience means for leaseholders and the concern and the worry that it causes. And certainly, speaking with them and speaking with the committee as well—. As we move forward, I hope that the local government committee will help us to scrutinise the regulations to do exactly what you suggest, which is to make regulations that will lie under the legislation now to make sure that that is clear and that those regulations are suitable. So, there is that work. There is a lot of work to do under this Act; it's not just passing the Act—there is so much work that needs to happen underneath that, and we do have a timetable for that. But the very first thing that I did was to bring forward that consultation on regulations about the costs of remediation, because I was aware that that was something that was weighing very heavily on a great number of people.

In terms of the expert, specialist workforce that's needed, certainly that is something that we are giving due attention to. As you know, building control departments and planning departments have lost workers, have lost staff, over a long period of time now, and, certainly, we are paying attention to that and how we can bring that expertise back in. Of course, the idea is that there would be three authorities leading on this work, and I think by doing it in that way—and I was pleased to support that amendment to the Bill as well—in doing it in that way—. We aren't expecting all 22 local authorities to take on this burden individually. We're going to do it in a regional way, and I think that that will create the specialist workforce that we are going to need. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Can I thank you, Cabinet Minister, for your statement today? There are many sentiments within it that I align with, especially regarding the victims of Grenfell. Our hearts still go out to them and their families.

Every resident in Wales deserves to know their home is safe, that identified risks are being addressed swiftly, and that they will not be left facing years of uncertainty while Governments debate responsibility. Progress must be measured by outcomes. For too long, many people across Wales have faced uncertainty about the safety of their homes, the costs they may face and the timescales for remediation.

We must ensure that those responsible for building failures contribute towards putting them right. Residents who bought or rented homes in good faith should not be left carrying the burden of mistakes made by others. I note the announcement of the Wales interim measures alarm grant, which will provide support for leaseholders facing the costs of interim alarm systems. Now, while any assistance for affected residents will be welcome, leaseholders will want clarity on how many people are expected to benefit, how quickly support will be available, and whether the scheme will fully address the costs many residents continue to face as a consequence of failures for which they bear no responsibility.

Looking now at remediation orders, as well as the need to hold developers to account, the key test is not how many powers are available, but how quickly unsafe buildings are fixed and how many families are able to move on with their lives. There are concerns about the pace of progress. Clearly, we've heard them all today, and you acknowledge those yourself. But people need confidence that meaningful action is being taken now, and that remediation will not be delayed. As always in Wales, we need action, not more bureaucracy.

Minister, there is also a wider challenge here. You have made it clear that increasing housing supply is one of your priorities, with ambitions for 20,000 new social homes by 2030. Now, while increasing supply is important, quantity must never come at the expense of quality. And some of you may have heard Radio Wales this morning, where they were talking about snagging—so many new houses that have got so many faults. Well, we can't have poorly built houses in the first place, and the lessons of past building failures must be fully embedded in future development, so that every new home is built to the highest standard of safety, quality and resilience.

At the same time, Wales faces a housing crisis. We need more homes, but we need safe homes. We need faster development, but we also need public confidence that safety standards are being rigorously upheld. These objectives are not in conflict. They must go hand in hand. We also recognise that public confidence depends on ensuring that all significant safety risks are addressed, whether they relate to cladding, asbestos, reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete or wider structural concerns. People deserve safe homes, clear information and swift action when problems are identified. Therefore, can you, Minister, confirm how many leaseholders are expected to benefit from the Wales interim measures alarm grant? What assessment has been made of whether the scheme will meet the costs faced by affected residents? And what assurances can you provide that remediation work and developer compliance will accelerate well before the planned registration of the category 1 buildings, as you mentioned, in December 2027?

Ultimately, success will not be judged by the number of strategies, working groups or announcements; it will be judged by whether families can sleep safely in their homes and whether the public can have confidence that the failures of the past are not repeated. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gaf i ddiolch i chi, Weinidog Cabinet, am eich datganiad heddiw? Mae yna lawer ynddo yr wyf yn cytuno ag ef, yn enwedig ynglŷn â dioddefwyr Grenfell. Rydym ni'n dal i gydymdeimlo o waelod ein calonnau gyda nhw a'u teuluoedd.

Mae pob preswylydd yng Nghymru yn haeddu gwybod bod eu cartref yn ddiogel, bod risgiau sydd wedi'u nodi yn cael eu hystyried yn gyflym, ac na adewir nhw yn wynebu blynyddoedd o ansicrwydd tra bod Llywodraethau yn trafod cyfrifoldeb. Rhaid mesur cynnydd yn ôl canlyniadau. Am amser rhy hir, mae llawer o bobl ledled Cymru wedi wynebu ansicrwydd ynghylch diogelwch eu cartrefi, y costau y gallan nhw eu hwynebu a'r amserlenni ar gyfer cyweirio.

Rhaid i ni sicrhau bod y rhai sy'n gyfrifol am fethiannau adeiladau yn cyfrannu tuag at eu cywiro. Ni ddylid gadael preswylwyr sy'n prynu neu rentu cartrefi yn ddidwyll yn cario baich camgymeriadau a wnaed gan eraill. Nodaf y cyhoeddiad am grant larymau mesur interim Cymru, a fydd yn darparu cymorth i lesddeiliaid sy'n wynebu costau am systemau larymau dros dro. Nawr, er y bydd croeso i unrhyw gymorth i breswylwyr yr effeithir arnyn nhw, bydd lesddeiliaid eisiau eglurder ynghylch faint o bobl y disgwylir iddyn nhw elwa, pa mor gyflym y bydd cymorth ar gael, ac a fydd y cynllun yn mynd i'r afael yn llawn â'r costau y mae llawer o breswylwyr yn parhau i'w hwynebu o ganlyniad i fethiannau nad ydyn nhw'n gyfrifol amdanynt.

Wrth edrych nawr ar orchmynion cyweirio, yn ogystal â'r angen i ddwyn datblygwyr i gyfrif, y prif brawf yw nid faint o bwerau sydd ar gael, ond pa mor gyflym y mae adeiladau anniogel yn cael eu trwsio a faint o deuluoedd sy'n gallu symud ymlaen â'u bywydau. Mae pryderon am gyflymder y cynnydd. Yn amlwg, rydym ni wedi eu clywed nhw i gyd heddiw, ac rydych chi'n cydnabod y rheini eich hun. Ond mae angen hyder i bobl fod camau ystyrlon yn cael eu cymryd nawr, ac na fydd cyweirio yn cael ei ohirio. Fel bob amser yng Nghymru, mae angen gweithredu, nid mwy o fiwrocratiaeth.

Weinidog, mae her ehangach yma hefyd. Rydych chi wedi ei gwneud hi'n glir bod cynyddu'r cyflenwad tai yn un o'ch blaenoriaethau, gydag uchelgeisiau ar gyfer 20,000 o gartrefi cymdeithasol newydd erbyn 2030. Nawr, er bod cynyddu cyflenwad yn bwysig, ni ddylai maint byth ddod ar draul ansawdd. Ac efallai bod rhai ohonoch chi wedi clywed Radio Wales y bore yma, lle roedden nhw'n sôn am fân broblemau—cymaint o dai newydd sydd â chymaint o ddiffygion. Wel, ni allwn ni gael tai wedi'u hadeiladu'n wael yn y lle cyntaf, ac mae'n rhaid i wersi o fethiannau adeiladu'r gorffennol gael eu hymgorffori'n llawn mewn datblygiad yn y dyfodol, fel bod pob cartref newydd yn cael ei adeiladu i'r safon uchaf o ddiogelwch, ansawdd a gwytnwch.

Ar yr un pryd, mae Cymru yn wynebu argyfwng tai. Mae angen mwy o gartrefi arnom ni, ond mae angen cartrefi diogel arnom ni. Mae angen datblygiad cyflymach arnom ni, ond mae angen hyder y cyhoedd hefyd bod safonau diogelwch yn cael eu cynnal yn drylwyr. Nid yw'r amcanion hyn yn gwrthdaro. Rhaid iddyn nhw fynd law yn llaw. Rydym ni hefyd yn cydnabod bod hyder y cyhoedd yn dibynnu ar sicrhau bod yr holl risgiau diogelwch sylweddol yn cael eu datrys, p'un a ydyn nhw'n ymwneud â chladin, asbestos, concrit awyredig awtoclafiedig cyfnerth neu bryderon strwythurol ehangach. Mae pobl yn haeddu cartrefi diogel, gwybodaeth glir a gweithredu cyflym pan fydd problemau yn cael eu nodi. Felly, allwch chi, Weinidog, gadarnhau faint o lesddeiliaid y disgwylir iddyn nhw elwa o grant larymau mesurau interim Cymru? Pa asesiad sydd wedi'i wneud ynghylch a fydd y cynllun yn talu'r costau sy'n wynebu preswylwyr yr effeithir arnyn nhw? A pha sicrwydd allwch chi ei roi y bydd gwaith cyweirio a chydymffurfiaeth datblygwyr yn cyflymu ymhell cyn cofrestru arfaethedig yr adeiladau categori 1, fel y soniwyd gennych chi, ym mis Rhagfyr 2027?

Yn y pen draw, ni fydd llwyddiant yn cael ei farnu yn ôl nifer y strategaethau, gweithgorau na chyhoeddiadau; bydd yn cael ei farnu yn ôl a all teuluoedd gysgu'n ddiogel yn eu cartrefi ac a all y cyhoedd fod yn ffyddiog nad yw methiannau'r gorffennol yn cael eu hailadrodd. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Peter, am y cwestiynau yna. Wrth gwrs, dwi’n cytuno'n llwyr efo chi: mae’n rhaid gweld gweithredu. Dyna sydd yn bwysig yn fan hyn, a dyna pam roeddwn i wedi cynnal y cyfarfod efo datblygwyr wythnos diwethaf, er mwyn pwyso’r neges glir yna ein bod ni yn disgwyl gweld cynnydd, a chynnydd ar gyflymder, er mwyn lles y bobl sydd yn byw efo pryder parhaus oherwydd eu bod nhw'n cael eu hatgoffa drwy'r amser am beth ddigwyddodd yn Grenfell. A dwi'n meddwl ei bod hi'n bwysig—. Diolch i chi am sôn am hynny. Mae'n bwysig inni gofio pam rydym ni yn gwneud y gwaith yma. Mae o'n deillio nôl i'r drasiedi yna saith mlynedd yn ôl, bellach. Felly, dyna oedd fy neges i'r datblygwyr. Dwi yn atebol i'r lesddeiliaid. Dwi ddim yn atebol i'r datblygwyr. Y lesddeiliaid sydd ar fy meddwl i, a drwoch chi yn y Senedd dwi'n atebol iddyn nhw hefyd, a dyna pam byddaf i'n dod ag adroddiadau cynnydd i chi yn fan hyn.

Ac mae'r monitro agos yna yn digwydd. Mae fy swyddogion i yn siarad efo'r datblygwyr yn barhaus ac yn ceisio eu helpu nhw i gael gwared ar rai o'r rhwystrau sydd yna. Ond, ar ddiwedd y dydd, mae’n rhaid iddyn nhw gymryd eu cyfrifoldeb o ddifri, a dwi yn gobeithio gweld cynnydd erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn. Dyna oedd yn y contract gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol. Roedden nhw'n disgwyl gweld y gwaith wedi’i ddechrau gan bob datblygwr erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn yma. Rydym ni'n bell o hynny, ond dyna'r disgwyliad dwi'n gosod arnyn nhw, ac, os nad ydy hynny'n digwydd, dwi wedi egluro byddaf i yn gorfod cymryd camau pellach, a byddaf i yn dechrau sôn yn benodol am broblemau yn y Siambr yma, achos dwi'n atebol i chi yn hynny o beth.

O ran y grant, dwi’n falch eich bod chi yn croesawu hwnna. Mae hwn yn medru cael ei weinyddu yn sydyn iawn, i'w gael o allan o’r drws cyn gynted â phosib. Y bore yma, roeddwn i'n siarad efo cynrychiolydd o Swansea Point yn Abertawe oedd yn sôn bod yna ryw 240 o adeiladau mae o'n eu cynrychioli ac y byddai'r datblygiadau yna yn gallu cael budd penodol allan o'r grant. Yn Sand Wharf, mae yna 100 o bobl—100 o unedau—a allai gael budd allan o hwn.

Y meini prawf, bydd y rheini ar gael yn fuan iawn i bobl gael craffu'r rheini, ond yn sicr fydd y grant ddim yn talu am gostau patrolio adeilad ar droed, sef y waking watch, achos mae hwnna wedi bod yn gost sylweddol. Rydyn ni'n symud rŵan at grantiau ar gyfer y larymau, a gobeithio bod y larymau yna yn gallu bod yn rhai parhaol. Mae modd rhoi larymau dros dro i mewn sydd efo'r gallu i gael eu haddasu ar gyfer pan fydd y gwaith wedi cael ei orffen. Felly, gobeithio bod hwnna'n esbonio ychydig bach mwy am hynny.

Mae eich pwynt chi ynglŷn â chartrefi cymdeithasol ac awydd clir y Llywodraeth yma i gynyddu'r cyflenwad o dai cymdeithas yn hollol, hollol briodol. Wrth gwrs, mae safonau diogelwch yn gorfod eu cynnal. Rydym ni'n sôn am gartrefi cymunedol, cartrefi cymdeithasol o ansawdd uchel, carbon isel ac yn saff. Felly, mae hynny'n holl, holl bwysig. Mae o'n rhan o uchelgais y Llywodraeth yma fod pobl yng Nghymru yn gallu cael cartref diogel a fforddiadwy ar gyfer y tymor hir.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much, Peter, for those questions. Of course, I agree entirely with you: we do have to see action. That is what is important here, and that is why I held that meeting with the developers last week, in order to emphasise that very clear message that we do expect to see progress, and progress at pace, for the benefit of the people living with this ongoing concern and anxiety, because they are constantly reminded of what happened at Grenfell. And I do think it is important—. Thank you for mentioning that. It is important that we remember why we are doing this work. It does all go back to that tragedy seven years ago now. So, that was my message to the developers. I am accountable to leaseholders. I am not accountable to the developers. It is the leaseholders who are at the forefront of my thoughts, and through you in the Senedd I am also accountable to them, and that is why I will bring progress reports to you in this place.

And that close monitoring is happening. My officials speak to the developers on an ongoing basis and are trying to help them remove some of the barriers that are in place. But, at the end of the day, they do have to take their responsibilities seriously, and I do hope to see progress by the end of the year. That is what was in the previous Government's contract. They expected to see the work started by all developers by the end of this year. We are a long way from that point, but that is the expectation I am placing on them, and, if that does not happen, as I have explained, I will then have to take further steps, and I will start to talk specifically about problems in this Chamber, because I am accountable to you in that regard. 

In terms of the grant, I am pleased that you have welcomed that. This can be put in place very quickly, and we can get it out of the door as soon as possible. This morning I was speaking to a representative from Swansea Point in Swansea and he mentioned that there are around 240 buildings that he represents, and that those developments could benefit specifically from the grant. In Sand Wharf, there are 100 units that could benefit from this. 

The criteria will be made available very soon so that people can scrutinise those, but certainly the grant won't pay for waking watch costs, because those have been significant. We are now moving to grants for the alarms, and I do very much hope that those alarms can be permanent. You can put in temporary alarms that can be adapted for when the work has been completed and retained. So, hopefully that explains a little more on that.

Your point on social housing and the clear desire of this Government to increase the supply of social housing is entirely appropriate. Of course, safety standards have to be maintained. We are talking about community housing and social housing that is high quality, low carbon and safe. That is crucially important. It's part of the ambition of this Government that people in Wales should be able to access a safe and affordable home for the long term.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Weinidog, am eich datganiad heddiw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Minister, for your statement today.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I appreciate the update and that this Government is taking this work seriously to better support impacted residents. For years now, residents have been afraid in their own homes and have felt that this issue has not been given the attention it deserves. Despite receiving assurances that their property was safe when they moved in, one resident in Cardiff has shared that they face a £3,000 cost for a waking watch, which costs £15,000 a week between 96 flats, and the management company are having to find £150,000 to install fire-detecting equipment. Without the necessary improvements, residents have faced the possibility of being made homeless as their homes aren't safe to live in. I welcome the Minister introducing financial support as an interim measure while remediation works are carried out. How will the Minister make sure tenants don't have to pay out of pocket for remediation work again? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n gwerthfawrogi'r diweddariad a bod y Llywodraeth hon yn cymryd y gwaith hwn o ddifrif i roi cefnogaeth well i drigolion yr effeithir arnyn nhw. Ers blynyddoedd bellach, mae trigolion wedi bod yn ofni yn eu cartrefi eu hunain ac wedi teimlo nad yw'r mater hwn wedi cael y sylw y mae'n ei haeddu. Er gwaethaf derbyn sicrwydd bod eu heiddo yn ddiogel pan symudon nhw, mae un preswylydd yng Nghaerdydd wedi rhannu eu bod yn wynebu cost o £3,000 am wyliadwriaeth effro, sy'n costio £15,000 yr wythnos rhwng 96 o fflatiau. Heb y gwelliannau angenrheidiol, mae trigolion wedi wynebu'r posibilrwydd o gael eu gwneud yn ddigartref gan nad yw eu cartrefi yn ddiogel i fyw ynddyn nhw. Rwy'n croesawu'r Gweinidog yn cyflwyno cymorth ariannol fel mesur dros dro tra bod gwaith cyweirio yn cael ei wneud. Sut bydd y Gweinidog yn sicrhau nad oes rhaid i denantiaid dalu o'u pocedi eu hunain am waith cyweirio eto? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr. Fel chi, dwi wedi cyfarfod llesdeiliaid sydd yn bryderus iawn ac wedi wynebu costau mawr, a chyda dim bai o gwbl arnyn nhw eu hunain, wrth gwrs. Felly, mae'r rheoliadau sydd newydd gael eu hymgynghori arnyn nhw, pan ddaw'r rheini i rym, mi fydd tenantiaid a llesdeiliaid yn gallu hawlio costau yn ôl ar gyfer y gwaith cyweirio. Roedd hwnna'n un o'r pethau penodol gwnaethon ni weithio arno fo wrth i'r Bil fynd trwyddo, fod y tribiwnlysoedd yma yn gallu rhoi llwybr i denantiaid i gael eu costau cyweirio yn ôl, achos dydy o jyst ddim yn deg eu bod nhw'n wynebu, heb unrhyw fath o fai arnyn nhw o gwbl, y costau yma sydd yn achosi cymaint o bryder iddyn nhw.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much. Yes, like you, I have met leaseholders who are very concerned and who have faced enormous costs, and through no fault of their own at all, of course. So, the regulations that have just been consulted on, when those come into force, tenants and leaseholders will be able to claim costs back for the remediation work. That was one of the specific things that we worked on as the Bill went through, that the tribunals would be able to provide a pathway for tenants to be able to claim their remediation costs back, because it just isn't fair that they have to face, through no fault of their own at all, these costs that are causing so much concern and worry for them.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Minister, the building safety programme risks becoming yet another example of taxpayers being asked to foot the bill for failures that they did not cause. England regulates buildings above 18m under its strictest duties. Wales has brought every multi-occupied residential building of any height into the new framework. That's over 51,000 buildings, mostly owned by small private landlords. The Senedd's own committee called the compliance timeline 'unrealistic'. Has the Minister modelled the impact on housing supply and on the capacity of authorities that must enforce it, while residents living in the most dangerous buildings still wait? With housing affordability worsening and house building targets already being missed, can you provide evidence that these measures will not further slow housing delivery? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Weinidog Cabinet, mae'r rhaglen diogelwch adeiladau mewn perygl o ddod yn enghraifft arall o ofyn i drethdalwyr dalu'r bil am fethiannau nad achoswyd ganddyn nhw. Mae Lloegr yn rheoleiddio adeiladau uwchlaw 18m o dan ei dyletswyddau mwyaf llym. Mae Cymru wedi dod â phob adeilad preswyl aml-feddiannaeth o unrhyw uchder i'r fframwaith newydd. Mae hynny dros 51,000 o adeiladau, y mae'r rhan fwyaf ohonyn nhw yn eiddo i landlordiaid preifat bach. Galwodd pwyllgor y Senedd ei hun yr amserlen gydymffurfio yn 'afrealistig'. A yw'r Gweinidog wedi modelu'r effaith ar gyflenwad tai ac ar gapasiti awdurdodau y mae'n rhaid iddyn nhw ei gorfodi, tra bod trigolion sy'n byw yn yr adeiladau mwyaf peryglus yn dal i aros? Gyda fforddiadwyedd tai yn gwaethygu a thargedau adeiladu tai eisoes yn cael eu methu, allwch chi ddarparu tystiolaeth na fydd y mesurau hyn yn arafu'r ddarpariaeth dai ymhellach? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am y cwestiwn. I fod yn glir, dydyn ni ddim yn gofyn i drethdalwyr dalu am y gwaith cyweirio; rydyn ni'n gofyn i'r datblygwyr symud ymlaen efo'r gwaith cyweirio.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for your question. Just to be clear, we are not asking taxpayers to pay for remediation work; we are asking the developers to proceed with that remediation work.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We're not asking taxpayers to pay; we're asking the developers to speed up the remediation work and, in that way, make the homes safe for the leaseholders who are living in anxiety at the moment, and facing costs as well that, following the introduction of the new regulations, they will be able to go to a tribunal to claim.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Dydyn ni ddim yn gofyn i drethdalwyr dalu; rydym ni'n gofyn i'r datblygwyr gyflymu'r gwaith cyweirio ac, yn y modd hwnnw, gwneud y cartrefi yn ddiogel i'r lesddeiliaid sy'n byw mewn pryder ar hyn o bryd, ac yn wynebu costau hefyd y byddan nhw, ar ôl cyflwyno'r rheoliadau newydd, yn gallu mynd i dribiwnlys i'w hawlio.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: O ran y pwynt bod cysylltiad rhwng y gwaith yma a'r gwaith cyflenwi tai cymdeithasol, dwi ddim rili yn gweld bod yna gysylltiad. Mae'n rhaid i'r gwaith yma ddigwydd. Mae'n rhaid i'r adeiladau yma gael eu gwneud yn saff. Mae'r Ddeddf yn dweud hynny. Mae'r gwaith o gynyddu’r cyflenwad o dai cymdeithasol yn rhywbeth sydd yn mynd i ddigwydd yn raddol dros gyfnod. Mae yna pipeline da o brosiectau o fewn y system yna. Felly, dwi ddim wir yn gweld cysylltiad rhwng y ddau beth. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: In terms of your point that there's a link between this work and the supply of social housing, I don't really see that there is a link there. This work must happen. These buildings must be made safe. The legislation states so. The work to increase the supply of social housing is something that will happen gradually over a period of time. There is a good pipeline of projects in place in that system. So, I don't really see a link between the two things. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ac yn olaf, Weinidog, Mike Hedges.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: And finally, Minister, Mike Hedges.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. I welcome the update on the building safety programme and the steps the Government is taking to protect leaseholders and ensure that the homes covered by the programme are safe, and those living in them are treated with the fairness and dignity they deserve. This has been a long time coming. My constituents have waited a very long time for this to be resolved. It's created hardship and worry for my constituents. The commitment to provide financial support to leaseholders facing the cost of interim alarm systems required to support the simultaneous evacuation policy is a positive step, but it's an acknowledgement that, despite all the agreements, we have not reached the stage where work is going to be done everywhere in the near future. My constituents living in fear of being another Grenfell want the obligations under the contract to be met, and the Welsh Government needs to get legally enforceable agreements with guaranteed completion dates so that my constituents can sleep safely at night.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Rwy'n croesawu'r diweddariad ar y rhaglen diogelwch adeiladau a'r camau y mae'r Llywodraeth yn eu cymryd i amddiffyn lesddeiliaid a sicrhau bod y cartrefi sy'n dod o dan y rhaglen yn ddiogel, a bod y rhai sy'n byw ynddyn nhw yn cael eu trin â'r tegwch a'r urddas maen nhw'n ei haeddu. Mae'n hwyr glas gwneud hyn. Mae fy etholwyr wedi aros amser hir iawn i hyn gael ei ddatrys. Mae wedi creu caledi a phryder i'm hetholwyr. Mae'r ymrwymiad i ddarparu cefnogaeth ariannol i lesddeiliaid sy'n wynebu cost systemau larwm dros dro sydd eu hangen i gefnogi'r polisi gwagio cydamserol yn gam cadarnhaol, ond mae'n gydnabyddiaeth, er gwaethaf yr holl gytundebau, nad ydym ni wedi cyrraedd y cam lle bydd gwaith yn cael ei wneud ym mhobman yn y dyfodol agos. Mae fy etholwyr sy'n byw mewn ofn o fod yn Grenfell arall eisiau i'r rhwymedigaethau o dan y contract gael eu cyflawni, ac mae angen i Lywodraeth Cymru gael cytundebau y gellir eu gorfodi'n gyfreithiol gyda dyddiadau cwblhau gwarantedig fel y gall fy etholwyr gysgu'n ddiogel yn y nos.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Mike. Rydych chi hefyd yn pwysleisio'r caledi y mae rhai o'ch etholwyr chi wedi bod ac yn wynebu oherwydd y sefyllfa yma, a'r angen i'w trin nhw efo tegwch a pharch ac urddas. Yn sicr, dwi yn gwneud hynny. Fe wnes i gyfarfod etholwr o Abertawe heddiw a oedd yn sôn am y pryder sydd ganddyn nhw oherwydd yr arafwch efo datblygiad Swansea Point yn benodol.

Dwi'n deall eich pwynt chi o ran rhoi grantiau tuag at larymau interim, a bod hynny efallai yn arwydd bod pethau mynd i arafu. Ond, beth dwi'n gwybod all ddigwydd ydy bod y larymau yma yn medru cael eu gosod fel mesur dros dro, ond mae yna ffordd o'u haddasu nhw fel eu bod nhw yna yn barhaol. Felly, mae hwnna yn arwydd bod pethau'n gallu symud ymlaen, oherwydd fe fydd y larymau yna yn gallu bod yna ar ôl i'r gwaith gael ei gwblhau.

Jest i'ch atgoffa chi, wrth i ni gloi, Ddirprwy Lywydd, gofyniad y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf yn y cytundeb efo'r datblygwyr oedd bod gwaith i ddechrau ym mhob adeilad erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn yma. Dyna'r disgwyliad. Efallai nad ydy'r disgwyliad yna wedi cael ei wneud y ddigon clir i ddatblygwyr—dwi'n credu efallai ei fod o—gan y cyn-Lywodraeth, ond mae'r Llywodraeth yma yn benderfynol bod y datblygwyr yn cymryd eu gwaith yn gwbl, gwbl o ddifrif.

Dwi'n edrych ymlaen at ddod yn ôl yma i'r Senedd, nid i sôn am y problemau, ond i sôn am y stori dda sydd wedi digwydd yng Nghymru efo'r rhaglen diogelwch adeiladau. Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much, Mike. You are also emphasising the hardship that some of your constituents have faced and are facing because of this situation, and the need to treat them with dignity, respect and fairness. Certainly, I am doing that. I met with a constituent from Swansea today who spoke about the concern that they have because of the slow progress with the development at Swansea Point in particular.

I understand your point in terms of providing grants for the interim alarms, and that that perhaps is a sign that things are going to slow down. However, what I know can happen is that these alarms can be installed as a temporary measure, but there is a way of adapting them so that they can remain there permanently. So, that is a sign that things can move forward, because those alarms can remain there after the work is completed.

Just to remind you, in closing, Dirprwy Lywydd, the requirement of the previous Government in the agreement with developers was that work was to be started in every building by the end of this year. That was the expectation. Perhaps that expectation hasn't been made clear enough to developers—I think it probably was—by the previous Government, but this Government is determined that the developers will take their work completely and entirely seriously.

I look forward to returning here to the Senedd, not to talk to you about the problems, but to tell a positive story about what's happened in Wales with the building safety programme. Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Weinidog Cabinet. Daw hynny â thrafodion heddiw i ben. Fe wnaf eich gweld chi yfory.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much, Cabinet Minister. That brings today's proceedings to a close. See you tomorrow.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 7. Datganiad gan y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Lywodraeth Leol, Tai a Chynllunio: Diweddariad ar y Rhaglen Diogelwch Adeiladau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 7. Statement by the Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning: Building Safety Programme Update
